### 2026-07-16 (Claude Code, interactive) — pack-dist smoke false-fail root-caused DEEPER than round 6: swallowed streamed-body timeout → hard "200, needle=false"; fixed in `checkHtmlContains`

The "pack dist 5048: 200, Sales History=false" hard-fail (fired 07-16 during the live 60s-statement-timeout contention window — `analytics-smoke` cancelled 18:43–21:43Z, `rpc_sales_summary_topshot_30d` 16–25s) is the SAME class round 6 mitigated by retargeting 7800→5048, but the actual bug is in the smoke harness, not the probe target. Every RPC the pack page's streamed bottom block runs is <200ms in isolation (get_pack_sales_history 177ms, get_pack_contents 109ms, exhausted-count 0.16ms, top-pulls pool sub-second) — so dist 5048 is not a module regression. Root cause: the pack "Sales History" (and edition "Activity") sections flush from a `<Suspense>` boundary AFTER the 200 shell headers; `fetch()` resolves on headers, so the retry/inconclusive guard was already past when the streamed-body `res.text()` read ran under the SAME AbortSignal budget. Under contention the flush blew the budget, `res.text()` rejected mid-stream, and the old `.catch(() => "")` swallowed the abort to `""` → `needle`-absent read out as a HARD "HTTP 200, <needle>=false" — bypassing the whole soft-inconclusive machinery built for exactly this.

- **SHIPPED (code) — `checkHtmlContains` now reads the streamed body INSIDE the retry/inconclusive handling** (`app/api/smoke-test/route.ts`). A timeout in the fetch OR the streamed-body read is now transient (retry once → SOFT inconclusive, never Sentry); a body that fully reads but genuinely lacks the needle still HARD-fails as a real module regression. Fixes both HTTP-contains probes (pack Sales History + edition Activity). Complementary to the round-6 retarget (which reduced frequency but not the swallow). **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`. **Target metric:** the hourly "pack dist … Sales History=false" hard page stops firing during contention windows (reclassifies to soft inconclusive); a real missing-module regression still pages.

### 2026-07-16 (Claude Code, interactive) — smoke inline soft-probes get retry-once parity (`smokeFetchRetry`); finishes the file's transient-retry pattern + 4 tests

After confirming (via `smoke_test_results`, 24h) that the pack-dist "Sales History=false" was the last recurring HARD false-fail (all other failing probes — wallet-search 51/24h, sniper-feed 42, market 21, fmv-rpc 32, profile/badges — are `soft`-by-design external-dependency noise that never pages), closed the one remaining consistency gap: the inline `soft` probes did a bare single fetch with NO retry, while the helper probes (`checkUrl`/`checkPublicPage`/`checkHtmlContains`) all retry once on the timeout/transient class. A single transient blip therefore logged a soft-fail indistinguishable in the smoke summary from a real outage, and doubled the soft-fail noise. Added `smokeFetchRetry` (fetch + one retry on the `/abort|timeout/i` class; a non-transient throw still surfaces on attempt 1; a legit non-200 response passes straight through — only *thrown* transients retry) and wired the four inline soft probes onto it (sniper-feed ×2, og/collection, wallet-search POST [idempotent search], profile). 4 new unit tests in `__tests__/api-smoke-test-html-contains.test.ts` (10 total in file). Behavior on genuine double-failure unchanged (still a soft-fail); only single-blip false soft-fails are removed. Full suite green, `tsc` 0 errors repo-wide. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`. **Target metric:** wallet-search/sniper-feed soft-fail rows in `smoke_test_results` drop materially (transient blips no longer logged), so a persistent 2-in-a-row failure becomes a meaningful signal.

### 2026-07-16 (Claude Code, interactive) — analytics-smoke stops hard-failing on DB saturation (inconclusive-classify); new shared `isSaturationError` + tests

Verified the DB/IOPS domain was quiet ~2.5h (last migration 21:15Z, last Cowork/Trevor IOPS commit 21:17Z) → the `analytics-smoke` flap was NOT being actively worked, so picked it up. Root: when `analytics_smoke_run()` hits a statement-timeout under the daytime contention windows, the route logged `ok=false` (~14/48 ticks/24h, all `canceling statement due to statement timeout`) — a false HARD pipeline failure that pollutes health and would MASK a real smoke break (identical shape). A saturation timeout is the smoke QUERY being slow, not a regression. Fix: extracted the sentinel's `isSaturationError` classifier to a shared `lib/pipeline/saturation.ts` and used it in `app/api/admin/analytics-smoke/route.ts` — a saturation-class RPC error now logs `ok=true` + `{inconclusive, warn: db_saturated}` (mirrors the sentinel's INCONCLUSIVE-warn handling); a NON-saturation RPC error still logs `ok=false`. ### 2026-07-17 (Claude Code, interactive) — SHIPPED: bulk-classify SSE writer double-close fix (real unhandled-rejection bug the wave-8 test flagged + deferred)

Owned the double-close route bug the wave-8 coverage sweep documented and explicitly left for a follow-up owner (its test deliberately skipped the two crashing paths). **SHIPPED `24874f1b` (code + test):** `app/api/bulk-classify/route.ts` — the background SSE streamer's two early-return paths (`requestedOffset >= total`, and the mid-run wall-clock TIMEOUT) each called `await writer.close()` then `return`, but `return` inside the `try` still runs the `finally`, which closed the writer AGAIN → `ERR_INVALID_STATE` unhandled promise rejection from the fire-and-forget IIFE. These are the classifier's two most common terminal paths (a caught-up wallet; any backlog exceeding one 55s call), so the rejection fired routinely in prod. Fix: made the `finally` the single close point (dropped the two explicit closes) + guarded the finally close and the error-path `send` with `.catch(()=>{})` so a client-aborted SSE (already-errored writer) also can't throw. Added 2 regression tests (offset>=total → done/processed:0; timeout branch via a `Date.now` spy → timeout/nextOffset:0) — a clean stream read is the assertion the writer closes once; **7/7 green, tsc clean** (both paths previously crashed the test process with exit 1). **Revert:** `git revert 24874f1b`.

### 2026-07-17 (Cowork, interactive, round 5) — SELF-CORRECTION: rwfd v2 was a regression (read the fmv_current VIEW = full-history scan); v3 reads fmv_snapshots directly (818k buffers -> 130)

Caught my own regression by EXPLAIN-ing what I'd shipped this morning instead of trusting a warm-cache timing (the exact "measure the loop, don't trust a warm sample" lesson).

- **The regression:** round-2 rwfd v2 sourced the changed-set + values from the **`fmv_current` VIEW**, which I'd assumed was a cheap maintained table. It is a **VIEW** = `DISTINCT ON (edition_id) ... FROM fmv_snapshots ORDER BY edition_id, computed_at DESC` — a FULL scan of the 876k-row fmv_snapshots_2026 partition (**818,583 buffers / 1.09s**), and v2 read it TWICE per call. That was WORSE than the v1 it replaced (315 MB/call). My v2 "1s" number was warm-cache-lucky.
- **SHIPPED — rwfd v3** (migration `audit_20260717_rwfd_delta_v3_direct_snapshots`): reads the delta straight from `fmv_snapshots` with the `computed_at > watermark` predicate on `idx_fmv_snapshots_2026_computed_at_desc` — a snapshot newer than the watermark IS by definition that edition's latest, so `DISTINCT ON (edition_id) ... WHERE computed_at > cutoff` returns exactly the changed editions with current FMV. **EXPLAIN: 130 buffers / 3ms** (index range scan — structurally cheap, NOT cache-dependent this time; ~6,000× fewer reads than v2). Measured 1.8s backlog / 0.015s steady-state; invariants []. Semantics identical to v1/v2; watermark unchanged. **Revert:** restore the v2 (fmv_current) def from migration history.
- **Lesson reinforced (memory updated):** before claiming a rewrite is cheaper, EXPLAIN(BUFFERS) the actual inner read — a warm-cache wall-clock sample hid a 6,000× regression. And: check `relkind` before assuming a name is a table (fmv_current is a view; my earlier "fmv_current has no PK, add one" flag was moot).

### 2026-07-17 (Cowork, interactive) — test-only: fix worker-pack-events-ingest local hang (leaked AbortSignal.timeout timers)

__tests__/worker-pack-events-ingest.test.ts hung its 3 fetch-making tests on Windows-local Node (CI Linux green — flagged by CC during the Candy work, proven independent). Root cause: the worker guards every Flow REST fetch with AbortSignal.timeout(20_000); the mocked fetch resolves instantly but the 20s timer stays scheduled (~12/test), and on Node builds where those timers are ref'd they hold the vitest worker open past its timeout. Fix is TEST-ONLY — neutralize AbortSignal.timeout to a no-timer, never-aborting signal in beforeEach + restore in afterEach; the pack-events worker (off-limits) is UNTOUCHED. **Verify:** local `npm test __tests__/worker-pack-events-ingest.test.ts` (CI can't reproduce a hang it never had). **Revert:** `git revert` this commit.

### 2026-07-17 (Claude Code, interactive) — PERF/read-diet lever #1 SHIPPED (DB-only): throttled the #1 IOPS backfill 6× (verified live)

Measured attack on the first-paint latency (P2). `pg_stat_statements` (by `shared_blks_read`) showed the top ~15 IO consumers are ALL background cron/backfills — the public first-paint queries (collection-stats/market/pack-reality) aren't even in the top 15, confirming the finding's thesis: **cheap user queries running slow under IOPS saturation from heavy background jobs**, not slow queries themselves. So the lever is the read-diet, not query optimization.

- **SHIPPED (DB-only, prod-state) — throttled `backfill_topshot_historical_pack_ev` (pg_cron jobid 71, owner `cron_heavy`).** The #1 total-exec-time consumer (2.77h total / 222 calls / 1.64M block reads). It re-scanned ALL TS `pack_distributions` with expensive per-dist correlated subqueries (`count(DISTINCT drop_weight)`, `NOT EXISTS pack_ev_history`, `sec_ask`) **every 10 min** to find ≤10 dists lacking a fresh (<12h) EV row — but ~146 of the ~157 candidates can never insert (pool_incomplete `ok:false` / no live ask post the 07-16 guard), so it **spun** on them, burning ~7.4K blocks/scan × 6/hr during the contention windows. Freshness invariant is 12h → 10-min cadence was ~6× overkill. Changed to **hourly** (`13 * * * *`) + `p_limit` 10→15 so 12 runs × 15 = 180/12h still refreshes the full 157-dist backlog inside 12h. **~6× fewer candidate scans; no logic/output change.** Verified live: jobid 71 `13 * * * *`, `...(15)`, owner still `cron_heavy`, active. (`alter_job` was blocked — postgres has EXECUTE but not ownership; cron_heavy owns it but lacks EXECUTE — so updated in place via `cron.schedule` upsert-by-name AS cron_heavy.) **REVERT:** `SET ROLE cron_heavy; SELECT cron.schedule('rpc-backfill-historical-pack-ev','3,13,23,33,43,53 * * * *','SELECT public.backfill_topshot_historical_pack_ev(10)'); RESET ROLE;`
- **SHIPPED 3 more measured throttles (DB-only, all owner `cron_heavy`, all proven-spinning by direct measurement, cadence-only/reversible):**
  - **`backfill_null_serial_sales_from_moments` (jobid 76): every-15-min → hourly (`5 * * * *`, ~4× cut).** Scans 1,505 null-serial sales (45d window) every run to find only **2 resolvable now** — ~99.9% spinning on unresolvable rows; historical-sale serials tolerate hourly latency (new sales resolve as their moments hydrate). **REVERT:** `SET ROLE cron_heavy; SELECT cron.schedule('rpc-recover-null-serial-sales','5,20,35,50 * * * *','SELECT public.backfill_null_serial_sales_from_moments()'); RESET ROLE;`
  - **`rollup_allday_rip_pull_value` (jobid 72): every-30-min → hourly (`14 * * * *`, ~2× cut).** Full 173K-row `allday_pack_pull` GROUP BY every run but only **9 changed writes/6h** (22 AllDay rips/24h — AllDay ended primary packs). **REVERT:** `... cron.schedule('rpc-allday-rollup-rip-value','14,44 * * * *','SELECT public.rollup_allday_rip_pull_value()'); ...`
  - **`sync_allday_pack_dist_totals` (jobid 75): every-30-min → hourly (`24 * * * *`, ~2× cut).** Full `v_allday_pack_info` scan every run but **0 of 3,052 AllDay dists updated in 24h** (`total_minted` frozen post-primary-end) — pure spinning. **REVERT:** `... cron.schedule('rpc-sync-allday-pack-dist-totals','12,42 * * * *','SELECT public.sync_allday_pack_dist_totals()'); ...`
- **Intentionally LEFT ALONE (throttling = real user-facing-freshness tradeoff, not free):** `refresh_mv_pack_ev_latest` (10-min, keeps core pack-EV boards fresh), `roll_pack_ask_hourly_low` (15-min, each run captures the intra-hour ask MINIMUM via `LEAST` → extra runs add real 24h/7d low-ask accuracy), `refresh_allday_badge_low_ask` (30-min, real badge-ask work), `dedup_allday_cross_source_sales` (already hourly). These do incremental real work at their cadence — not throttled blind.
- **Seed-wallet-refresh read-diet (handoff `03`-I / cost-runbook #3): FINDING — already comprehensively implemented in code (2026-06-14 `VERCEL-FLUID-RIGHTSIZE`):** dispatch pacing (`DISPATCH_BATCH_SIZE=6`, `TARGET_SPREAD_MS=9min`, ~18× lower peak child-arrival), a low-priority interval gate (skip priority-≥4 discovered-cohort wallets walked <24h ago, env-tunable `SEED_REFRESH_LOWPRI_INTERVAL_HOURS`), AND a cohort-split mechanism (`?cohort=K&of=N`). The remaining levers there — widening the env interval or activating staggered cohort cron entries — are **operator/config actions** (Vercel env / cron-job.org), NOT new code. Deliberately did not invent a marginal staleness-risking code change.
- **NET:** 4 measured throttles on the top IOPS-spinning offenders (6× + 4× + 2× + 2×), each proven-spinning and reversible → cuts background IOPS during the contention windows that were the root cause of the 8–16s public first-paint. Validate the aggregate IOPS/latency impact over the next cycle; further cuts need the operator config levers or user-facing-freshness tradeoffs.

### 2026-07-18 (Claude Code, interactive) — post-ship page fixes: logged-in Market fetch un-gated (P1) + AllDay thumb size (P2) + edition Activity contention-resilience (P3)

- **P1 (SEV-HIGH) — logged-in `/market` no longer strands on the loading skeleton.** The fetch effect hard-gated on `supabaseCollectionId`, which — unlike `collectionId` — has **no fallback** in `buildContext` (`collection?.supabaseCollectionId ?? null`). During the logged-in first-commit window (extra auth/profile/wallet fetches race `useParams()` resolution) it was momentarily null, so the page committed its filter UI but never issued `/api/market` (no error, logged-in only, intermittent — anon resolves params synchronously and never hits the window). Fix: derive `resolvedCollectionUuid = supabaseCollectionId ?? getCollectionUuid(collectionId)` (collectionId is always a valid published slug → always a non-null UUID) and gate/fetch on that. **Corrects the handoff's root-cause premise** — the stuck "Loading market…" is the outer Suspense fallback and the fetch was gated, not an async context race in the hook (the hook is a pure synchronous `useMemo`).

- **P3 — edition Activity section survives DB contention.** `EditionBottomSections` fetched via one `Promise.all` whose members only handled the supabase-js `{ error }` shape; a statement/gateway timeout that **rejects** the promise bypassed `if (error)`, rejected the whole `Promise.all`, and dropped the entire bottom section incl. the `<Section title="Activity">` heading → recurring `/nfl-all-day/edition/446` smoke false-fail during morning heavy-cron windows. Fix: per-fetch `.catch(() => <empty fallback>)` so each leg degrades to its titled empty-state and the section always renders.

### 2026-07-18 (Cowork, interactive) — Phase 3: `v_moments_needing_hydration` #3-disk-reader FIXED (237 MB → 1.5 MB/call, 4,326 ms → 165 ms) — and the standing "trigger-queue" premise DISPROVEN

The carried Phase 3 item (`V-MOMENTS-NEEDING-HYDRATION`, deferred since 07-17 as "structural fix only — trigger-maintained incremental queue"). Measured it properly first; the premise was wrong and the real fix was far smaller and safer.

- **PREMISE DISPROVEN — it was never a selectivity problem.** The standing note said "its seq-scan predicate matches ~89.6% of `moment_acquisitions`, so no index helps," implying only a trigger-maintained queue could work. The predicate figure is right (636,495 of 711,625 rows are `pack_pull`+`verified`) but it was not the cost driver. Proof: `SELECT * FROM v_moments_needing_hydration LIMIT 300` already ran in **431 ms / 12 MB** — Postgres pipelines the CTE and stops pulling once the limit is met. So the limited read was never the hog.
- **ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE — an optimizer fence, found in `pg_stat_statements`.** The real consumer is the `topshot-moments-hydrator` worker via PostgREST: `... WHERE collection_id=$1 **ORDER BY acquired_date DESC** LIMIT 300 OFFSET $3` — **300 calls, 70 GB total, 237 MB + 4,326 ms each**. The view body wrapped its candidates in `WITH cand AS MATERIALIZED (...)`. Under an outer `ORDER BY`, that fence forces all ~636k candidates to materialize and hash-anti-join a **full seq scan of `moments` (540k rows)** before the top-N sort, so the `LIMIT` can never short-circuit. The ordering, not the predicate, was the problem.
- **SHIPPED (index, concurrent) — `idx_ma_hydration_queue_desc`** on `moment_acquisitions (collection_id, acquired_date DESC) INCLUDE (nft_id, wallet, source_pack_rip_id) WHERE acquisition_method='pack_pull' AND acquisition_confidence='verified'`. 58 MB, built `CONCURRENTLY` via standalone `execute_sql` (never inside `apply_migration` — that wraps in a txn). `INCLUDE` carries every column the anti-join and output need, so the candidate side is a true Index Only Scan. Sized against a measurement, not a guess: a `DESC` walk needs only **14,203 of 636,495 candidates (2.2%)** to collect 300 unhydrated, because the backlog reaches right up to the newest rows (newest unhydrated was 2 min old; oldest 2026-04-10). **REVERT:** `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY public.idx_ma_hydration_queue_desc;`
- **SHIPPED (view) — `audit_20260718_moments_needing_hydration_unfence_cte`.** Dropped the `AS MATERIALIZED` fence, rewriting the body as a direct `NOT EXISTS`. Removing a fence only ADDS plan choices — the planner still picks the hash anti-join for unlimited/count-shaped calls — so this cannot regress the other call shapes. **REVERT:** restore the prior `AS MATERIALIZED` body from migration history.
- **MEASURED, worker query shape, before → after:** execution **4,326 ms → 165 ms (~26×)**; disk blocks read **~29,000 → 186 (~1.5 MB, ~160×)**; candidate rows walked **636,571 → 14,102**; plan Hash Anti Join + full `moments` seq scan → **Nested Loop Anti Join with early stop** off the new index. At the observed ~300 calls/window that is ~70 GB → ~0.5 GB.
- **POST-FLIGHT ALL GREEN:** `view_rows_now` 172,017 == independent recompute 172,017 (parity exact; +5 vs pre-change = normal ingest drift); columns/order/types unchanged; grants preserved (**postgres + service_role only, anon NOT granted**); `reloptions` unchanged (null); `check_public_security_invariants()` []; `check_secdef_anon_execute_violations()` []; `tables_without_rls` 0; no invalid indexes DB-wide.
- **NOT DONE deliberately — no trigger, no queue table.** The trigger-maintained queue would have added write-path amplification to TWO active ingest tables (`moment_acquisitions` + `moments`) and new correctness surface, to solve a problem that turned out to be a one-line fence plus an index. **Recommend removing "build a trigger-maintained hydration queue" from the standing queue.**
- **RESIDUAL (optional, low):** the remaining 165 ms is dominated by `Heap Fetches: 14,012` on the `moments` index-only probe — stale visibility map on an actively-written table. A `VACUUM (ANALYZE) public.moments` would convert most of those to true index-only reads, but it is I/O on an IOPS-constrained instance; left for a deliberate quiet-window call, not bundled here.

### 2026-07-18 (Cowork, interactive) — SELF-INFLICTED REGRESSION CAUGHT BY THE MONITOR + FIXED SAME SESSION: the 12h gate silently killed the GHA wallet-backfill backstop

The 21:06Z daytime monitor inbox flagged my own `4c631412` as HIGH within ~30 min of the deploy. It was right. Fixed in the same session.

- **THE BUG (mine).** The 12h gate skips any wave where `utcHour % 12 >= 2`. The GHA backstop `.github/workflows/wallet-backfill-backstop.yml` fires `38 2,8,14,20 * * *` and calls **the same route** — and `2%12=2`, `8%12=8`, `14%12=2`, `20%12=8`, so **every backstop invocation began silently no-op'ing.** That backstop is the only redundancy for cron-job.org trigger dropout — the platform's documented recurring failure class, with an instance (`pinnacle-sync`, 35h silent) live at that very moment. Nothing broke; the safety net did.
- **ROOT CAUSE OF THE MISS (process, worth keeping).** I reasoned about the gate against the 4 cron-job.org cohort entries and never grepped for **other callers of the route**. One `grep -rn "seed-wallet-refresh" --include=*.yml` would have surfaced it before the push. **Rule: before gating/short-circuiting any route, enumerate every caller — cron-job.org, GHA workflows, vercel.json, pg_cron, in-repo fetches — not just the one you had in mind.**
- **SHIPPED — `?force=1` bypass.** The route now honours `force=1|true` alongside the `SEED_WALLET_REFRESH_EVERY_WAVE` env hatch, and the backstop workflow URL gains `&force=1` with a LOAD-BEARING comment so a future reader can't drop it. Safe to expose as a query param: the route is already Bearer-auth-gated above the check.
- **VERIFIED the bypass is nearly free (the monitor asserted this; its stated reasoning was wrong, the conclusion held).** The monitor argued `skip_cached` makes a redundant backstop fire a no-op — but `skip_cached` is **not** a per-wallet skip; it is passed *down* to `wallet-backfill-multicollection` meaning "walk only the on-chain→cache diff", so the child fan-out still fires. The only true per-wallet skip is `LOW_PRIORITY_INTERVAL_HOURS` (24h) and it applies to low-priority rows only. Checked empirically instead: over 3 days the backstop hours produced **0 runs at 02/08/20 and 14 runs at 14 (~5/day)** vs ~1,213/day for the gated waves — the backstop only does real work when a primary cohort actually failed. **Bypass cost ≈ 5 runs/day. The cost lever is intact.**
- **REVERT:** `git revert <fix sha>` restores the un-bypassed gate (and re-breaks the backstop — prefer reverting `4c631412` too if backing the whole lever out).
- **Monitor items 2–4 acknowledged, not actioned (correctly):** (2) wallet-backfill stall thresholds vs the new cadence is explicitly **measure-first after a full post-gate day (07-19)** — pre-raising blind is what the monitor warned against, and its own caveat (a second non-wave driver exists) is now confirmed above; (3) pool-exhaustion Sentry `JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-1Z` is the designated post-ship watch target for this gate, no action to ship; (4) `pinnacle-sync` catalog half unbackstopped → operator, watch the 07-19 10:07Z tick.

### 2026-07-18 (Cowork, interactive) — ROOT-CAUSED "I should have way more than 7 moments sold": `sales` counterparty coverage is 21% (TS), not a Sold-view bug

Trevor flagged the new Moments→Sold tab as under-reporting. It is — and the cause is a platform-wide data gap, not the view.

- **MEASURED — counterparty (buyer AND seller) coverage in `public.sales`:** nba_top_shot **618,468 / 2,962,790 = 20.9%**; nfl_all_day 63,989 / 527,448 = 12.1%; laliga_golazos 177 / 78,250 = 0.2%; ufc_strike **2 / 813,435 = 0.0%**. By TS year: **2020 0%, 2021 0%**, 2022 14%, 2023 9%, 2024 19%, 2025 **5%**, 2026 57%.
- **ROOT CAUSE — buyer and seller coverage move together (618,468 vs 618,301), because they are populated by the SAME path.** Only the on-chain indexers write counterparties. The bulk of the historical record came from the Dapper **studio-platform GQL deep-history backfills** (`*_studio_history_v1`, shipped 2026-06-24/25) which carry price + edition + serial but **no wallet addresses**. So any wallet-scoped "sold" view can only ever see the on-chain-ingested minority. Trevor's 7 rows are exactly the ones that survived that filter (2024-03-01 → 2026-05-30).
- **INFERENCE LANES TESTED AND REJECTED (do not re-attempt without new data):** (1) *buyer-side inversion* — "the next sale after his buy is his sale": only 949 of his ~14.9k moments were marketplace buys at all (the rest are pack pulls), yielding 16 candidates of which 10 CONFLICT with an already-recorded different seller. (2) *acquisition-side inversion* over `moment_acquisitions` (which does include pulls): 522 candidates, but **`candidate_and_no_longer_held` = 0** — every one is still in his wmc, so those later sales are not his. The sale↔ownership chain is too lossy to reconstruct seller by inference. (3) Note `moment_acquisitions` is itself incomplete: he holds 14,945 wmc rows vs 14,553 acquisition rows, and **wmc is a CURRENT snapshot** — rows are deleted when a moment leaves — so RPC retains **no durable record of past holdings**. That is the deeper structural gap.
- **SHIPPED (code) — coverage disclosure on the Sold tab.** The view now states plainly that it shows only on-chain-recorded sales and is a **lower bound**, not a complete sale history. A Sold list that looks complete but isn't is worse than no list; this is marked do-not-drop in the source.
- **QUEUED (NEW, MEDIUM–LARGE, owner/CC — NOT blind-shippable) — SALES-COUNTERPARTY-BACKFILL.** Restoring real "sold" history needs counterparties recovered onto historical `sales`. Viable lanes, in order of ratio: (a) **per-account Flow event walk** — walk the wallet's own `MomentNFT.Withdraw`/`Deposit` events and join to the sale at that tx/block; scoped per-wallet so it is tractable on demand rather than 2.3M rows at once; (b) **tx re-decode via Flow REST on `sales.transaction_hash`** — exact precedent exists and worked at **100% recovery** (the 2026-07-07 job that recovered `subeditionId` for 2,379 offers by decoding each offer's own OfferAvailable tx), but wholesale scope here is ~2.3M TS rows so it must be prioritized (e.g. seeded//verified wallets first). Both touch sales ingest = the documented off-limits class; deliberate owner session.

### 2026-07-18 (Cowork, interactive) — SALES-COUNTERPARTY-BACKFILL: DB layer SHIPPED + proven end-to-end (20/20 recovered); runner is the one remaining piece

Trevor approved building the recovery. The engine is live and verified; only the scheduled runner is outstanding.

- **FEASIBILITY PROVEN FIRST.** Flow REST is reachable from the Cowork sandbox (same lane as the 2026-07-07 offer-subedition job). A tx decode yields ground truth: `TopShot.Withdraw.from` = seller, `TopShot.Deposit.to` = buyer, `TopShotMarketV3.MomentPurchased.seller` corroborates. **Random sample of 12 NULL-seller rows → 11 recovered BOTH sides** (1 transient timeout, retryable). Scope: **2,344,322** TS sales have a NULL seller, **2,303,527** of them carry a valid 64-hex tx hash. Dominated by `ts_history_backfill_v1` (2,128,284).
- **CORRECTED MY OWN EARLIER ADVICE — a Flow *event* walk is NOT tractable.** Flow's REST events API is queried by type + block range, not by account, so "walk this wallet's Withdraw events" means scanning tens of millions of blocks. The tx-decode lane (we already store `sales.transaction_hash`) is the correct one. I had proposed the event walk as the easy option; that was wrong.
- **INFERENCE LANES KILLED WITH ON-CHAIN EVIDENCE (do not retry).** Decoded 12 of the "first sale after his acquisition" candidates: **0 seller, 10 buyer, 2 neither** — the set is his PURCHASES, which is exactly why all 522 were still in his wmc. Inference from the sale/ownership chain cannot identify a wallet's sales.
- **SHIPPED (DB) — `audit_20260718_sales_counterparty_backfill_scaffold_v2`** (+ `_revoke_anon_execute`, `_monotonic_cursor`): state table `sales_counterparty_backfill_state`, audit table `sales_counterparty_recovered`, `claim_sales_counterparty_batch(int)` (newest-first, tx-hash-valid, cursor-bounded) and `apply_sales_counterparty(jsonb)`.
- **SAFETY PROPERTIES, each verified live, not assumed:** **fill-only** — `COALESCE` + `IS NULL` guard means it can never overwrite an indexer value (proved by replaying a row with `0xDEADBEEF`: `applied:0`, real seller untouched); **idempotent** — re-running a batch is a no-op; **no INSERT/DELETE on `sales`**, so the destructive-op circuit-breaker is never engaged; **fully attributable/revertible** via the audit table; **monotonic cursor** — walks newest→oldest only.
- **TWO BUGS I INTRODUCED AND FIXED IN-SESSION:** (1) the scaffold's `REVOKE ... FROM PUBLIC` did NOT strip Supabase's default **anon/authenticated EXECUTE** grants on two SECDEF fns, one of which writes to `sales` — caught on post-flight grant check, fixed by explicit per-role REVOKE (grants now postgres + service_role only). This is the documented SECDEF anon-grant regression; `REVOKE FROM PUBLIC` is not sufficient. (2) the cursor was set unconditionally to the batch min, so replaying a newer batch **rewound the watermark** and would re-walk covered ground — caught by the idempotency test, fixed with `LEAST(...)`.
- **PROVEN END-TO-END: 20 claimed → 20 decoded → 20 applied**, `scanned 20 / recovered 20 / undecodable 0`, audit table 20 rows, spot-checked real addresses on `sales`. Cursor at 2026-07-18T21:58:33Z.
- **RUNNER SHIPPED (Trevor chose the Cloudflare worker) — `workers/sales-counterparty-backfill/`.** Self-scheduling via **Cloudflare Cron Triggers** (`*/5 * * * *`), so it needs no cron-job.org entry and is structurally immune to the recurring external-trigger dropout class. Per tick: claim 120 newest-first → decode via Flow REST (concurrency 6, 12s timeout) → apply → `log_pipeline_run('sales-counterparty-backfill', …)`. `scheduled()` is Cloudflare-invoked (not externally reachable, no auth needed); `fetch()` is Bearer-`INGEST_SECRET_TOKEN`-gated for manual ticks + `/health`. Transient Flow REST timeouts are self-healing: the row stays NULL and is re-claimed on a later pass. **NOT on the `TS_PROXY_SECRET` rotation surface** — Flow's public REST endpoint is reachable directly from Workers, so no proxy secret is involved. **Cadence deliberately conservative** (120/5min ≈ 34.5k/day ⇒ ~9–10 weeks for the full 2.30M) because this UPDATEs the hottest table on an IOPS-constrained instance; newest-first means live-user value lands in days, and the long tail is old history. **OPERATOR (Trevor, one-time):** `cd workers/sales-counterparty-backfill && wrangler deploy`, then `wrangler secret put SUPABASE_URL|SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY|INGEST_SECRET_TOKEN --name sales-counterparty-backfill`. **Revert:** delete the worker (or `wrangler delete`); the DB fns are inert without a caller.
- **SUPERSEDED — runner options considered:** Needs a loop that calls claim → decode via Flow REST → apply, on a conservative cadence. ### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — WMC-LOCK-CHECK-COVERAGE re-diagnosed: it is a FRESHNESS failure that OVERSTATES locks, not a coverage gap that understates them

Investigated Trevor's "lock number doesn't seem accurate". The earlier framing (88.9% of TS wmc rows never lock-checked ⇒ "systematic lower bound") is **directionally wrong for real users**, and the fix it implies would be the wrong fix.

- **The 88.9% is real but concentrated in whales, not spread across users.** TS wmc has only **244 distinct wallets**, and **240 of them (98.4%) have been lock-checked**. The 1,430,158 unchecked ROWS sit in a handful of mega-wallets — the top 5 hold **357,150** of them (largest: 146,097 unchecked of 149,506 rows). So "88.9% unchecked" describes wallets nobody views; it does not describe a typical user's board.
- **The real defect is FRESHNESS, and it inverts the sign.** Reference wallet (`0xbd94…50ac`, 14,945 rows): **95.2% checked** — coverage is fine — but newest check **2026-07-12**, oldest 2026-04-13, and **14,203 rows last verified >30 days ago**. Of its 13,207 rows flagged `is_locked`, **13,183 were last verified >30d ago** and only **0** within 24h. **Top Shot locks EXPIRE**, so a months-old `is_locked=true` is very likely already released ⇒ the UI **OVERSTATES** locks for exactly the wallets users actually look at. An "understating" fix (chase raw coverage) would make this worse by spending scarce budget on whale rows instead of refreshing viewed ones.
- **The freshness promise is ~70× oversubscribed.** `app/api/cron/lock-check-batch/route.ts` declares `MAX_AGE_DAYS = 7` with `BATCH_LIMIT = 200`, scheduled every 30 min (48 runs/day ⇒ 9,600 rows/day ceiling). Honouring a 7-day refresh over 1.6M TS rows needs **~229,000 rows/day**. Measured actual: **22,985 rows in 7 days ≈ 3,283/day**, i.e. a full pass takes **~435 days** against a 7-day target. The route also burns batch slots on collections it cannot check (`unsupported_collections: {nfl_all_day: 200, laliga_golazos: 44}` every run — AllDay/Golazos/UFC have no on-chain lock primitive).
- **Implication for the fix (do NOT just raise throughput).** The Cadence leg is the bound, so 70× is not reachable by tuning. The correct shapes are (a) **scope the promise to what's viewable** — prioritise seeded/saved/verified wallets and refresh them on a real 7-day cycle (244 wallets, and the non-whale ones are small), letting whale rows go deliberately stale; (b) **stop pulling unsupported collections** into the batch entirely; (c) **display honesty** — surface "locks as of <date>" (or suppress the lock figure past a staleness threshold) so a months-old snapshot never reads as current; (d) optionally **on-demand re-check** when a user opens their own wallet view.
- **NOT shipped** — this changes what the fix should be, and the route is an ingest-adjacent hot path that was itself rewritten 2026-07-16 (`get_lock_check_batch` index-driven rewrite). Wants a deliberate owner session with the above shape, not a throughput bump. **Queued as WMC-LOCK-FRESHNESS (supersedes WMC-LOCK-CHECK-COVERAGE).**

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — SIZED the `sales` ingest gap independently: real, and ERA-CONCENTRATED (pre-2026 ~18-27% covered, 2026 ~61-74%)

Two conflicting figures were in play for the missing-rows gap: commit `65fbc146` recorded "39 real sales vs 8,352 lifetime withdrawals" for `0xbd94…50ac` (implying our data was ~complete for it), while the follow-up summary reported "486 on-chain sales vs 39 rows (~8%)". A multi-million-row insert into the partitioned hot `sales` table was about to be scoped on the latter, so it needed resolving first.

- **MEASURED DB-side, no Dune needed.** Independent test from the BUYER side: every marketplace purchase writes a `moment_acquisitions` row (`acquisition_method='marketplace'`), so an acquisition with no corresponding `sales` row is a missing sale. Result for Top Shot:

  | era | mkt acquisitions | sale row in ±2d | any sale row ever | coverage |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | pre-2026 | 6,733 | 1,217 | 1,851 | **18–27%** |
  | 2026 | 539 | 329 | 400 | **61–74%** |

- **CONCLUSION — the gap is REAL but neither figure was right.** Not ~8% (that was the ungated-withdrawals framing) and not ~0%. Historical sale ingest captured roughly a quarter of known marketplace purchases; current ingest captures two-thirds to three-quarters. The reference wallet reads worst-case (~8%) because its sales span 2024-03 → 2026-05, i.e. mostly the under-ingested era.
- **Corroborating shape:** TS sales/quarter run 104k–248k across 2023–2025 but **309k / 311k in 2026 Q1/Q2**, with 2026 Q3 tracking current daily volume (62,125 over 19 days ≈ 3,270/day). The market did not double in 2026 — the live indexer got complete while history stayed partial. Consistent with the counterparty cross-validation finding **0 conflicts across 13,874 recent rows**, which rules out large-scale row loss in the recent era.
- **The ±2d vs ever delta is itself a finding:** pre-2026, 634 acquisitions have a sale row that falls OUTSIDE a ±2-day window (1,217 → 1,851). Some of that is date drift on backfilled rows rather than true absence, so ~27% is the fairer historical coverage figure and any gap-filling job must dedup on `(tx_hash, nft_id)` rather than on date proximity or it will double-insert.
- **NOT SHIPPED.** Inserting into `sales` is a different risk class from the fill-only UPDATEs shipped this session: partitioned hot table, feeds FMV, and a bad insert is far harder to undo than a fill. This entry sizes the work; it does not start it. **Recommended scope when picked up: pre-2026 Top Shot only** (that is where ~73% of the loss is), sourced from the already-validated `flow.cadence_events` settlement-gated query, written through a new fill-or-insert RPC with `(tx_hash, nft_id)` dedup and its own audit table — mirroring `apply_sales_counterparty_external`.

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — All Day lock freshness was UNKNOWABLE: `allday-lock-refresh` wrote `is_locked` without ever stamping `lock_checked_at`

Found while auditing the lock pipeline per-collection. Small, bounded, and it unblocks the queued WMC-LOCK-FRESHNESS work.

- **THE ANOMALY.** Per-collection wmc lock state: `nfl_all_day` has **333,115 rows, 3,682 flagged `is_locked`, and 0 rows with any `lock_checked_at`** (`max(lock_checked_at)` NULL). Top Shot 179,750/1,608,798 checked, Pinnacle 44,350/44,368 (99.96%) — both stamped and current.
- **NOT phantom data — a missing timestamp.** `app/api/allday-lock-refresh/route.ts` legitimately recomputes All Day locks by diffing the on-chain unlocked-id set against wmc, so the 3,682 values are real. But it wrote **only** `is_locked` and never `lock_checked_at`. Consequences: (a) All Day lock freshness is unknowable, and since locks EXPIRE a stale `true` is a lie the UI cannot detect; (b) any staleness-based display-honesty fix would treat All Day as "never checked" and be unable to distinguish real-but-undated data from genuinely-missing data; (c) `lock-check-batch` reports All Day under `unsupported_collections` every run, implying nothing maintains its locks, when this route does.
- **SHIPPED (code).** Stamp `lock_checked_at` alongside both `is_locked` writes, **plus a third pass over every examined row**. That third pass is the load-bearing part: the two existing loops only touch rows whose lock state FLIPPED, so in the steady state (nothing changed) no row would ever be stamped and freshness would never advance — which is precisely the failure being fixed. The third pass writes only the timestamp, never `is_locked`: it asserts "verified at", not a value.
- **Test-safe (checked, not assumed):** `__tests__/api-allday-lock-refresh.test.ts` uses a chainable Supabase stub (`update: () => sb`) and asserts only on response-body counts (`total_cached`, `marked_locked`, `marked_unlocked`) — none of which changed. The added loop just calls the stub once more. Verified by reading the test; vitest cannot run from the Cowork sandbox (Windows-native `node_modules`), so **CI is the gate** — this is the same class as the 07-18 wave that left CI red 24h, and the new `ci-status` monitor job now watches for exactly that.
- **REVERT:** `git revert <sha>` (single route file, no schema change — `lock_checked_at` already existed).
- **⚠ CORRECTION (same session, ~1h later) — the fix is INERT and the All Day picture is WORSE than written above.** I claimed "`lock-check-batch` reports All Day as unsupported … when in fact this route does [maintain its locks]". **It does not.** `/api/allday-lock-refresh` has **ZERO rows in `pipeline_runs`** — the only lock pipeline that runs at all is `lock-check-batch` (153 runs, newest 2026-07-19 05:08). Nothing schedules the All Day route: not cron-job.org (no pipeline_runs telemetry would exist if it fired), not vercel.json, not GHA, not pg_cron. So the 3,682 All Day `is_locked` flags are **undated AND unmaintained** — frozen at whatever past manual invocation set them, with no refresh path. **My stamping fix is correct but dormant: it changes nothing until something calls the route.** Making All Day locks trustworthy therefore needs a scheduling decision (add a cron + a watchlist row, mirroring `lock-check-batch`) or an explicit decision to stop displaying All Day locks at all. Folded into WMC-LOCK-FRESHNESS. This is the same enumerate-the-callers failure the 07-18 seed-wallet gate produced — I should have checked `pipeline_runs` for the route before asserting it was live.

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — Panini: discovery is listing-GATED, not merely listing-biased — quantified + measurement view shipped; board surfacing deliberately NOT done

Investigating what Panini still needs before go-live. The runner is healthy (data 1.1h fresh, 375 `panini-ingest` runs/7d, 1,647 editions / 2,542 FMV rows / 7,105 serials). The blocker is not freshness or plumbing — it is **catalog completeness**, and it is worse and more structural than the standing "index is ~20% of the set and listing-biased" note.

- **FINDING (measured, launch-relevant) — discovery is strictly gated on being LISTED, and the bias is monotonic in scarcity.** The runner discovers editions by walking the marketplace grid, so an edition enters `panini_editions` only once it has been listed. Against the 474-player base checklist, discovery falls cleanly with scarcity: Red (avg cap 124) **64%** -> Silver (259) 45% -> Blue (49) 44% -> Cracked Ice (25) 33% -> Gold (10) **24%** -> Old Glory (7) 11% -> Black (cap 1) **8%** -> Nebula (cap 1) **7%**. The decisive tell: for the two 1-of-1 parallels (Black, Nebula) **100% of discovered copies are currently listed** (40/40 and 33/33). That is impossible for an unbiased sample of a real 1-of-1 population — it proves we can only ever see a 1-of-1 while its single copy happens to be for sale. Bucketed across all 55 families: **`listing_gated` 12 families / 102 editions (100% listed, avg cap 1), `heavily_biased` 17 / 459 (26–52%), `partial` 16 / 318 (10–24%), `broad` 10 / 768 (4–9%)** — i.e. only **768 of 1,647 editions (47%) sit in a trustworthy-coverage bucket**, and coverage is thinnest exactly where scarcity is highest.
- **Product consequence for `/insights/panini-squeeze`:** per-row numbers are HONEST — `rip_pct`, `still_in_packs`, `mint_cap` are true API supply stats for any discovered edition, so nothing displayed is wrong. The defect is **completeness**: the board is a leaderboard over a listing-gated sample, so it cannot support the implicit claim "these are THE squeezed cards", only "these are squeezed cards among those we happen to have indexed". The scarce tail — the most interesting squeeze candidates — is 7–24% present. Un-gating as-is would ship a board that is quietly least complete precisely where it is most interesting.
- **SHIPPED (DB) — `audit_20260719_panini_coverage_audit_view`: `public.panini_coverage_audit`.** Per (set_name, parallel_family): discovered_editions, avg_mint_cap, pulled, listed_now, `pct_pulled_listed` (the diagnostic — as it approaches 100 the family is visible to us ONLY through live listings), `pct_of_base_checklist`, a `coverage_flag` (broad / partial / heavily_biased / listing_gated), and refresh-age min/max. This is the measurement instrument for the gap: it lets the surface disclose real coverage instead of implying completeness, and lets a full-catalog walk be prioritized worst-family-first. `security_invoker = on`; `REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC` + `GRANT SELECT TO authenticated, service_role` (ops/diagnostic, deliberately NOT anon). **Revert:** `DROP VIEW public.panini_coverage_audit;`
- **DELIBERATELY NOT DONE — surfacing the 5 built-but-unsurfaced Panini boards.** Six views carry real data but only `panini_squeeze_board` has a route: `panini_deal_board` (136 rows), `panini_player_board` (552), `panini_nation_board` (71), `panini_special_serials_board` (1,012), `panini_pack_ev_board` (2), `panini_pack_ev_model` (1). Building pages for them looked like the obvious parity win, and it is the wrong next move: every one of them reads the SAME listing-gated index, so surfacing them now would **multiply one completeness defect across five more public boards** — and `panini_special_serials_board` is the worst case, since special serials live disproportionately in the scarce tail that is 7–24% covered. Fix coverage first, then surface; the views are ready and the squeeze page is the template, so the surfacing work is cheap once the index is trustworthy.
- **QUEUED (Panini, HIGH — the real go-live blocker):** full-catalog walk to replace listing-gated discovery. The runner already auto-enumerates pskus from the grid; the fix is to walk the CHECKLIST (all players x all parallel families) rather than the listings grid, so an edition is discovered whether or not it is currently for sale. Prioritize by `panini_coverage_audit` ascending `coverage_flag`. Until then, any public Panini surface should render an explicit coverage disclosure (same honesty stance as the 07-18 Sold-tab lower-bound note).
- **QUEUED (Panini, MED) — refresh cycle does not cover the catalog daily.** Only 848 of 1,647 editions were refreshed in the last 24h and the oldest rows are ~59h stale, so the 4h runner is not completing a full sweep between runs. Walk order was already shuffled (`0736fbc4`) so stalled runs rotate coverage; the residual is throughput, not ordering.

And the trailing id is not derivable — `player_id` is not a fixed function of `card_id` (41 distinct offsets in Base Prizms Red; only 13/54 parallels constant), and rank-alignment fails too (only **3 of 15** parallels ≥20 rows are perfectly co-monotonic; Red 271/304 rank mismatches, Spearman 0.938).

Field 2 has 54 distinct values (= the 54 set names), field 4 has 474 (= the checklist players). Anyone parsing pskus off the old comment will mis-attribute every card.

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — CORRECTION: `panini_editions.updated_at` is inert; my own coverage view was reading it. Fixed + trigger added

Self-correction. While verifying a claim I had put in the handoff ("coverage accumulates on its own"), I found the freshness column I had been measuring is not a freshness column at all — and that my own `panini_coverage_audit` view, shipped hours earlier, was reading it.

- **THE TRAP:** `public.panini_editions.updated_at` has `DEFAULT now()` and **NO trigger**, and `lib/chains/panini/ingest-normalize.ts` sets `last_seen_at` (not `updated_at`) on edition rows. So `updated_at` is written once at INSERT and never again. Verified live: `created_at = updated_at` on **1647/1647** rows, max gap **0.00h**. Anything reading it as freshness is reading INSERT AGE. The real per-row freshness column is **`last_seen_at`** (1,383 rows carry `last_seen_at > created_at`, max gap 29.5h).
- **WHAT I GOT WRONG (corrected):** the MED item below states "only 848 of 1,647 editions were refreshed in the last 24h ... the 4h runner is not completing a full sweep." That 848 is the count of editions **first INSERTED** in 24h. The true re-observation figure is **1,285 / 1,647 = 78% in 24h** (1,062 = 64% within 8h). The concern is real but much smaller than stated: there IS a stale tail out to **61.4h**, so the sweep is not complete, but daily coverage is 78% not 51%. Treat the MED item as re-scoped to "close the ~22% / 61h tail", not "the runner is missing half the catalog".
- **WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED:** the listing-GATED finding is independent of this bug and stands exactly as recorded — `coverage_flag` buckets re-verified post-fix at `listing_gated 12 / heavily_biased 17 / partial 16 / broad 10`, identical to before. The 100%-of-1-of-1s-are-listed proof does not involve either timestamp column.
- **ALSO NOW VERIFIED (was previously an assumption):** `created_at` IS a genuine first-seen stamp precisely BECAUSE it is never updated, so discovery drift IS measurable after all. Retention is real: 13 zero-listing editions persist, and rows sit unrefreshed up to 61h without being dropped. The handoff line claiming monotonic accumulation has been updated from assertion to verified fact.
- **SHIPPED (DB) — `audit_20260719_panini_freshness_column_fix`.** (a) `trg_panini_editions_touch_updated_at` (BEFORE UPDATE, sets `updated_at = now()`) so the column means what its name says from here on and stops being a trap for the next reader — this matches every other table's convention. (b) Recreated `panini_coverage_audit` against `last_seen_at`, and added two explicit columns so the distinction can never be silently conflated again: **`refreshed_24h`** (re-observed) and **`first_seen_24h`** (newly discovered). Post-fix totals: refreshed_24h **1,285**, first_seen_24h **848** — the two numbers I had collapsed into one. `security_invoker=on`, grants unchanged (authenticated + service_role), `check_secdef_anon_execute_violations()` `[]`. **Revert:** `DROP TRIGGER trg_panini_editions_touch_updated_at ON public.panini_editions; DROP FUNCTION public.panini_editions_touch_updated_at();` + recreate the prior view body from migration history.
- **BLAST RADIUS: exactly one object — my own view. Swept, nothing else affected.** Of the 7 views over `panini_editions` (`panini_squeeze_board`, `panini_coverage_audit`, `panini_pack_ev_model`, `panini_nation_board`, `panini_special_serials_board`, `panini_deal_board`, `panini_player_board`), **none** reference `updated_at` except the coverage view, now fixed (`pg_get_viewdef` sweep). Repo grep: the only hit is `docs/drafts/panini/panini-schema.sql`, a draft doc with no live consumer. **The daily `panini-freshness-check` scheduled task already reads `last_seen_at` correctly** — I flagged it as suspect in the first draft of this entry and that was wrong; retracted. Its own stated baseline ("a healthy full walk refreshes roughly 900-1,300 editions") in fact matches the corrected 1,285 figure, which is independent confirmation that 848 was the anomalous reading and not the truth.

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — RPC Packs: delivery-to-Dapper claim MEASURED (n=235, was asserted-only); the ~20-pack ceiling is a rail artifact, not a market ceiling

Follow-on to the pricing-engine entry below. Docs-only — no code, no schema, no prod state change. Doc: [docs/strategy/repack-drops-addendum-2026-07-18.md](../strategy/repack-drops-addendum-2026-07-18.md) §5.2.

- **CLOSED (measurement) — "delivery to a Dapper-custodial account is permissionless" was asserted in 3 docs + the ledger and NEVER probed.** It is load-bearing (`BREAK_MULTI_TRANSFER_TS` panics an entire 30-recipient chunk if one recipient can't receive) and it was pure contract-shape reasoning. Now measured from RPC's own production data: `app/api/wallet-backfill/route.ts:30-37` (the `wallet_moments_cache` writer) walks TS wallets via `getAccount(addr).capabilities.borrow<&{TopShot.MomentCollectionPublic}>(/public/MomentCollection)`, returning `[]` when the cap is absent — so **every wmc row is a successful public-capability borrow**. Live: of **244** TS wallets in wmc, **235 have never appeared in `linked_accounts` in any role** (no hybrid custody, no self-custody parent) and hold **1,558,636 moments**. Separately, 9 known Dapper-custodial *children* hold 50,162 moments while their self-custody parents hold **0** — moments live in the custodial account, as the model predicts. **The public collection capability demonstrably exists on ordinary never-linked Top Shot accounts at n=235.**
- **RESIDUAL INFERENCE (named, not papered over):** the walk borrows `TopShot.MomentCollectionPublic`; the delivery paths borrow `NonFungibleToken.CollectionPublic` (`break-transactions.ts:34,63`) and `NonFungibleToken.Receiver` (`gift.ts:77`). Same published cap **iff** it is published as concrete `&TopShot.Collection` — which `docs/audits/purchase-moment-2026-05.md:203` recorded from a live Cadence MCP read — since a concrete-type cap is borrowable as any conforming interface. Standard Cadence semantics, high confidence, but reasoning not measurement. `/api/wallet-preflight` borrows exactly `NonFungibleToken.CollectionPublic` and would close it in one GET, but it is **not** on the `proxy.ts` public allowlist and auth config was deliberately NOT modified to reach it (off-limits class).
- **QUEUED (OPERATOR, ~2 min, Trevor) — one low-value gift on mainnet closes the last inch.** `moment_gifts` has **0 rows**: the live `/dashboard/gift` parent-signed flow has never executed end-to-end. Sending one common moment to a Dapper-custodial recipient converts the residual inference into a measurement AND smoke-tests a shipped-but-unexercised feature. Highest value-per-minute item in the RPC Packs workstream.
- **STRATEGIC CONSEQUENCE — the ~20-packs-per-drop ceiling is a RAIL artifact, not a market ceiling.** Vaultopolis's buyers must sign a FLOW Storefront purchase (needs a FLOW-funded FCL wallet), which is the most likely cause of drop 7 selling 8 of 40. Delivery is a *separate* leg and is unwalled. So **selling for credits/Stripe (off-chain) + delivering on-chain removes the buyer-side FLOW/self-custody requirement entirely** — buyer needs no FLOW, no FCL wallet, no signature, just a TS account that can receive. Addressable pool goes from the ~108 linked wallets to ~every TS account (RPC alone indexes **4,031 active buyers/90d**). This points the same direction as the legal analysis: **transparent lots + off-chain payment + on-chain delivery is simultaneously the legal-clean shape and the large-market shape**; the sealed FLOW-priced pack is both the risky one and the small one.
- **Recommendation updated (§7.1 next steps, ordered):** (1) operator gift probe; (2) generalize the scorer into an arbitrary-moment-set lot pricer; (3) only then inventory/cost-basis + `shop_items` lot listing, re-funding payer wallet `0x73f55c4450b8d466` first; (4) do NOT start `RPCPacks`/commit-reveal/multi-chain.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (docs-only).

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — INCIDENT: ledger clobbered by `fecda2e` (13 entries); restored + CI guard shipped; Candy sales-indexer confirmed live-clean

- **INCIDENT — commit `fecda2e` silently deleted 13 ledger entries** (**353 → 340 entries; 3,298 → 3,184 lines**) **while ADDING its own entry**, so the diff looked like normal growth.
- **CORRECTION to my own first draft of this entry (verified, was wrong):** I initially reported this as TWO clobbers and named `eb5d7f6` as the second. **That was false and is retracted.** `eb5d7f6` touched only `.github/workflows/ops-monitor.yml` (+52 lines) and never touched the ledger — verified via `git diff eb5d7f6~1 eb5d7f6 -- docs/overnight/ledger.md` (empty). What misled me: my FIRST restore commit was rejected on push (`! [rejected] main -> main`) and never landed, so the "137 deleted lines" I measured were the diff between my own **unpushed local** restore and the remote, not a deletion by anyone. A per-commit sweep of the last 40 ledger commits confirms exactly ONE entry-count drop: `fecda2e`. Falsely attributing data loss to a commit — and by implication to another session — is not a thing to leave in the permanent record. Cause is the documented concurrent-session hazard: a session reads the ledger, works for a long stretch, then writes its whole in-memory version back, so everything committed in the interim vanishes. **Not a Cowork-vs-Claude-Code thing — the losses spanned both**, and the single most costly casualty was Claude Code's OWN `Candy best-offer capture SHIPPED (candy_offers + candy-offers-indexer)` entry, which carries the revert path for a live prod migration. Also lost: `package-lock "desync" is NOT real`, `Sales seller-recovery, both lanes: 16,492 rows`, `chain-rename TODO COMPLETE`, `Per-wallet Dune seller-recovery`, 3 Cowork RPC-Packs entries and 5 Cowork Candy/Panini entries. **Losing revert paths for shipped prod DB changes is precisely the failure the ledger exists to prevent.**
- **RESTORED non-destructively.** Recomputed from the union of the pre-clobber snapshots (`b860648`, `fecda2e`), splicing back only blocks whose `### ` heading is absent from the CURRENT file — so `fecda2e`'s own new entry was explicitly preserved. Verified: **0 duplicate headings, 354 headings, `fecda2e`'s entry present exactly once, line count reconciles** (3,184 + 14 restored blocks = 3,314).
- **DURABLE RULE — now MECHANICALLY ENFORCED, not just documented.** Shipped a `ledger-guard` CI job (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, pure bash, no deps): on every push to `main` it compares `grep -c '^### '` between `HEAD~1` and `HEAD` and **fails the build if the entry count DROPPED**, with an `[ledger-roll]` commit-message opt-out for the legitimate biweekly `rpc-context-hygiene` archive roll. Validated against real history before shipping: FAILs on `fecda2e` (353→340), PASSes on clean appends (`19aae22` 340→341, `53100f6` 352→353, the restore 340→355), SKIPs commits that don't touch the ledger. Behavioural rule stands too: the ledger is APPEND-AT-TOP and must be re-read from disk immediately before writing. Never write back a whole copy you read earlier in the session. Splice your entry into the freshly-read file, then sanity-check `grep -c '^### ' docs/overnight/ledger.md` went UP by exactly the number of entries you added — if it went DOWN, you just destroyed someone's revert path. A rejected `git push` is the tell that someone else landed work; re-read after every pull, never rebase a whole-file rewrite.
- **CONFIRMED (post-ship watch) — the Candy sales-indexer arming decision was correct.** First live tick 2026-07-19 03:20:22Z: **ok=true, sales_found 0, written 0, skipped 0, no error**, `sol_usd` 75.92, duration 59s. Exactly as predicted — armed against the live ME symbol it polls for real, `SALE_TYPES` excludes `bid` so the bid-only book yields nothing, and the first printed sale is now captured automatically. Also proves **Vercel egress reaches Magic Eden** (Claude Code's sandbox is blocked; production is not), which was the open risk on the offers route built without live API access. CI green on `b255eb1` (8/8 checks).
- **CORRECTION — SOL is ~$76, not ~$150.** Live tick reports `sol_usd: 75.92`. I earlier valued the standing Candy bids at "$0.50-$6"; the true range for the observed 0.003-0.04 SOL bids is **~$0.23-$3.04**. Strengthens the honesty constraint: a ~$0.23 bid on a /15 Rainbow parallel is a lowball floor and must never be shown as, or folded into, FMV.
- **QUEUED (LOW) — CANDY-SALES-INDEXER-UNBOUNDED-ACTIVITIES-WALK.** With 0 sales the high-water cursor is 0, so `reachedKnown` never trips and every tick walks the full `MAX_PAGES = 40` window — the 59s duration on a tick that found nothing, i.e. ~40 Magic Eden calls every 3h (~320/day) until the first sale lands. Inside `after()` and ok=true, so not dangerous today, but a standing rate-limit exposure (a 429 throws in `fetchActivities` → ok=false). ### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — Panini coverage disclosure BUILT INTO the squeeze surface (page + API contract + test), so go-live can't ship a census claim by accident

Branch 2b requires that any public Panini surface disclose its own coverage. Making that a documented instruction is weak — someone un-gates the proxy line and the disclosure is forgotten. Built it into the surface instead, in both the render path and the response contract.

- **SHIPPED (code) — `app/insights/panini-squeeze/page.tsx` + `PaniniSqueezeClient.tsx`.** The server page now fetches `panini_coverage_summary` in parallel with the board (`Promise.all`) and passes it to the client, which renders a bordered disclosure directly under the subtitle: *"RPC indexes 1,647 editions of this set. Panini publishes no full checklist, so an edition is indexed once it has been listed for sale — coverage is strongest on high-print parallels (46.6% of indexed editions) and thinnest on the scarcest ones (102 editions across 12 of 54 parallels are visible to us only while listed). Treat this board as a floor, not a census."* All figures come from the self-measuring view, so the wording can never drift from reality. Brand tokens only (`--rpc-red`, `--rpc-surface`, `--rpc-border`, `--rpc-text-*`) per the no-hardcoded-literals rule. The `coverage` prop is optional and defaults to null, and the fetch is fail-soft (logs + returns null), so a coverage error degrades to "no banner" and can never take the board down.
- **SHIPPED (code) — `app/api/public/insights/panini-squeeze/route.ts` now carries `meta.coverage`.** Same figures plus `basis: "listing_gated"` and an explicit `note` ending "Treat as a floor, not a census." Putting it in the CONTRACT means an API consumer (or the OG card, or a future embed) cannot render this board as complete by accident — not just the one page we happen to have styled. Also fail-soft: a coverage-query error logs and nulls the block; the board rows are the primary payload and still serve 200.
- **SHIPPED (test) — `__tests__/api-public-panini-squeeze.test.ts`, 5 tests, all green.** The route had NO test before, so this both pins the new contract and keeps the coverage ratchet honest (net-new covered lines rather than net-new uncovered ones). Pins: invalid-tier 400; board-error 500; `meta.coverage` shape incl. the "floor, not a census" / "no full checklist" wording; **fail-soft** (coverage error → `coverage: null` but rows still served); and empty-summary → null. Verified `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- **Net effect on go-live:** un-gating Panini is still the single `proxy.ts:127` deletion, but the honesty requirement is now structural rather than a checklist item someone has to remember. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (page/client/route/test only — no schema change; `panini_coverage_summary` stays as an independently useful ops view).

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — the Candy bid book is INTERNALLY RATIONAL (prices scarcity ~8x); my own "suppress when distinct_bidders = 1" guard would have inverted the board — retracted

Analysed the first real `candy_offers` data (47 standing offers, 2 bidders, 24 editions) to test whether the captured signal carries information or is noise. It carries information — and the answer overturns a guard I proposed earlier this session.

- **The bid book prices scarcity correctly.** Broken out by tier: **LEGENDARY (Rainbow, circ 15)** — 5 editions with offers, avg best offer **$2.74** (range $1.52-$3.04), 7 offers total. **COMMON (base ICON, circ 250)** — 19 editions, avg best offer **$0.34** (range $0.23-$1.90), 40 offers. That is a **~8x premium for the 16.7x-scarcer tier**, rationally ordered. So while the book is thin and lowball in ABSOLUTE terms (2 wallets, all sub-$5), its RELATIVE ordering is meaningful — which is exactly the property that makes a "best offer" column informative even when the levels are low. It also means the sweep is resolving mints to the right editions (a mis-mapped gate would smear tiers together, not separate them cleanly).
- **RETRACTED — my "suppress the display when `distinct_bidders = 1`" suggestion is backwards and must not be implemented as stated.** The data: **LEGENDARY editions have `max_bidders` = 1; COMMON editions have 2.** The second wallet bids only on commons. So a per-edition `distinct_bidders >= 2` gate would **hide every scarce/chase row and show only the commons** — precisely inverting what a collector cares about, and making the board look like the cheap tier is the whole market. I proposed that guard before any data existed; the first real tick disproves it.
- **Better shape (for whenever Candy has a surface):** do not suppress on bidder count — **display it as context** ("best offer $2.74 · 1 bidder") and let the reader weigh it. If a suppression rule is wanted at all, apply it at the COLLECTION level (e.g. hide the whole column while the entire book is a single wallet), never per-edition, because per-edition bidder counts are correlated with scarcity and therefore with interest. Honesty constraint unchanged and reinforced: best-offer framing only, never FMV, never `fmv_snapshots`.
- **VERIFIED in production — the Panini coverage disclosure ships correctly in BOTH surfaces.** Rendered DOM at `/insights/panini-squeeze`: h1, 4 KPI cards, 300 table rows, no client exception, `.psq-cov` banner live. Public JSON `/api/public/insights/panini-squeeze?limit=3`: **HTTP 200 with `meta.coverage` present** — `total_editions` 1769, `pct_trustworthy` 46.4, `listing_gated_editions` 115, `families` 54, `basis: "listing_gated"`, and the note matching /floor, not a census/. Figures track the live view between reads, confirming nothing is hardcoded in either path.

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — SELF-AUDIT of the Panini disclosure: my own headline number was misreadable and its denominator was a lower bound. Fixed to a range + caveat.

Audited the coverage disclosure I shipped earlier today, because it puts a number I invented onto a public-bound surface. The bucketing survived; the headline did not.

- **VALIDATED — the `coverage_flag` thresholds are sound.** They are my own heuristic (`pct_pulled_listed` >= 90 / 25 / 10), so I tested them against an INDEPENDENT measure, `pct_of_base_checklist` (discovered ÷ checklist players). They order **perfectly, with no overlap**: `broad` = 64.5 / 47.2 / 46.2% of checklist · `partial` = 36.8 · `heavily_biased` = 26.3 / 18.9 / 15.6 / 14.4 / 12.9 · `listing_gated` = 9.4 / 8.6. So the listed-fraction proxy really does track true completeness, and the buckets are trustworthy.
- **DEFECT 1 (fixed) — the headline was MISREADABLE.** The banner led with `pct_trustworthy` ("46.7% of indexed editions"). That is a **composition** statistic — the share of editions sitting in well-covered families — **not a coverage percentage**. A reader will take "46.7%" to mean "RPC has 46.7% of the set", which is wrong in BOTH directions: real per-parallel coverage runs ~**65%** (Base Prizms Red) down to ~**9%** (the 1-of-1 parallels). Publishing one ambiguous number in place of the true range is the kind of thing the disclosure exists to prevent.
- **DEFECT 2 (fixed) — the denominator is a LOWER BOUND, and it moved under me.** The "checklist" is itself discovered data (distinct players across base families). It **grew 474 → 487** during the day, with **26-44 players first seen in the last 24h**. So the true checklist is at least as large as what we have seen, and **every percent-of-checklist figure is an upper bound on true coverage** — i.e. reality is somewhat worse than any number we can print. That has to be stated, not buried.
- **SHIPPED (DB) — `audit_20260719_panini_coverage_summary_honest_range`.** Adds `best_family_checklist_pct`, `worst_family_checklist_pct`, `checklist_players_seen`, `checklist_players_new_24h` to `panini_coverage_summary`; existing columns untouched so page + API keep working. View COMMENT now warns that `pct_trustworthy` is a composition share and that the checklist count is a lower bound. **Revert:** recreate the prior view body from migration history.
- **SHIPPED (code) — disclosure rewritten to lead with the RANGE plus the caveat.** New copy: *"RPC indexes N editions of this set. Panini publishes no full checklist, so a card is indexed only once it has been listed for sale. Coverage per parallel runs from about 65% down to 9% — thinnest exactly where cards are scarcest (118 editions across 12 of 54 parallels are visible to us only while listed). We are also still finding players we had not seen (26 new in the last 24h), so our own checklist count is a lower bound and these figures are best-case. Treat this board as a floor, not a census."* Same treatment in the public JSON `note`, which now explicitly says `pct_trustworthy` is a COMPOSITION share and `checklist_players_seen` is a LOWER bound. Both paths still fail-soft.
- **SHIPPED (test) — anti-misreading guards pinned.** `__tests__/api-public-panini-squeeze.test.ts` now asserts the note matches `/COMPOSITION share/i` and `/LOWER bound/i` alongside the range fields, so a future edit cannot quietly strip the caveats and leave a bare percentage. 5/5 green, `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- **Trend note:** `pct_trustworthy` continued to slide during the audit — **46.6% → 46.4% → 45.6%** as the index grew 1,647 → 1,769 → 1,842. This is the third independent confirmation that waiting does not improve the quality ratio.

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — BUG found by rendering the page: every Panini KPI was a top-300 slice presented as a set-level total (Sealed copies off by 30x). Fixed.

Rendering the squeeze board (rather than trusting tsc + tests) surfaced a real user-visible defect on the surface that is one line from going public.

- **THE BUG.** All four KPIs were computed client-side from `initialRows`, the server page's `.limit(300)` slice — so they described the page while reading as set-level headlines. Worst, the KPI row said **"EDITIONS 300"** directly beneath a coverage banner saying **"RPC indexes 1,842 editions"** — a flat contradiction on the same screen. Displayed vs truth: **Editions 300 vs 1,833 (-84%) · Value sealed $703,804 vs $938,170 (-25%) · Chases ≤/25 271 vs 935 (-71%) · Sealed copies 742 vs 22,575 (-97%, off by ~30x)**. Sealed copies is the extreme case for a structural reason: top-300-BY-FMV are scarce low-print cards, while nearly all sealed volume sits in high-print commons that never make that cut — ordering by FMV maximally anti-correlates with what that KPI measures.
- **SHIPPED (DB) — `audit_20260719_panini_squeeze_totals_view`: `public.panini_squeeze_totals`.** One row, whole-board: `editions`, `sealed_fmv_exposure_usd`, `chases_lte_25`, `sealed_copies`, using the same `fmv_usd IS NOT NULL` predicate as the page/API so figures are directly comparable to the rows beneath them. `security_invoker=on`; `REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC` + `GRANT SELECT TO authenticated, service_role`. **Revert:** `DROP VIEW public.panini_squeeze_totals;`
- **SHIPPED (code) — KPIs now read whole-board totals, fail-soft.** `page.tsx` fetches totals in the same `Promise.all` as rows + coverage; the client prefers `totals?.x` and falls back to the slice-derived values on error, so a totals failure degrades to the old behaviour rather than blanking the KPIs. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **ALSO FIXED — the asymmetry the fix introduced.** With whole-board KPIs, a reader sees "Editions 1,833" above a 300-row table and reasonably assumes the table is the whole set. Added a scope note beneath it: *"Showing the top 300 editions by FMV. The totals above cover all 1,833 indexed editions."* Rendered only when totals exceed displayed rows; brand tokens only.
- **Standing lesson, restated because it paid out twice in one session:** `tsc --noEmit` + green tests proved the code *compiles and behaves as written* — they could never catch this, because the code did exactly what it said. Only rendering the DOM exposed a headline wrong by 30x. Read CLAUDE.md's "verify by rendered DOM, not HTTP 200" as "not HTTP 200 **and not a green test suite** either".

### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — Panini Item 1 RESOLVED (no catalog exists — 2b is the path) + coverage-disclosure data; Candy best-offer expiry guard

Closed out both handoff items to a terminal state.

- **RESOLVED — Panini has NO catalog surface, so listing-gated discovery is a PLATFORM limit, not a fixable defect.** Settled by driving the logged-in SPA directly rather than waiting on an operator session. The complete authenticated route map is: `/`, `/marketplace/nfts.html`, per-card `/<psku>.html`, `/claim/claim_bonus_card.html`, 11 `/myaccount/**` pages, and static/social — **no checklist, set-browse, catalog or collection route anywhere.** The grid's facets (YEAR / COLLECTION / **CARD SET** / TEAM / ATHLETE / RARITY / CARD TYPE / BADGES / OWNERSHIP) sit ON the `getMarketPlaceList` **listings** query, so filtering by CARD SET narrows which listings you see and never surfaces an unlisted card (`OWNERSHIP` is the lone non-marketplace axis and returns only the signed-in user's own cards). Consistent with the op's own name and with 100% of discovered 1-of-1s being currently listed. **=> handoff branch 2b.** Residual uncertainty is small but non-zero (a checklist could hide behind an unlabelled control rather than a route), so the shipped capture instrumentation (`PANINI_DISCOVERY_HOLD_MIN` / `PANINI_DISCOVERY_ONLY`) makes the 10-minute operator session **confirmatory, not deciding**. Handoff Item 1 rewritten accordingly.
- **SHIPPED (DB) — `audit_20260719_panini_coverage_summary_view`: `public.panini_coverage_summary`.** One row backing the now-MANDATORY coverage disclosure on any public Panini surface: total_editions, trustworthy_editions, pct_trustworthy, listing_gated_editions/families, families, and family refresh min/max. Live values: **1,647 total · 768 trustworthy (46.6%) · 102 listing-gated across 12 of 54 families · refresh 3.8-29.9h.** It self-measures, so the disclosure can never go stale and nothing is hardcoded; suggested copy is in the handoff. `security_invoker=on`; `REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC` + `GRANT SELECT TO authenticated, service_role` (the public JSON route reads via service role, same as the squeeze board). **Revert:** `DROP VIEW public.panini_coverage_summary;`
- **SHIPPED (DB) — `audit_20260719_candy_best_offers_expiry_guard`.** Reviewing Claude Code's offers pipeline end-to-end: the deactivation logic is genuinely well-guarded (sweep-based deactivation runs only when `bidderFetchErrors === 0 && !biddersTruncated`, so a partial fetch can never mark standing offers dead; expiry-based deactivation runs unconditionally, which is right; and it soft-sets `is_active=false` rather than deleting, so nothing is destroyed). **But `candy_best_offers` filtered only on `is_active`, not on `expiry`** — and expired rows are only flipped off when the 6-hourly sweep runs, so between ticks an already-expired bid could still set `best_offer_sol` for up to 6h. That is the one signal that must be true (capturing bids is only defensible because "best offer" is honest where a bid-derived FMV would not be), so the view is now self-correcting: added `AND (o.expiry IS NULL OR o.expiry > now())` — NULL expiry means "no expiry", not expired, so it still passes. Read-side only: no data change, `is_active` semantics untouched, sweep unchanged, identical column list so grants were preserved (verified: anon SELECT, authenticated SELECT, service_role write). `check_secdef_anon_execute_violations()` `[]`. **Revert:** recreate the prior view body (same definition minus the expiry predicate) from migration history.
