### 2026-07-25 (Claude Code, interactive) — MEASURED the historical-sales gap (Trevor: "we should have all historical sales"). Blocked on Dune billing + an 85–90% edition-resolution miss. NOTHING SHIPPED — decision required.

Measurement only, no code/DB change. Trevor rejected "accept the loss", so I measured. **The 23505 bug is a rounding error next to a missing ERA.** Full write-up: [docs/handoff-2026-07-25-sales-indexer-23505-batch-loss.md](../handoff-2026-07-25-sales-indexer-23505-batch-loss.md) §5.

- **The gap, self-evident from our own data:** `sales` = 4.56M rows. By partition 2020 79k / **2021 166k** / 2022 748k / 2023 **1.21M** / 2024 804k / 2025 738k / 2026 815k. **Top Shot alone: 166,141 in 2021 (mania year) vs 679,691 in 2023 (quiet year) — 4.1×.** (TS-to-TS; the raw 2023 partition of 1,209,696 includes other collections.) Intra-2021 TopShot is inverted vs reality (Jan 74,969 → Feb **27,552** → Mar 7,133). The 2020–21 V1 `Market.MomentPurchased` era is essentially absent.
- **Blocker 1 — `DUNE-DATAPOINT-CAP-402` (hard stop).** `sales-ingest-dune` fires every 2h, **4 ok / 37 runs**; every tick since 07-24 06:23Z dies on `HTTP 402 … exceed your configured datapoint limit per billing cycle`. Cursor parked at **2025-06-21** against a 2019-01-01 floor (~6 months done of ~7 years), `inserted: 0`. The 07-19 `window_days` 7→2 hedge did NOT clear it — the cap is per *billing cycle*, not per request.
- **Blocker 2 — edition resolution, the deeper one.** Even on the 4 successful runs, ~**85–90%** of each batch was dropped `skipped_unresolved` (e.g. 152,195 found → 139,266 unresolved → **1,074 inserted**). Cause: `nft_id → edition` resolves via `moments`, which holds only **565,345** rows (`nft_edition_map` 130,946) against a TopShot mint universe in the millions. **And `apply_sales_ingest_external` does NOT park the unresolved rows** (verified against the live function definition — no `unmapped_sales` reference); they are counted and discarded, so every Dune datapoint spent on them is spent again on any re-run.
- **⇒ Key conclusion: lifting the Dune cap TODAY would burn ~85–90% of the spend on rows we immediately throw away.** Recommended order: (1) free — park unresolved rows in `unmapped_sales`; (2) free — extend the AllDay-proven `backfill_nft_edition_map_from_sales` immutable-edition trick (pg_cron jobid 215) to TopShot, then re-measure the miss rate; (3) only then size the Dune spend, and evaluate the free Flow-REST lane that already beat Dune once here (`sales_counterparty_recovered` 26,127 → 208,834).
- **Not shipped deliberately:** (1)+(2) are `sales` ingest/resolution logic (off-limits for autonomous shipping) and (3) is a billing decision. All three are Trevor's call.

Sentinel reported `hard 37/38` — `check_public_security_invariants()`: `rls_off_base_table` on `audit_20260725_allday_v1_unsplittable_retag` (19,589 rows) and `audit_20260725_allday_unmapped_dedupe_tx_nft`. - **Verified functionally, not from `information_schema`:** both now `rls_on=true, policies=0, anon_sel=false, auth_sel=false, svc_sel=true`; `check_public_security_invariants()` → **0 violations**; `rls_off` public base tables → **0**; anon-readable `audit_*` tables → **0**.

Latest-wins would bake those into `nft_edition_map` → propagates into sale resolution → FMV. Needs an **ambiguity-safe variant** (`count(DISTINCT edition_id)=1` only, quarantine the rest). And (2) it only drains nft_ids already in `unmapped_sales`, which the Dune path never populates — so **"park unresolved rows" is a hard prerequisite**, not an optimisation.

Drained the 07-24 sweep FLAG and re-audited the two crons shipped earlier today. **The reported symptom was real but its stated root cause was wrong**, and the previously "expected LOW yield" lanes were in fact structurally incapable of yielding. All DB-only via MCP; every claim below measured live. Times Pacific.

- **VERDICT — inflow vs outflow.** Backlog measured **43,066 open** (not 44,021; it had already drained slightly). Inflow is a *bounded historical backfill winding down*, but NOT as fast as the sweep said: it claimed 07-25 = 163, actual **07-25 = 1,909 / 07-24 = 2,051** (sweep measured a partial day). Autonomous outflow was **~81 rows/24h** from the resolver, so inflow beat drain **~25:1** and the ETA was infinite. **Correction to the sweep:** "each nft_id appears ~2x (duplicate ingestion), so distinct events = half" is wrong — measured duplication on `(transaction_hash, nft_id)` is **9 rows**, not ~21k. The repeated nft_ids are the same moment re-sold in DIFFERENT txs, i.e. distinct real sales. The backlog is ~43k genuinely distinct sale events.

- **DECOMPOSITION (the backlog is 4 cohorts, not one blob).** price ✓ / edition ✗ **20,196** · price ✗ / edition ✗ **16,459** · price ✗ / edition ✓ **6,397** · price ✓ / edition ✓ **14**. Exactly **14 of 43,066 rows were promote-eligible** (verified by replaying `promote_unmapped_sales`' own candidate predicate), so the resolver's "0.4% yield" was never a tuning problem — 43,052 rows were missing an input no amount of resolver work could supply.

- **DEFECT 1 — `allday-price-recover` could never reach its own work (the no-cursor class).** Its selector is `.eq(price_extraction,'v1_tx_decode_budget_exhausted').limit(2000)` with **no cursor, no ORDER BY, no attempted-marker**; PostgREST caps the page at 1,000, so all **42 ticks/24h returned the identical 1,000 rows** — `candidates=1000, distinct_txs=255, fail_reasons={multi_nft_tx_total_unsplittable:1000}, written 0, ok=true`. Every one of those rows belongs to a multi-NFT V1 Dapper tx that is **genuinely unpriceable** (`decodeV1SaleTx` sums every DUC `TokensWithdrawn` from the DUC contract = the GROSS for the whole tx, and uses `nftId` only to pick buyer/seller — there is no per-NFT attribution, so splitting would fabricate an FMV input). Measured split: **19,589 rows / 4,910 txs unsplittable (2–4 NFTs each) vs 3,267 rows in single-NFT txs the route CAN decode but never saw.**
  - **SHIPPED `audit_20260725_allday_v1_unsplittable_retag` (+`_apply`)** — recorded the route's own already-verified verdict durably instead of re-deriving it every 20 min: re-tagged the 19,589 unsplittable rows to `price_extraction='v1_tx_decode_multi_nft_unsplittable'` (+`unsplittable_nfts_in_tx`, `unsplittable_marked_at`). Attempted-marker pattern applied *through the hint the consuming route already filters on*, so it needed **no code push**. Original hints preserved verbatim in the audit table. ### 2026-07-25 (Claude Code, interactive) — SHIPPED (data-only): repositioned the Dune backward cursor OFF our best-covered era and ONTO the actual gap. A full month of Dune budget was spent re-walking 2025.

Trevor spotted that the whole month's Dune usage went in one day. Confirmed from `pipeline_runs` and it is worse than "we ran out" — **we spent it on the wrong era.**

**What 2026-07-24 actually bought (4 ok runs, 37 windows, ~74 days of history):**

| | rows | share |
|---|---|---|
| pulled | **581,664** | 100% |
| discarded as edition-unresolvable | 517,553 | **89.0%** |
| already had | 56,926 | 9.8% |
| counterparty fills on existing rows (real value) | 55,292 | — |
| **new sales gained** | **7,104** | **1.2%** |

**Root cause of the low yield: the walker starts at 2025-12-31 and walks BACKWARD, so it was grinding through the era we already cover best.** TS rows already held — **2025: 612,219** · 2022: 159,812 · **2021: 166,141** · **2020: 79,160**. It had only reached 2025-06-21, i.e. it would have burned many more monthly budgets on 2025→2022 before ever touching the 2020–21 boom, which is the era that is structurally absent (TS-only: 166,141 rows for 2021 vs 679,691 for 2023 — 4.1× fewer despite 2021 being the mania year).

- **CHANGED (1 row, `sales_ingest_state`):** `cursor_end` **2025-06-21 → 2022-01-01**. `floor_date` (2019-01-01) and `window_days` (2) unchanged. The next budget cycle now walks 2021-12-31 backward into 2020–21, where marginal value per datapoint is highest.
- **Known trade-off, recorded:** this SKIPS 2022-01-01..2025-06-21. That range is comparatively well covered, and it can be swept later by setting `cursor_end` back to `2025-06-21` with `floor_date` `2022-01-01`.
- **Compounding fix already live:** the parking shipped earlier today means a future pull no longer *discards* that 89% — it retains it for later resolution, so each datapoint is bought once instead of being re-bought on every pass.
- **Still blocked on the operator:** the datapoint cap itself. Nothing flows until Dune's cycle resets or the plan is raised — this change only ensures the *next* budget lands on the gap instead of on 2025.
- **Revert:** `UPDATE public.sales_ingest_state SET cursor_end = DATE '2025-06-21', updated_at = now() WHERE id = 1;`

### 2026-07-25 (Claude Code, interactive) — test-coverage pass (cont. 26): sniper-feed 50%→83% — and a TEST-HARNESS BUG that was silently voiding an existing test

Test-only, behavior-preserving. Biggest single-route jump of the whole program.

- **BUG FOUND IN THE HARNESS (the important part).** `makeSupabaseFixture` captures its fixtures object **by reference**. Any test that does `fx.tables = { ... }` (plain reassignment, the obvious idiom) **detaches** it — the fixture keeps serving the original object, so every table reads empty. The pre-existing `api-sniper-feed-compute` "runs the compute body end-to-end over a populated pool" case was therefore asserting on **zero deals** while appearing to pass: its only assertions were `Array.isArray(body.deals)` and `count === deals.length`, both trivially true on an empty feed. Diagnosed from the route's own `[sniper-feed] ts_listings: 0 rows` log. **Fix:** the mock now hands the fixture a live `Proxy` view of `fx.tables`, so both reassignment and in-place mutation are seen. **Any other test using this fixture with reassignment has the same latent defect — worth a sweep.**
- **`/api/sniper-feed` 50.3%st/34.9br → 82.8%/62.7.** With the fixture actually connected, added the data contract that makes the enrichment fan-out execute instead of early-returning on empties: `get_editions_for_sniper` (edition resolution parses `"Player — Set"` out of `edition.name` — the key nothing else supplies), `editions` → `fmv_snapshots` joined by uuid, `badge_editions` by player, `players` by jersey, and a `serial_fmv_estimate` RPC for the `#1`-serial path. Now covers `fetchTopShotPool` → `resolveEditionKeys` → `fetchFmvBatch` → `fetchBadgesByPlayers` → `fetchJerseyNumbers` → `attachSerialFmvEstimates` → build/sort/filter, plus the newest-snapshot-wins dedupe (stale duplicate ignored), `editions.thumbnail_url` preferred over the constructed asset URL, degradation on a `badge_editions` **and** a `players` read error, the editions-miss and no-FMV unpriced feeds, and `?limit=`.

**HYGIENE CLOSEOUTS (this pass).**

**1. The wmc lock-freshness "crisis" was the METRIC, not the pipeline — false alarm retired.**

- **Carried as:** `MAX_AGE_DAYS=7` promise ~70x oversubscribed, ~1.61M of 2,038,344 `wallet_moments_cache` rows (79%) stale. **Refuted at the column level.** wmc has **two independent** freshness dimensions and the alarm collapsed them into one.
- **Ownership freshness is genuinely healthy.** `wallet-backfill` enumerates each wallet's **complete** on-chain id set every run; cached ids in that set are **confirmed still owned** and the `skip_cached` path then writes nothing. Measured live: **2,390,895 such confirmations in 24h** vs **~291,192/day** needed to honour a 7-day promise across 2,048,775 rows — an **~8.2x surplus** — and **250 distinct wallets walked in 72h against 246 distinct Top Shot wmc wallets**, i.e. every wallet every <=3 days. `last_seen_at` nonetheless showed **1,188,087** Top Shot rows older than 30 days, because `upsert_wmc_batch`'s 2026-06-10 change-detect deliberately skips rows whose `edition_key`/`serial` are unchanged. **`last_seen_at` is a content-change watermark, not a verification watermark.**
- **Lock freshness IS oversubscribed and was left alone, honestly labelled.** 1,385,681 of 1,623,424 TS rows never lock-checked; `lock-check-batch` stamped 46,383 rows in 7d (~6,626/day) vs ~232,000/day for a 7-day promise. That constant is already documented as a background target at the callsite and displayed-lock trust comes from the on-view refresh, so **no behaviour was changed** — an old `lock_checked_at` is a real but expected signal.
- **Fixed the metric, not the data — deliberately.** A blanket `last_seen_at` bump on cache-skip would be **~2.39M UPDATEs/day on a 2.05M-row / ~800MB table on the hot write path** — more than a full table rewrite per day in heap churn + WAL, to move a number already true at the grain that matters. **And the correct grain already existed and was already being written every run:** `wallet_backfill_state.last_scanned_at`, per wallet+collection, via `record_wallet_backfill_scan`. Ownership verification is a per-**wallet** event (the whole id set is enumerated atomically), so per-wallet is the right grain. **Zero new writes.**
- **Shipped:** `audit_20260725_wmc_freshness_metric_truth` — column comments on `last_seen_at` (explicitly "do NOT raise a staleness alarm off this column") and `lock_checked_at`, plus `check_wmc_ownership_freshness(p_max_age_days integer DEFAULT 7)`, set-returning, **0 rows = clean**. **Live proof: the truthful metric returns 4 rows — ONE wallet (`0x01be49cb0c...`) across 4 collections at 9.25 days — against the 1.61M-row alarm it replaces.** Code comment added at the `skip_cached` callsite in `app/api/wallet-backfill/route.ts` so the next reader cannot re-file it.
- **Revert:** `DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.check_wmc_ownership_freshness(integer); COMMENT ON COLUMN public.wallet_moments_cache.last_seen_at IS NULL; COMMENT ON COLUMN public.wallet_moments_cache.lock_checked_at IS NULL;` + `git revert <sha>` for the code comment.

**2. `evm-transfers-ingest` muted — it will flag forever otherwise.**

- Runs ~24x/day returning `{"message":"no_active_contracts"}` because the **Beezie/Base plane was retired 2026-07-13**. Its own watchlist notes already said "No product consumer — monitoring only", so `cron_silent` on it can never be actionable. `pipeline_cadence_watchlist.is_active` -> **false** (`audit_20260725_mute_evm_transfers_ingest_watchlist`). **4. Badge coverage — one gap closed, one proven NOT portable.**

- **All Day: 584 of 6,190 editions have no `badge_editions` row — confirmed exactly (90.57% coverage).** **Top Shot's mechanism is NOT portable, and that is the finding.** Top Shot self-heals via a GHA catalog sweep (`badge-sync?mode=catalog`), but All Day badges come from the Dapper Atlas `EditionService`, which **WAF-blocks Vercel egress AND datacenter runners** — that is exactly why the All Day writer runs on a residential runner (`scripts/ingest-allday-badges.mjs`). A GHA cron would be blocked at the source. **Also: the gap is not growing.** All 584 were created in a single batch on **2026-04-12** and none since; 352 are ULTIMATE tier; only 225 have any sale and 211 any owner. **Deliberately did NOT backfill** — writing `badge_editions` rows with no real Atlas badge data would be exactly the fabricated-data class killed in the pack-EV P0 above. **No change shipped; recorded as a residential-runner coverage limit.**
- **Golazos badge feed: the reported blocker was re-checked and was WRONG, so it is now WIRED.** The report said edition resolution was blocked (610/610 `cached_listings_v2` rows NULL `edition_id`) and hoped today's ownership fix would unblock it. **It did not:** all **9,494** Golazos wmc rows have **NULL `edition_key`**, so `flow_id -> wmc -> editions.external_id` resolves **0 of 610** (272 of 610 flow_ids *are* now in wmc — the missing bridge is `edition_key`, not ownership). **But a different bridge works and always did:** `sales.nft_id -> sales.edition_id` resolves **426 of 610, 0 ambiguous**, 184 unresolvable (never-traded NFTs have no sales row by definition). **So the blocker was resolution LOGIC, not data.**
- **Shipped the Golazos equivalent of `allday-badge-low-ask-refresh`:** `resolve_golazos_listing_edition_ids()` (NULL-only, **ambiguity-safe** — writes only when exactly one distinct `edition_id` exists, so a mis-keyed NFT stays NULL rather than being guessed), the `golazos_edition_floor_ask` view (exact mirror of `allday_edition_floor_ask`, `security_invoker=on`, **no anon grant**), `refresh_golazos_badge_low_ask()` (port of the All Day function **plus** a self-heal call to the resolver each tick, which the All Day path gets for free), and `cron.job rpc-golazos-badge-low-ask-refresh` at `10,40 * * * *` (offset off All Day's `*/30`).
- **Live proof:** `edition_id` **0 -> 426**; the floor-ask view **0 -> 135 editions**; first tick logged `updated: 34, cleared: 70`; `badge_editions` newest row moved **2026-07-21 -> 2026-07-25 20:33 UTC** (feed no longer frozen). **Note the honest direction of `low_ask`: 116/218 -> 67/218.** That is a *correction*, not a regression — **70 of the old 116 were stale asks for editions with no live listing**, held over from the frozen 07-21 snapshot. All 67 now correspond to a live ask. **`highest_offer` remains 0/218** — no Golazos offer writer exists; out of scope here.
- **Deliberately did NOT invent badge rows:** 68 of the 135 floor-ask editions have no `badge_editions` row, because **no Golazos badge-classification writer exists at all**. That is the remaining Golazos gap and is left open rather than papered over.
- **Revert:** `SELECT cron.unschedule('rpc-golazos-badge-low-ask-refresh'); DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.refresh_golazos_badge_low_ask(); DROP VIEW IF EXISTS public.golazos_edition_floor_ask; DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.resolve_golazos_listing_edition_ids(); UPDATE public.badge_editions SET low_ask = NULL WHERE collection_id = '06248cc4-b85f-47cd-af67-1855d14acd75';` (to undo the 426 `edition_id` writes: `UPDATE public.cached_listings_v2 SET edition_id = NULL WHERE collection_id = '06248cc4-b85f-47cd-af67-1855d14acd75';` — safe, that column was 100% NULL for Golazos before today).
- Migrations: `audit_20260725_golazos_listing_edition_resolver`, `..._fix_uuid_agg`, `audit_20260725_refresh_golazos_badge_low_ask`, `audit_20260725_cron_golazos_badge_low_ask_refresh`.
- **Trap worth keeping:** the resolver's first version used `min(sa.edition_id)` on a **uuid** column — there is no `min(uuid)` in Postgres, so it raised `42883` and resolved 0 rows. **This is the second time today** (`audit_20260725_resolve_sales_ingest_unresolved_fix_uuid_agg` was the first). Use `(array_agg(DISTINCT col))[1]` + `count(DISTINCT col)` in one LATERAL — it gives the candidate *and* the ambiguity count in a single pass.

### 2026-07-25 (Claude Code, interactive) — live-audit QA: the `/moment` soft-404 root-caused to the Suspense shell, the guessable Pinnacle moment URL, meta-description trim; `% LISTED` + `TOP OWNERS` investigated (correct as-is)

Five items off a live rippackscity.com audit: three shipped, two closed as investigate-only after the reported symptom turned out to be honest behaviour. Full suite green (841 files / 6208 tests); `tsc --noEmit` 11 errors, all pre-existing in `__tests__/`, 0 in touched files.

- **FIX 1 (P2) — soft-404 on `/moment/<id>`, root-caused to `loading.tsx`, not to the page.** The audit reported `/disney-pinnacle/moment/GEN-DPIN-SIMB-S0` landing on a **200 with "Moment Not Found"**. Live re-check found the described redirect only happens for a signed-in user — anonymously that URL **307'd to `/login`**, so a crawler never even reached the soft-404. Three distinct defects, fixed separately:
  - **The soft-404 is mechanical and class-wide.** `app/moment/[id]/` ships a `loading.tsx`, so Next wraps the page in an implicit `<Suspense>`, flushes the document shell + fallback immediately, and streams the page after. By the time the page's own `notFound()` fires the status line is already out as 200; the 404 arrives as a streamed `NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;404` row. Verified against **Next 16.2.9** with a four-variant probe app, unresolvable id in each: `loading.tsx` + `notFound()` in the page → **200**; + `notFound()` in `generateMetadata` → **200** (metadata streams too, so the common "throw in generateMetadata" advice does NOT work here); + `notFound()` in a segment **`layout.tsx`** → **404**; no `loading.tsx` → **404**. A layout is part of the shell so Next must await it before the first flush. Shipped the layout variant — it keeps the navigation skeleton. New [app/moment/[id]/layout.tsx](../../app/moment/%5Bid%5D/layout.tsx) gates on `resolve_moment_id`, deliberately **not** `get_moment_detail`: it is the same resolver `get_moment_detail` calls internally, so a 404 here is a strict subset of what the page already 404'd on and cannot invent a false 404, and it returns 0/1 rows instead of a large jsonb. It **fails OPEN** on RPC error so a transient blip can't deindex a real moment. Also wrapped `fetchDetail` in React `cache()` — `generateMetadata` and the page were each firing `get_moment_detail`, so the request went from 2 heavy calls to 1 cheap + 1 heavy (net faster than before the gate).
  - **The guessable URL now resolves.** `GEN-DPIN-SIMB-S0` is a `pinnacle_catalog.render_id` (1 row) and **not** a `pinnacle_editions.id` (0 rows), which is exactly why only `/pinnacle/moment/*` — the surface that reads `pinnacle_catalog` — can render it. Added a `/disney-pinnacle/moment/:id` → `/pinnacle/moment/:id` 308 in [next.config.ts](../../next.config.ts). Direction is deliberate: `/pinnacle/moment/*` is the canonical surface (~2,412 sitemap URLs, `lib/sitemap-data.ts` segment 4, and the page self-canonicals there), so redirecting the other way would churn every indexed URL and contradict its own canonical tag — **those 2,412 stay untouched 200s**. No loop: `moment` is absent from both `/pinnacle/:page` allowlists. `next.config` redirects also run **before** the `proxy.ts` auth gate (verified live: `/pinnacle/overview` 308s cleanly rather than bouncing to `/login`), so anonymous crawlers get one hop to the rendered page.
  - **The `/login` bounce.** `moment` was the one entity segment missing from the public-entity allowlist in [proxy.ts](../../proxy.ts), so every `/<collection>/moment/<id>` 307'd anonymous traffic to `/login`. Added it. The route is a pure resolver that renders nothing and only forwards to `/moment/<id>` or `/<collection>/overview`, both already public — no new data exposure, just no bounce.
  - **NOT shipped, follow-up:** the identical soft-404 affects **5 more routes** — `edition`, `set`, `player`, `team`, `series` under `app/(collections)/[collection]/` — each of which ships part of the ~20.5K sitemap URLs and returns **200 on an unknown slug** (confirmed live: `/nba-top-shot/edition/bogus-xyz`, `/nba-top-shot/set/bogus-xyz`, `/nba-top-shot/player/bogus-xyz` all 200). The correlation is exact: every route with a `loading.tsx` soft-404s, every route without hard-404s (`/pinnacle/moment/BOGUS` and `/insights/not-a-real-board` both correctly 404). Left alone because the two fixes are a **trade-off call, not a bug fix**: deleting the 5 `loading.tsx` files is trivial and guaranteed, but drops the loading skeleton on the five highest-traffic SEO surfaces; the layout variant keeps it but needs a cheap existence resolver per entity type (5 new RPCs). Mechanism and probe results above are the hard part and are now settled.
  - **Reverts:** `git rm app/moment/[id]/layout.tsx`; drop the `/disney-pinnacle/moment/:id` block from `next.config.ts`; drop `|moment` from the entity regex in `proxy.ts`; unwrap the `cache(...)` around `fetchDetail` in `app/moment/[id]/page.tsx`.

- **FIX 2 (P3) — `% LISTED` em-dash on `/nba-top-shot/edition/262:8754`: INVESTIGATED, correct as-is, no code change.** The em-dash is honest, and it is **collection-wide, not edition-specific** — every NBA Top Shot edition page shows it. `get_edition_market_bundle`'s `active_listings` leg gates the Top Shot branch on `(SELECT max(ingested_at) FROM ts_listings) > now() - interval '6 hours'`; **`ts_listings` holds 1 row, last ingested 2026-05-15 — 71 days stale**, so the gate returns NULL and `page.tsx`'s `pctListed == null` renders `—`. The edition-id shape is a red herring: `262:8754` matches the branch's `^\d+:\d+(::\d+)?$` regex and `split_part` resolves `set_id=262/play_id=8754` fine (the sibling-parallel ladder for that id works, proving the path). The live `TOP SHOT ASK $7.00` beside it comes from a **different, fresh table** — `edition_offers.low_ask`, updated minutes ago — which is why the page reads inconsistent. Per the existing in-code comment ("a 0% listed off a dead feed would be a lie, not a datapoint") the em-dash is the correct output; **no percentage was fabricated**. Worth a ticket, not a frontend fix: `ts_listings` has no surviving writer (the Flowty GitHub-Actions lane is gone), while Top Shot listings *are* being ingested into `cached_listings` (no `edition_id`, ~100-row deal sample) and `topshot_active_listings` (has `edition_id` but scoped to high-value serial-board targets) — **neither can supply a complete per-edition count**, so wiring either in would produce a wrong percentage. ### 2026-07-25 (Claude Code, interactive, ~15:50 PT) — three defensive-correctness fixes: NULL-FMV fabrication (3 feeds + the board), a confidence chip that survived the 2026-07-11 removal, and real 404s on the five entity SEO routes

Audit-sourced, all three independent of any pending product decision — plus a fourth (FIX 4) found while verifying the first, which FIX 1 turns out to depend on. **All verified against the live site after Vercel reported READY**, not just from the diff: five entity routes curl'd good-slug-200 / bogus-slug-404, a 20-URL real-sitemap regression sweep across all five collections, an A/B of both sniper feeds against the immediately-preceding production deployment, and the shipped client chunk grepped for the deleted chip. `tsc --noEmit` **0 errors before and after** (pristine `main` was already clean this pass — the ~11 `__tests__` errors named in the brief had been cleared by cont. 36). ESLint delta on every touched file: **zero** new errors. New/updated tests all green.

**FIX 1 — a NULL FMV was being rendered as a fabricated number in four places, not the three the audit named.** Standing policy is that an em-dash is always correct where data is absent and a substituted number never is. Each site verified against current code first.
- `app/api/sniper-feed/route.ts` (Top Shot live leg, ~L1372): the ask-proxy fallback guards on `baseFmv < 1`, and **`null < 1` is `true` in JavaScript** — so an edition whose `fmv_usd` is NULL fell into the branch and got priced at `floor_price_usd * 0.90`. A *fabricated fair value for an edition that has none*. Now the row is dropped before the guard; a genuine near-zero FMV still takes the documented ask-proxy path (pinned both ways). `FmvRow.fmv` is typed `number | null` so the compiler enforces the null check at future call sites.
- `app/api/sniper-feed/route.ts` (All Day live leg, ~L1031): `fmvEntry?.fmv || askPrice` **substituted the ask for the FMV**, producing a fake 0% discount — and, when an `fmv_snapshots` row existed with a NULL `fmv_usd` (folded to 0 by `Number(x) || 0` upstream), it shipped that row labelled `confidenceSource: "fmv_snapshots"`. Missing FMV now excludes the listing. Note `||` vs `??`: a legitimate 0 is also not a usable fair value (nothing is "40% off" $0), so both are excluded.
- **Two siblings the audit did not name**, same class, found by grep: the All Day **RPC-fallback** path (~L950) and the Top Shot **RPC** path (~L1231) both emitted `baseFmv: Number(r.fmv_usd) || 0` → a literal **$0.00** fair value on the board. Both now filter on a shared `hasUsableFmv` predicate.
- `app/api/golazos-sniper-feed/route.ts` (~L94): emitted `baseFmv: 0` as the stand-in for unknown. Now emits **null**.
- **Consumer end** (`app/(collections)/[collection]/sniper/page.tsx`, the real path — the audit cited a non-existent `app/insights/sniper/page.tsx`): `(deal.aspUsd - deal.baseFmv) / deal.baseFmv` with `baseFmv` 0 returned **Infinity**, whose `Math.abs(diff) >= 0.1` is always true → a permanent spurious ↑ trend arrow. Replaced with `safeRatioDiff` (returns null for a zero/absent denominator) and all three FMV cells now go through `fmvDisplay`, which renders an em-dash rather than `$0.00`/`NaN`/`∞`. Both helpers live in `lib/sniper/helpers.ts` and are unit-tested.
- **Product impact — MEASURED, and smaller than I first wrote.** I initially recorded "the All Day board will show fewer rows". Then I A/B'd the live production deploy against the immediately-preceding one (`0a63da72`, still serving on its deployment URL) and the counts are **identical: PRE 200 / NEW 200, zero rows lost**, with 0 fabricated rows on either side. Reason: the live AD path is currently the **RPC fallback**, and `get_allday_sniper_deals(0,100000,'all','all','listed_desc',200)` returns 200 rows of which **200 have a positive `fmv_usd`** (checked in SQL), so the new filter drops nothing. My first request did return 0 — but so did the PRE deployment on the same minute; that was a transient upstream blip, not my change. The exclusion only bites on the **GQL live-pool** path, where **1,075 of 6,190 AD editions (17.4%)** have a NULL newest `fmv_usd` — those are exactly the rows that used to render `baseFmv == askPrice` while labelled `confidenceSource: "fmv_snapshots"`. Re-measure if the GQL pool comes back. `[sniper-feed] AD DONE: … fmv_hits=` logs the reach.
- **Tests:** `api-sniper-feed-compute.test.ts` (+2: NULL `fmv_usd` → row excluded and never `ask_proxy`/72/0; real near-zero FMV still takes ask_proxy — the over-correction guard), `api-sniper-feed-allday-compute.test.ts` (+2 new, 2 rewritten — the old "no FMV entry → ask-fallback, baseFmv 60" case **pinned the bug** and now asserts exclusion), `api-golazos-sniper-feed-deep.test.ts` (+2 new, 1 rewritten off `baseFmv === 0`), `sniper-helpers.test.ts` (+7 on `fmvDisplay`/`safeRatioDiff`, incl. the Infinity case).

It could not leak a low tier (the route gates to HIGH/MEDIUM) so it was policy-only, not a data leak. **FIX 3 — an unknown slug on `edition` / `set` / `player` / `team` / `series` answered HTTP 200 (soft-404); ~20,500 sitemap URLs sit on these five routes.** Mechanism was already settled and not re-derived: each segment ships a `loading.tsx`, which wraps the PAGE in an implicit `<Suspense>`, so Next flushes the shell and commits a **200 status line** before the page's `notFound()` runs. Applied the **layout variant** (keeps the skeleton), same as `app/moment/[id]` (`e835882c`).
- New `lib/entity-detail-gate.ts`: a React-`cache()`d `fetchEntityDetailRaw(kind, collectionId, slug)` plus `entityResolves`. Two safety properties, both unit-tested: (1) **strict subset** — the gate calls the *same* `get_<entity>_detail` RPC with the same args that the page itself 404s on, so it cannot invent a false 404; (2) **fails OPEN** on any RPC error or thrown exception, so a transient pool blip can never emit a 404 and deindex a real page.
- Five new `layout.tsx` files. Each also promotes the page's pre-existing pure 404 conditions (unknown collection slug; Top Shot UUID-fossil edition slugs; exhibition/all-star team slugs) from soft to real. Pinnacle edition URLs are skipped in the gate so the page's 308 to `/pinnacle/moment/<id>` still wins. A malformed percent-escape fails open (we cannot reproduce the page's key, so we do not guess).
- **Net faster, not slower:** all five pages' own `fetchDetail` now routes through the same cached fetch, so the layout gate + `generateMetadata` + the page render collapse into **one** detail RPC per request, where metadata + page already made two. `edition`/`set`/`series` additionally pick up `rpcWithRetry`'s connection-class backoff, which `player`/`team` already had.
- **Tests:** `__tests__/entity-detail-gate.test.ts` (15) — per-kind RPC+arg wiring, the four resolve-TRUE/FALSE shapes, both fail-open arms, and `decodeSlugOrNull` on a malformed escape.
- **Revert:** `rm app/(collections)/[collection]/{edition,set,player,team,series}/[slug]/layout.tsx lib/entity-detail-gate.ts __tests__/entity-detail-gate.test.ts && git checkout <this-sha>^ -- 'app/(collections)/[collection]/edition/[slug]/page.tsx' 'app/(collections)/[collection]/set/[slug]/page.tsx' 'app/(collections)/[collection]/player/[slug]/page.tsx' 'app/(collections)/[collection]/team/[slug]/page.tsx' 'app/(collections)/[collection]/series/[slug]/page.tsx'`. Deleting the five layouts alone restores the soft-404 without touching anything else.

**FIX 4 (not in the brief — found while measuring FIX 1, and it is what makes FIX 1 safe) — the All Day FMV map was silently truncated by the PostgREST 1000-row cap.** The map was built from a raw, **unbounded** `fmv_snapshots.eq(collection_id).order(computed_at DESC)` read, justified by a comment asserting the AD snapshot table was tiny (~341 rows). Now that a missing FMV **excludes** the row, the same truncation would have dropped most of the AD board on the GQL live-pool path. - Now reads **`fmv_current`** (DISTINCT ON (edition_id) latest, ≤1 row/edition — verified to agree exactly with the JS dedupe it replaces: 6,190 / 5,115 positive / 1,075 null), paged with **`.range()`** (6,190 > 1,000), with `.gt("fmv_usd", 0)` filtering unusable FMVs server-side so a map MISS and an unusable FMV are one condition for `buildDeal`.
- **This is the class `__tests__/invariants-postgrest-cap.test.ts` exists to prevent** (documented there as having bitten prod at least six times). It slipped through because that guard's allowlist is **per-file**, and `app/api/sniper-feed/route.ts` was already listed for its *other*, genuinely `.in()`-bounded Top Shot read. Added an explicit regression pin to that guard (`fmv_current` + `.range()` present, stale premise absent) — the per-file allowlist granularity is the underlying weakness and is worth a follow-up.

### 2026-07-26 (Claude Code, interactive) — test-coverage pass (cont. 47): the four deferred-`after()` admin/cron bodies that had never actually run

Test-only, behavior-preserving. **No product code changed.** Suite 866 files / 6,637 tests, 0 failures; `tsc --noEmit` 0 errors.

Four small routes share one shape — sync auth, then a deferred `after()` body — and therefore one blind spot: **their existing tests all stopped at the 401/202, so the work itself had never run.** That is exactly the silent-run class the 2026-06-10/06-11 dark-run incidents came from: the route answers 202, the cron entry stays enabled, and nothing ever happened. All four now drive the deferred body.

- **`admin/cron/refresh-error-triage` 33.3% → 100% statements.** Because the HTTP response is now always 202, the `pipeline_runs` row **is** the success signal — so it must be written on every outcome. Pinned on the clean path, on a returned RPC error, and on an RPC *throw* (each producing `ok:false` + the message), plus the case where `log_pipeline_run` itself throws and must not reject the deferred body.

### 2026-07-26 (Claude Code, interactive) — the wallet-lookup wedge moved to the surfaces that actually get traffic, and made measurable for the first time

The top-of-funnel wedge ("paste a wallet, see what you own") was reachable only from the LEAST-visited surface, and two thirds of the boxes that did exist emitted no event at all. Both halves are fixed. Evidence-driven throughout; the placement decision was changed mid-pass by the data.

**What the measurement actually said (funnel_events, 30d, read at the start of the pass).** The brief's premise — home 20/7d vs collection_view 131/7d vs insights_view 40/7d — held. But the obvious fix (put the box on the collection landing page) was a trap. Broken down by tab, `/<c>/overview` is only **8.8%** of `collection_view`: `edition/*` **51.4%**, `pack/*` **15.5%**, `/collection` **14.2%**, overview 8.8%, rest ~10%. The same shape holds on insights — the `/insights` hub is only ~18% of `insights_view` (first-mint 44, squeeze 14, pack-sniper 10, … across ~30 boards). **A page-level block on either landing page would have reached under 10% of the traffic it was meant to catch.** So the entry point went in the two LAYOUTS, mounted once each, covering 100% of both subtrees.

**The second, larger finding: the wedge was already on the high-traffic surfaces — it just wasn't instrumented.** `wallet_paste` reading 24 lifetime / 2 in 7d was NOT purely a placement problem. There were **four** hand-rolled copies of the same input (`HomePageMarketing`'s private `WalletSearch`, `InsightsWalletSearch`, `AccountValueSearch`, and a block on `/<c>/overview`) and **only the home one called `trackFunnelEvent`**. Every lookup on `/insights` and `/insights/account-value` — the #2 surface by traffic — has been invisible for its entire life. The `/overview` copy was worse than invisible: it pushed anon visitors at the **auth-gated `/dashboard`**, so the #1 CTA on a public landing page bounced to `/login`. All four are now one component.

- **NEW `components/WalletSearch.tsx`** — the canonical input, factored out of `HomePageMarketing`'s private copy. Same behaviour, same styling: `variant="hero"` and `variant="inline"` reproduce the two looks that already shipped 1:1, so this is a placement+instrumentation change, not a restyle. `destination` is constrained to the two ANON-SAFE public routes (`/share/<wallet>`, `/insights/tc-report?wallet=`) — never an auth-gated one.
- **NEW `components/WalletSearchBand.tsx`** — the compact layout-level placement. One row: a line of copy + the 52px input (stacks at ≤640px; ~112px on a 390px viewport). The old `/overview` hero's 32px decorative glyph and 32px padding are deliberately NOT reproduced. **§3 compliance:** it carries no logo, nav, breadcrumb, collection switcher, tab bar or ticker — it is the first CONTENT block inside the existing `<main>`, sharing that `<main>`'s max-width and padding, so it is not a second header. Renders in the SSR pass (crawlable + verifiable in delivered HTML) and removes itself one tick after hydration if a wallet is already known, so a returning collector is never nagged. Self-suppresses on `/insights`, `/insights/account-value`, `/insights/tc-report`, `/insights/squeeze-check` — the routes that already ARE the lookup.
- **Mounted in 3 layouts:** `app/(collections)/[collection]/layout.tsx`, `app/(collections)/disney-pinnacle/layout.tsx` (the bespoke Pinnacle layout serves its collection+sniper tabs from their own page dirs and would otherwise silently lose the wedge), and `app/insights/layout.tsx` (wrapped in a 1180px column matching `.rpc-ins-hero`).
- **`/<c>/overview`'s forked block DELETED, not patched** — the layout band supersedes it and a second box would be a duplicate. Its now-dead `WALLET_HINTS` / `ctaSubtitle` / `hasWallet` locals went with it.

**Instrumentation.** No new `event_type` and **no migration required**. `wallet_paste` was already emitted on SUBMIT, not on paste — read the emitter, the semantics already match "lookup submitted", so reusing it keeps the historical series comparable instead of splitting it. What changed is that every placement now emits it, under a **distinct `surface`** so the next read can attribute WHICH placement worked rather than just "more pastes": `home` (unchanged) · **`collection_layout`** · **`insights_layout`** · **`insights_hub`** · **`insights_account_value`**. This follows the existing convention — explicit strings for interaction events, pathname for the `perPath` view events.

**Attribution (`lib/track-funnel.ts`).** 990 of 1,086 `funnel_events` rows had a null/empty `referrer` and **zero** carried a `utm_*`, so nothing promoted anywhere would have been attributable. Attribution is now resolved **once per session** (the first event of a session IS the landing hit) and stamped on every later event, because `document.referrer` degrades to our own origin the moment a visitor navigates internally — which is the actual reason `/insights` arrivals all looked referrer-less. Folded into the EXISTING `referrer` column in a bounded documented format (`utm_source=…&utm_medium=…&utm_campaign=…&ref=https://host/path`, capped at the column's own 512 limit), so **no schema change ships**. `components/FunnelTracker.tsx` no longer passes the live `document.referrer`, which was overwriting the landing attribution with our own origin. **Privacy:** our own campaign params + the referring page only; utm values stripped to `[A-Za-z0-9._~-]` and capped at 64; the referrer reduced to **origin+pathname** so a referring URL's query string (which we do not control and which can carry personal data) is never stored; same-origin referrers dropped. No PII, nothing user-identifying, no user data placed in a URL.

**Verification.** `npx tsc --noEmit` **0 errors on pristine `origin/main` before editing and 0 after**. ESLint on every touched file: **0 errors** (one pre-existing `COLLECTION_TICKER` unused warning on the overview page, present at `origin/main` too, left alone). `next build` compiled + typechecked clean. Tests: **29 new/updated across 3 files**, and the full component+funnel suite **49 files / 248 tests PASS**. New `__tests__/component-WalletSearchBand.test.tsx` (13) pins the things that break the MEASUREMENT silently rather than the render — a distinct surface per placement, the two surfaces not colliding, `wallet_paste` firing at all, the band being in the FIRST render pass, the `/dashboard` regression guard, ≥44px touch target (§9), and no literal hex / font strings (§0). New `__tests__/component-WalletSearch-bindings.test.tsx` (6) pins each binding's surface + public destination and that the paste is emitted BEFORE navigation. `__tests__/track-funnel.test.ts` +5 on the attribution (utm capture, survival across internal navigation, same-origin drop, hostile-utm sanitising, explicit-referrer override).

**Revert paths (three, cheapest first).**
1. **Kill switch, no code change:** set `NEXT_PUBLIC_WALLET_BAND=off` in Vercel production and redeploy — both layout placements return `null`. Nothing else is affected (the home hero, `/insights` hub box and account-value box keep working, still instrumented).
2. **Placement only:** delete the four `<WalletSearchBand …/>` lines (one in each of the three layouts, plus the insights wrapper `<div>`). The unfork + instrumentation + attribution all survive.
3. **Everything:** `git revert <code-sha>`. To restore just the old `/overview` block: `git checkout <code-sha>^ -- 'app/(collections)/[collection]/overview/page.tsx'`.

**Migration left for review — NOT applied, and NOT needed for this to work.** The attribution above deliberately reuses `referrer`. If a future pass wants first-class UTM columns for cheap `GROUP BY`, this is the exact DDL; the shipped code needs no change to keep working without it, and would need a small emitter edit to populate the new columns:
```sql
-- audit_2026MMDD_funnel_events_utm_columns (REVIEW ONLY — not applied 2026-07-26)
alter table public.funnel_events
  add column if not exists utm_source   text,
  add column if not exists utm_medium   text,
  add column if not exists utm_campaign text,
  add column if not exists referrer_host text;
-- Mirror the existing anon-INSERT RLS length discipline (see the referrer cap):
alter table public.funnel_events
  add constraint funnel_events_utm_len check (
    coalesce(length(utm_source),0)   <= 64 and
    coalesce(length(utm_medium),0)   <= 64 and
    coalesce(length(utm_campaign),0) <= 64 and
    coalesce(length(referrer_host),0) <= 253
  );
create index if not exists funnel_events_utm_source_idx
  on public.funnel_events (utm_source) where utm_source is not null;
-- Revert: drop the constraint, the index, then the four columns.
```

**Target metric.** `wallet_paste` per week, split by `surface`. Baseline to beat: **2 in the trailing 7 days, 24 lifetime, all from `surface='home'`**. The read that matters is whether `collection_layout` + `insights_layout` + `insights_hub` together exceed `home` — that is the whole thesis, and it is now answerable. Note the 20-registered-users / 0-WAU demand problem is untouched by this; this makes the wedge reachable and measurable, it does not create traffic.

### 2026-07-26 (Claude Code, interactive) — SHIPPED (DB index, live): killed the cold-scan behind the `get_team_detail` connection-pool-timeout (Sentry JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-1Y)

**Additive index, no code / no function change, no deploy.** Chasing the 3 unresolved Sentry errors (`GET /[collection]/team/[slug]` + `/player/[slug]` "Timed out acquiring connection from connection pool", 4/4/1 events / 5–6 days). Profiled both RPCs: they're fast warm (LeBron 23 ms, Knicks 110 ms) and already well-indexed, so this is NOT a `get_team_activity`-style 28 s algorithmic stall — the pool-acquire timeout is a saturation symptom, worsened by one cold cost center in `get_team_detail`.

- **Root cause:** the team-variant lookup (`SELECT array_agg(DISTINCT team_name) … WHERE regexp_replace(lower(trim(team_name)),'[^a-z0-9]+','-','g') = $slug`) had no matching index — the slug is a functional expression — so it index-only-scanned the WHOLE collection's editions. New York Knicks: 18,121 rows examined (17,471 removed by the regexp filter), **8,186 heap fetches / 6,703 buffers**. Cold, that page-read amplification balloons to seconds and holds the pooled connection the whole time. `players` already had the exact mirror index (`idx_players_collection_name_slug`) — which is why `get_player_detail`'s own slug lookup was already a seek (its twin error is pure saturation collateral); `editions` was just missing the twin.
- **Fix:** `idx_editions_collection_team_slug` on `editions (collection_id, (regexp_replace(lower(trim(team_name)),'[^a-z0-9]+','-','g'))) WHERE team_name IS NOT NULL` — functional btree on the same immutable expression, partial to match the sibling `idx_editions_collection_team`. Built **CONCURRENTLY** via `execute_sql` (valid+ready verified), parity migration `20260726170000_audit_20260726_editions_collection_team_slug_index.sql` (plain `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` for history).
- **Measured (Knicks):** variant lookup **60.4 ms → 3.5 ms** (buffers **6,703 → 501**); full `get_team_detail` **110 ms → 63 ms** warm, output **byte-identical** (edition_count 650 / player_count 64 / fmv_total 42668.28 / sales_30d 3827 unchanged across Knicks·Lakers·Thunder). Function body untouched → results cannot change (an index is never chosen when slower); end-to-end strictly ≥ as good. Deliberately did NOT touch the remaining cold costs (per-edition FMV lateral — already indexed + FMV-adjacent; sales-30d join — already on its tuned partition index).
- **REVERT:** `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.idx_editions_collection_team_slug;` (+ `git revert <sha>` for the parity file).

- **SHIPPED (1/4) — `lib/analytics/rpc-with-retry.ts`: stop retrying SQLSTATE 57014.** `isTransient()` had no 57014 case, so it fell through to the message heuristic `msg.includes("timeout")` — and Postgres' 57014 text is *"canceling statement due to statement timeout"*, which **contains that substring**. Every statement timeout was retried 3x. A statement that blew its ceiling blows it again, so the retry is pure amplification: 272 `[edition] offers` timeouts/24h × 3 attempts × 8 s = **24 s of DB work each instead of 8 s**, on the surface that is 51.4% of collection page views, on an IOPS-bound instance. `53300`/`57P01` stay transient (pool problems, not statement problems). New `NEVER_RETRY_CODES` set checked BEFORE the heuristics, plus a SQLSTATE-less message guard. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **SHIPPED (2/4) — three GHA cron collisions staggered (schedule-only, no behavior change).** `topshot-listing-cache.yml` `5,25,45`→**`15,35,55`**; `topshot-active-listings-ingest.yml` `13 */3`→**`29 */3`**; `snapshot-institutional-wallets-backstop.yml` `7 7`→**`29 7`**. `docs/operations/cron-schedule.md` updated to match. **CORRECTION to the handoff:** its "11/31/51 are free" was a **GHA-only** enumeration — building the real cross-scheduler map (cron-job.org 64 + edge fns 12 + workers 3 + GHA 16) shows `11,31,51` carries the **Golazos sales indexer** (10 jobs) and `16,36,56` carries the **AllDay sales indexer** (8). `15,35,55` (6) is the lightest trio legal under the doc's own rule banning minutes 0/1/20/21/40/41. - **SHIPPED (3/4) — All Day resolver: 4 independent defects** (`allday-resolve-unmapped` + `-tail` + `lib/chains/flow/allday-edition-onchain.ts`). Live telemetry confirmed every claim and then some: 24h = 5,700 attempts, 196 resolved (**all** via one leg), **`resolved_via_scan` 0**, **`onchain_err` 0**, **24,284 Flow REST range-requests for zero scan resolutions**; the tail route logged **`ok: true` on 7 runs that resolved and promoted literally nothing**.
  - **(a) The tripwire was unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION.** It required `errs >= attempted/2`, but `onchain_err` counts only *thrown* errors — a nil borrow increments `onchain_nil`. With `onchain_err` = 0 on all 95 runs it could only fire if Flow itself was down. Added clause (b), a productivity floor (`attempted >= 20 && resolved === 0 && promoted === 0`), guarded on `promoted` so a Leg-A-only tick still counts healthy.
  - **(b) One bad stored address suppressed the leg that works.** `buyer_address` = `0xe4cf4bdc1751c65d` — the **AllDay contract**, not a wallet — is the **largest single value in the backlog (4,816 open rows) and the only one still arriving today**. It isn't in `EXCLUDED_ADDRESSES`, so `buyers` was non-empty and the `buyers.length === 0` gate blocked `decodeV1SaleTx` entirely — the leg that produced **196 of 196** resolutions. Contract address excluded; decode now runs whenever the borrow produced no edition, not only when there was no buyer at all.
  - **(c) The scan is structurally dead here.** Gated on `buyers.length > 0` and instrumented (`scan_ran` / `scan_new_holders_tried` / `scan_no_new_holder`) so keep-or-delete is decided from data. A new **non-fatal** `scan_ineffective` flag surfaces the waste **without** flipping `ok=false` — deliberately *not* the handoff's third clause, which had no productivity guard and would have reddened every run (~221 chunks each) even while the buyer leg resolved normally.
  - **(d) Latent swallow fixed.** `scanAllDayDepositsForNft` did `if (res.ok) blocks = ...` inside a bare `catch {}`; a `/v1/events` 403/429/5xx returned `[]` and counted as `onchain_nil` ("buyer moved") instead of `onchain_err`. New `onError` callback.

Two honest caveats, neither a defect: (i) `buyer_excluded: 0` is CORRECT — all 19 contract-address rows in the freshest-400 window are already in `nft_edition_map`, so `alreadyMapped` filters them before the on-chain slate; the contract-address class spans Feb→today and will exercise the exclusion as the resolver works deeper and on new arrivals. ### 2026-07-26 (Cowork, interactive) — Candy / Magic Eden ingest hardening: dead-letter for stranded sales, bidder cap 40->250 (offer deactivation had been frozen ~42h), an empty-feed guard that could otherwise have wiped the whole ask book, honest editions metrics

Prompted by a review of "are we tracking Candy secondary effectively" (project doc `claude/candy-ingest-review-2026-07-26.md`). All four Candy pipelines were green; every defect below was silent under `ok=true`. Code + 2 DB objects; no pricing/FMV logic touched, no public surface touched (`CANDY_MLB_PUBLIC` still false).

- **Stranded sales -> dead letter.** `candy-sales-indexer` stops at the first ME activity <= `max(sold_at)`, so a sale it SEES but cannot write (DAS throw, unresolvable serial, edition not yet ingested, no SOL rate, asset-budget exhausted) is only re-offered while it is still the newest thing — the next successful write steps the cursor over it and it is gone. Measured over the first 25 runs: **359 found vs 322 written = 37 skipped**, with no dead-letter and no signal. Now parked in new `public.candy_sales_unresolved` via SECDEF `candy_park_unresolved_sale()` (attempts++ on re-park) and drained oldest-first each tick (`DRAIN_LIMIT` 60, `MAX_PARK_ATTEMPTS` 25) with whatever asset budget the live walk left. A drained row keeps its original `sold_at`, so recovery can never move the cursor. A 23505 on drain closes the row `duplicate_tx_hash` (`sales` dedups on `transaction_hash` alone, so a second item under one ME signature can never land). New extras: `parked`, `drain_attempted`, `drain_resolved`, `unresolved_open`, `activities_seen`, `me_key_present`. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` + `DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.candy_park_unresolved_sale(text,text,timestamptz,numeric,text,text,text); DROP TABLE IF EXISTS public.candy_sales_unresolved;` (migrations `audit_20260726_candy_sales_unresolved_deadletter` + `audit_20260726_candy_park_unresolved_sale_fn`; table RLS on, anon/authenticated revoked, fn revoked from PUBLIC too — verified `has_*_privilege` false).
- **Offer sweep un-truncated: `MAX_BIDDERS` 40 -> 250.** `bidders_discovered` crossed 40 on 2026-07-25 06:50Z and reached 60, so every tick since logged `bidders_truncated: true` — and because step 5 correctly refuses to deactivate on a partial sweep, **the deactivation pass had not run for ~42h**: 6 of 17 `is_active` offers were last seen 07-25 00:50Z, i.e. `candy_best_offers` / `candy_offer_spread_board` could quote a cancelled bid. The failure mode was stale-LIVE, never false-dead. A truncated tick now also logs **ok=false** so the freeze cannot hide behind a healthy `offers_upserted`. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **Empty-feed guard on the listings sweep (latent mass-deactivation).** An empty first page set `sweep_complete=true`, so a single degraded ME response would have marked the **entire standing book** dead in one tick (420 asks) and emptied `candy_listing_floor` / `candy_deals_board` / `candy_offer_spread_board` until ME recovered. Reachable: ME's public arms for this symbol serve degraded answers (its `/stats` arm echoes `listedCount: 0` for ANY symbol). Now: 0 raw rows while active asks exist => sweep treated as incomplete, deactivation suppressed, `ok=false`. Expiry-based deactivation still runs. New extras `raw_listings_seen`, `active_before`, `me_key_present`. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **`candy-sales-indexer` empty activities feed => ok=false.** Previously `found=0, written=0, ok=true` — the silent-degradation shape, on the pipeline that feeds the only Candy price signal. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **Editions metrics renamed to what they measure.** `editions_written: 3108` was upsert ROWS TOUCHED across DAS page-chunks against a **125-edition** catalog. Now `edition_rows_touched` / `serial_rows_touched` plus true `editions_distinct` / `serials_distinct`. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **Tests:** +10 (4 sales, 2 listings, 2 offers, 2 editions assertions rewritten); **8 of them proven to fail against the pre-fix routes** by stashing each route and re-running. `__tests__/helpers/route-harness.ts` fixture type widened to carry `count` (needed by any `{ count: "exact", head: true }` read). `tsc --noEmit` clean; full suite **891 files / 7,007 tests, 0 failures**.
- **Measured but NOT changed (needs a decision):** ME reports 4,982 collection supply against our 7,251 circulating serials (treasury `BhA2Bfd8...` holds 18,124 of 25,375; no second treasury wallet exists, so our count is sound). Until that is reconciled, ME collection-feed volume cannot be claimed as the whole Candy secondary market. Pipeline severities left at `info`/`medium` per the go-live doc — raising `candy-sales-indexer` to `high` rides the launch flip, not this.

### 2026-07-27 (Claude Code, interactive) — bug fix: the 23505 batch-insert data-loss bug in 3 backfill scripts + guarded the superseded classify-acquisitions writer (resolves the 07-26 documented drift items)

Fixes the real drift items the 07-26 scripts audit had DOCUMENTED-but-not-edited (all three scripts confirmed dead one-offs — referenced by no `package.json`/workflow/scheduler). Code-only, no prod DB mutation, no migration; the scripts aren't imported by any test so verification is `node --check` + project `tsc` (both clean) + matching the canonical, tested row-by-row pattern from `app/api/sales-indexer/route.ts`.
- **23505 co-batch data loss fixed in 3 `sales` writers.** A batch `.insert()` is all-or-nothing: one duplicate `transaction_hash` (23505) fails the whole statement and writes NONE of it, so counting the batch as skipped silently drops every co-batched NEW sale (permanently, since the cursor still advances). `scripts/flow-backfill.ts` (its comment even claimed a `ignoreDuplicates` it never used) and `scripts/cryptoslam-scrape.ts` never retried; `scripts/sales-backfill.mjs` was **inverted** — it retried row-by-row on NON-23505 errors and counted the whole batch `duped` on 23505, exactly backwards. All three now retry row-by-row on any batch error so real dups skip individually while new rows land.
- **`scripts/classify-acquisitions.mjs` — superseded-WRITE guard.** It's superseded by `/api/bulk-classify` and has two cost-basis-corrupting defects (reads getMintedMoment `price` = current/listing price instead of `lastPurchasePrice` = price paid; upserts synthetic `classifier_<id>` rows instead of resolving the existing `unknown` row). Rather than a half-fix I can't verify, it now REFUSES a real write unless `--run-superseded` is passed; `--dry-run` inspection (writes nothing) stays available. ### 2026-07-27 (Claude Code, interactive) — CI FIX: `main` was RED (db-tests) on a midnight-boundary flake in a DB-invariant SQL test

Test-only, no product/DB change. Found via a proactive CI check: the `db-tests` job (only that one; typecheck/unit/component/cadence/ledger all green) was failing on every run since ~00:xx UTC — `get_edition_fmv_history.sql` asserted a default-30d window returns **2** daily points but got **3**. **Root cause:** the fixture used `now() - interval '2 hours'` for a "today" snapshot; CI ran at **00:58 UTC**, so `now() - 2h` = 22:58 the PREVIOUS day → a separate `DATE()` bucket → 3 buckets instead of 2. A pure date-boundary flake (the function is correct), latent since the test was added and tripped whenever CI runs in the first ~2h of a UTC day. **Fix:** anchor both "today" snapshots to `date_trunc('day', now()) + interval '1h'/'2h'` so they are guaranteed the SAME calendar day regardless of run time (the 10d/100d points already use full-day offsets, no boundary risk). Verified locally against a throwaway `postgres:16`: the full suite is **22/22 PASS** (was 1 FAIL), and `db-invariants-drift-guard` is 22/22 (only fixture lines changed — the verbatim function DDL is untouched). **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.

### 2026-07-27 (Cowork, interactive) — LIVE INCIDENT + FIX: a degraded Magic Eden response wiped 419 of 426 Candy asks in one tick; the zero-only guard was not enough, ratio guard shipped to BOTH sweeps

**Caught in the act while verifying the same day's work.** The `candy-listings-indexer` tick at **00:35Z** received **7 listings** from Magic Eden against a **426-ask** book and, because 7 is not 0, my hours-old empty-feed guard did not fire: it treated the sweep as complete and **deactivated 419 standing asks**. `candy_listing_floor` collapsed 114 editions → **7 rows**, `candy_deals_board` → **3**, `candy_offer_spread_board` → **11**.

**Proven upstream, not real, from the blockchain — not from Magic Eden's own feed.** An 80-transaction on-chain sweep of the collection over the same window (23:47Z → 02:04Z) shows the whole collection did **6 `CoreCancelSell` (delists) and 8 sales**. A 419-ask book collapse would need ~400 delists. The book did not move; the feed did. (Independent corroboration: the ME collection PAGE read 409 listed at ~23:40Z, and a sandbox fetch of `/listings?limit=100` returned 15 rows — this endpoint demonstrably serves truncated answers.)

- **Fix (both sweeps, symmetric):** guard on the RATIO, not on zero. A sweep that returns `< 50%` of the book already held (once that book is ≥ 20 rows) is treated as INCOMPLETE: deactivation is suppressed, rows that WERE returned still upsert, expiry-based deactivation still runs, and the run reports **ok=false** with the two counts in the message. Deliberately not self-clearing — a genuine >50% collapse keeps tripping it and stays visible, which is the right way round, because suppressing a deactivation is reversible and issuing a wrong one is not. Ported to `candy-offers-indexer` too (same shape is reachable there: every per-bidder fetch can "succeed" with a short answer). New metrics `active_before`, `active_offers_before`, `degraded_sweep`.
- **NO data repair issued, deliberately.** A healthy sweep re-upserts every live ask with `is_active=true`, so the book self-heals on the next good tick (03:35Z) — reactivating 419 rows by hand would also resurrect the handful that genuinely did die, and the surface is gated so nothing user-facing was affected. Verify at 03:35Z; repair by hand only if the feed is still degraded.
- **THE DURABLE LESSON:** I shipped the zero-case guard the same evening after reasoning that an empty response was the destructive case. The destructive case is a *partial* response, and partial is far more likely than empty. **When guarding a destructive sweep against a flaky upstream, never guard on the degenerate value — guard on the ratio to the state you already hold.**
- +3 tests (2 listings, 1 offers), each proven to fail against the pre-fix routes; one pre-existing offers fixture re-sequenced for the added count read. `tsc` clean; full suite **902 files / 7,123 tests, 0 failures**. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.

### 2026-07-27 (Cowork, interactive) — the ratio guard was ALSO not enough: Candy listing deactivation is now EVIDENCE-BASED, and the 419 falsely-killed asks are restored

Third and final iteration on the same incident, and the one that removes the class instead of narrowing it.

**Why the ratio guard failed.** It compares the sweep against "the book we already hold" — but after one bad tick, that number IS the damaged one. Verified live: the 03:35Z tick saw 22 listings against the (already-wrecked) 24-row book, sailed past a 50% ratio test, and reported a clean sweep. Meanwhile Magic Eden's `/listings` answers for this one collection over six hours were **420 → 7 → 22**, while its collection PAGE said 409 listed and the chain said the book barely moved. **That endpoint is not a census and must never be treated as one.**

- **Shipped: deactivation on POSITIVE EVIDENCE only.** The listings sweep now also walks the ACTIVITIES feed (2 × 500 rows — the reliable half of ME's API; `candy-sales-indexer` has walked it every 3h without a gap) and collects the mints with a listing-ENDING event: `delist`, `buyNow`, `buyNowFill`, `acceptBid`. Only those mints' asks are deactivated, plus anything past its own `expiry`. The "any row this sweep did not see is dead" rule is **deleted**, for cards and packs alike. A failed activities walk means no evidence, therefore no deactivation — never the other way round. A short listings answer is now merely fewer price refreshes, so it is reported as a metric (`feed_looks_truncated`, `activities_seen`, `listing_ending_mints`) rather than a failure. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **Shipped: the repair.** `audit_20260727_candy_listings_restore_false_deactivation` restored **407** of the 419 asks — every row the 21:38Z sweep last confirmed alive, minus the 7 whose token has since sold and 0 expired. Live after: active asks **428**, `candy_listing_floor` **7 → 112 editions**, `candy_deals_board` **3 → 53**, `candy_offer_spread_board` **11 → 109**. The restored PDAs are preserved in `public.audit_20260727_candy_listings_restored` (RLS on, anon revoked) and the revert is a one-line UPDATE against it.
- **THE DURABLE LESSON, in three versions because I needed all three:** (1) don't guard a destructive sweep on the degenerate value (empty) — partial is likelier than empty; (2) don't guard it on a ratio to your own state either — one bad tick poisons that baseline; (3) **only delete on positive evidence of deletion.** If the upstream cannot prove a thing is gone, it is not gone.
- **Checked the same class on the Flow side and deliberately did NOT change it.** `topshot/golazos/allday/ufc-listing-cache` all purge `cached_listings` rows older than the run start, guarded only by `upserted > 0` — the same degenerate-zero guard that just failed here. Measured before prescribing: over 3 days / 474 runs those routes wrote min **50**, avg **101**, max 122 rows with **zero** tiny or empty runs, i.e. Flowty's API is stable where ME's is not, and they feed ASK-side FMV. Queued as **CANDY-CLASS-PURGE-GUARD-FLOW-CACHES**, not shipped — a speculative edit to an FMV-feeding path is exactly the kind of change the standing rule says to hand off.
- +3 tests (delist/fill evidence deactivates; an unseen ask survives an empty feed; a failed activities walk deactivates nothing), each proven to fail against the pre-fix route; the 2 ratio-guard tests they replace were deleted. `tsc` clean; full suite **902 files / 7,122 tests, 0 failures**.

### 2026-07-27 (Cowork, interactive) — Candy pre-launch, part 3: the Deals board was advertising discounts the sales history contradicts. Median-sale publish guard shipped

The most serious thing found in the whole readiness pass, because Deals is the surface that tells a stranger *buy this, it is 45% under fair value*.

**The defect, measured at the top of the board:**

| edition | ask | FMV | advertised | sales | MEDIAN sale | truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bobby-witt-jr` | $4.58 | $8.31 | **44.9% off** | 4 (4.33 / 4.44 / … / 20.04) | **$4.44** | ask is ABOVE the median — **no discount at all** |
| `jordan-walker` | $5.00 | $10.49 | **52.3% off** | 3 (5.97 / 7.01 / 18.49) | **$7.01** | ~29% off |
| `junior-caminero-blue` | $135.68 | $255.50 | 46.9% off | **1** ($300.59) | $300.59 | rests entirely on one print |

On a 1–11 sale market a single high sale lifts the fitted FMV above every other trade, and the board converts that estimator noise into a headline "% off" aimed at someone's wallet. That is the fabricated-signal class this codebase refuses to ship, and it was pointed at the most actionable tab.

- **Shipped a PUBLISH guard, not a pricing change** (precedent: the troll-ask floor guard, the fabricated-EV publish guards): a listing is published as a deal only if it is below FMV **and** below the edition's median sale, when a median exists. `median_sale_usd`, `sales_count` and `discount_vs_median_pct` are exposed so the board shows its work. Live effect **47 → 40 rows**; `bobby-witt-jr` drops out; `jordan-walker` still appears but now also reads "28.7% below the median trade". FMV computation is untouched — this only changes what we are willing to CALL a deal. Prior definition captured in `audit_20260727_candy_deals_board_prior`; `security_invoker` and the anon revoke both verified after. Gotcha for the next person: `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` cannot insert a column mid-list (42P16) — append.
- **Client:** the Discount column is now **"vs FMV"** beside a new **"vs median sale"** column (hover shows the median and the sale count), the table sorts by the median-based figure by default, and the blurb explains the guard. It also loses another stale claim — *"FMV comes off just 1–2 sales"* and *"Empty until secondary listings open"* were both false.
- ⚠ **A rendered-DOM check on the Deals tab is OWED** (this sandbox cannot render). The change is one additive column plus a formatter in an existing DataTable, and `tsc` + the full suite are green, but the 390px mobile pass already owed for this board should cover this tab first.
- Also verified while here and NOT changed: the K=10 troll ceiling is healthy — median floor/FMV **1.20×**, 32 asks excluded across 28 editions. The one surviving 12.1× floor is NOT a leak: the ceiling is `10 × GREATEST(edition FMV, tier median FMV)`, and the tier-median arm deliberately protects thinly-priced editions from an absurdly low ceiling. The queued `K = 5` decision stands as Trevor's, with this measurement attached.

### 2026-07-27 (Claude Code, interactive) — SHIPPED (e): the ipfs-media proxy was streaming videos the edge cache SILENTLY REFUSES — every view an unamortised 16–23 MB (the Fast Data Transfer alert); + the 502 soft-fail was unreachable dead code

Route + component, one commit. **No migration, no DB.** Drains items 2 and 3 of [docs/handoff-2026-07-27-alert-triage.md](docs/handoff-2026-07-27-alert-triage.md); both handoff claims **re-verified live before coding**.

- **The leak.** `app/api/public/ipfs-media/[cid]/route.ts` set `s-maxage=31536000, immutable` and its header reasoned "the first request warms the Vercel edge and every subsequent load is a cached same-origin hit". True for images, **false for video** — the objects exceed Vercel's max cacheable response size and the route had **no size ceiling**, streaming `upstream.body` at any length. Measured on prod, same URL 3×: **4.03 MB image/png → MISS, HIT, HIT** vs **16.75 MB mp4 → MISS, MISS, MISS** and **23.27 MB mp4 → MISS, MISS, MISS**, with `s-maxage` **stripped** on the oversize responses. So every video view cost a full 16–23 MB of Fast Data Transfer forever, with zero amortisation. Blast radius **10,786 editions** carry an IPFS video URL (`nba_top_shot` 10,270 + `ufc_strike` 516; AllDay/Golazos/Candy 0). Fix: read `content-length` and **302 to the upstream gateway above 8 MB** (between the largest size proven to cache and the smallest proven not to), cancelling our own body so the bytes never transit the function. CSP-safe — `proxy.ts` already allows `https://ipfs.io` in **both** `img-src` and `media-src` (verified). SSRF-safe — `CID_RE` validates before the redirect target is built. A missing/chunked `content-length` falls through to the old streaming path rather than guessing.
- **The amplifier.** `components/MomentHeroMedia.tsx` was the **only** autoplaying `<video>` in the app without `preload="none"` — every sibling clip surface (`TrophySlab`, `EditionsGridPaginated`, `MomentMedia`, the profile trophy tiles) is hover-mounted and/or `preload="none"` (all four audited). So every `/moment/[id]` render pulled the entire clip whether or not anyone watched. Added `preload="none"`; the `poster` (which DOES cache) still paints immediately, so a real viewer sees no change.
- **The 504s (item 3).** `AbortSignal.timeout(25_000)` sat at **exactly** the platform's own initial-response cutoff, so the platform always won (`504 [error/serverless-middleware] … did not return an initial response within 25s`) and the `catch`'s 502 never ran — making the `<img onError>` candidate-advance chain **unreachable dead code for precisely the slow-gateway case it was written for**. Lowered to 8s so the abort fires first. (The 504 burst had already self-resolved — 205 in 12:25–13:05Z → 2 in 13:50–14:40Z — ipfs.io recovering, not a code change; fixed because the soft-fail path is proven not to work.)
- **Tests:** `__tests__/api-public-ipfs-media-cid.test.ts` 4 → 8, pinning the oversize 302 + body-cancel, the under-ceiling stream keeping `s-maxage`, the chunked-no-content-length fallback, and that the timeout is under the platform cutoff. **2 of the 4 new tests proven to fail** against the pre-fix route by stashing it. `tsc` clean on all real source.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (route + component only; no schema, config, or env).
