### 2026-07-31 (Cowork, interactive — "what's the status of Pack Open history?" → full remaining-pool audit) — SHIPPED 2 DB-only items: an AllDay pack-pull edition-attribution backfill (37.2% → 49.3%) and `v_pack_remaining_basis`, the per-dist instrument that says whether a pack's remaining-pull pool can be trusted. No deploy, no code change.

Trevor's framing was that pack-open history feeds "what's still in the packs." **It mostly doesn't, and establishing that was the audit's main value.** Remaining-pull pools come from the PUBLISHER (`packEditionsV3 { count remaining }`), not from our on-chain opens — and only Top Shot models remaining at all. Headline: of 1,398 distributions currently serving a live Pack EV, **only 390 (27.9%) have a trustworthy remaining pool.**

**SHIPPED 1 — `audit_20260801_allday_pull_edition_backfill_stage` + `_apply` (DB-only).** `allday_pack_pull.edition_id` was NULL on 372,454 of 593,021 rows (37.2% attributed), which is the binding constraint on any opens-derived AllDay remaining pool. Backfilled 65,430 moments / **+72,143 rows from local sources only** (wmc preferred, then collection-scoped `sales`), fill-only, zero ambiguous. Attribution now **49.3%**. ⚠ **METHOD NOTE, and the trap that nearly produced a false P0:** I first measured the derivation against the 220,567 rows that already had an `edition_id` and got **94.2% agreement**, with `sales` apparently wrong 13% of the time — which would have meant AllDay FMV was contaminated. It was **my query that was wrong, not the data**: I joined `sales` on `nft_id` WITHOUT `collection_id`, and Flow nft_ids are per-collection sequences that COLLIDE across collections. Collection-scoped, the three sources agree **100.00%** (n=1,503 three-way). **Durable: never join `sales`/`wallet_moments_cache` on `nft_id`/`moment_id` alone — always scope by `collection_id`.** Distrust the instrument before the system. **Revert:** `UPDATE public.allday_pack_pull p SET edition_id = NULL FROM public.audit_20260801_allday_pull_edition_backfill a WHERE p.moment_nft_id = a.moment_nft_id AND p.edition_id = a.edition_id;`

**SHIPPED 2 — `audit_20260801_v_pack_remaining_basis` (DB-only, additive view).** One row per distribution giving `remaining_basis` in {`publisher_remaining`, `original_supply`, `original_supply_mislabelled`, `placeholder_uniform`, `depleted`, `none`} plus a boolean `remaining_trustworthy` and a `basis_note`. `security_invoker = on`, anon/authenticated REVOKED, service_role SELECT. Deliberately cheap — no `pack_rips` scan (DB time is the binding constraint). Live read: TS **390 trustworthy** / 324 `pool incomplete (sum drop_weight < 0.5)` / 544 `original_supply_mislabelled` / 69 depleted / 33 uniform-placeholder / 679 no pool; AllDay 2,950 + Golazos 210 `original_supply`; Pinnacle 143 `none`. **Revert:** `DROP VIEW IF EXISTS public.v_pack_remaining_basis;`

**FINDINGS (measured, not shipped — full detail in [docs/handoff-2026-07-31-pack-remaining-pool.md](docs/handoff-2026-07-31-pack-remaining-pool.md)):**
- **The hydrator backlog is structurally UNREACHABLE, not slow.** `v_moments_needing_hydration` has no attempt/failure column, and the worker reads it `ORDER BY acquired_date DESC LIMIT 300`. Unresolvable nft_ids never leave the view, so they occupy the queue head permanently — the top-300 window spans only ~3.5 days and **~173,500 rows (Apr–May 2026) are never fetched at all**. Fix is an attempt-tracking column + least-recently-tried ordering (worker + wrangler deploy, so not shippable from Cowork).
- **Top Shot on-chain opens can NEVER be the remaining basis:** observed rips 762,082 vs publisher-opened 16,837,027 = **4.5%** (our TS rip history starts 2023-09-29; TS packs start 2020). Publisher remaining is the only viable TS source — correct as built.
- **AllDay opens ARE trustworthy at pack level:** observed rips 1,599,984 vs publisher-opened 1,599,257 = **100.0%** across 2,910/3,012 dists. So an opens-derived AllDay remaining pool is viable once pull attribution is high enough — the one place pack-open history genuinely unlocks remaining.
- **AllDay EV is overstated because it is original-supply weighted.** `compute-allday-pack-ev` weights by `circulation_count` and never queries `remaining`, while `app/api/allday-pack-ev/route.ts` DOES use `packEditionsV3 { remaining }` — **two different EV models on the same collection.** Real consumer packs show the bias: Grail Seekers Legendary dist 7073 `gross_ev` **$523 vs realized median $65.63** (n=124).
- **`pack_ev_latest` is publishing internal Dapper reserve packs.** AllDay dist 5730 "NFL Pack Hold - Genesis" carries `pack_price` **$999,999** and `gross_ev` **$900,000**; several "Holding Pack" rows sit at $9,999. These alone drive AllDay's average `gross_ev` to $1,880 vs `typical_ev` $14.18. Not purchasable — should be filtered off the EV surface.
- **Atlas pool (57 TS dists) stale since 2026-07-17** yet EV recomputes off it hourly. `gql_historical` (544 dists) writes `count/totalCount` — original mint share — but the RPC reports it as `ev_basis='remaining'`; currently latent (0 live EV rows) but a mislabel waiting to surface.

### 2026-07-31 (Claude Code, interactive — pre-ship validation of the AllDay remaining-pool port) — SHIPPED: a CORRECTION to `docs/handoff-2026-07-31-pack-remaining-pool.md`. Docs-only, no prod/DB state change. **Blocks a pricing change that was queued on invalid evidence.**
Set out to produce the before/after diff that handoff Item 1 requires before porting `packEditionsV3 { remaining }` into `compute-allday-pack-ev`. The diff could not be produced, and building it disproved the item's own premise. **The bias table in Item 1 was invalid**: it compared a WHOLE-PACK modeled `gross_ev` against `mv_allday_pack_realized`, which sums `pack_rips.pull_value_usd` — i.e. only the pulls we actually attributed. AllDay capture is low and, fatally, **uneven along the exact axis the bias was measured on**: pulls-per-rip by depletion bucket runs 0.91 / 0.31 / 0.48 / 0.33 with priced-share 55.7% / 37.7% / 41.9% / 19.2%, an ~8× spread in effective value capture. The two headline dists were the worst possible exemplars — 7073 captures 4.12 of 7 slots (59%), **7103 captures 0.56 of 7 (8%)**, and both are 99–100% opened (1 and 0 packs still sealed). Corrected read: warehouse ÷ realized medians are 1.46 / 1.21 / 1.98 / **0.67**, so on the freshest packs — holding **346,563 of ~460k sealed AllDay packs (74%)** — the warehouse model **UNDERSTATES**, and since realized is a floor there (~6% value capture) the true understatement is larger. That is the opposite sign to the "original-supply weighting overstates EV" thesis the port was justified by. **`v_allday_pack_realized_ev` cannot adjudicate EV-model accuracy in its current state, in either direction.** Also verified the port has an unstated transport blocker: `packEditionsV3` is on the **consumer** endpoint, CF-1009 blocked from worker AND residential egress (403 re-confirmed today) — only Vercel egress reaches it, which the edge function is not. **Actions taken:** rewrote Item 1 with the correction table + "do not ship on this"; upgraded Item 3's priority note (I had down-rated the hydrator/attribution gap as "not the Pack EV accuracy blocker" — wrong framing: realized-EV calibration is the only validation instrument for ANY EV model change, so attribution is upstream of the pricing work, not beside it); added a "What is NOT worth doing" entry so the confounded comparison is not re-derived. **Durable rule: never compare modeled `gross_ev` to `realized_*` without reporting `pulls_per_pack` + `pct_pulls_priced` alongside — if capture is not high AND uniform across the comparison axis, the ratio is an attribution-coverage measurement wearing a pricing-accuracy costume.** Same family as the collection-scoping trap logged in the Cowork entry below: distrust the instrument before the system. **Nothing shipped to prod; the AllDay port is NOT shipped and is now explicitly sequenced behind pull attribution.** **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (restores the prior handoff text).

Un-backfilled history, not a capability gap. **The "local sources are exhausted" measurement was true but the inference from it was wrong** — it was read as "therefore an external per-moment lookup is needed", when the live pipeline already resolves these on-chain.

That resolver, not a worker deploy, is the thing to fix.

### 2026-07-31 (Cowork, interactive — correction of my own correction) — RETRACTS three claims from the entry below and records the real, structural cause. Docs-only; no prod/DB state change, no deploy.

My previous entry correctly killed the "hydrator gates AllDay attribution" chain, then **replaced it with a wrong diagnosis of my own.** Retracting precisely:

- ❌ **"`allday-edition-resolver` is silently no-op'ing."** WRONG. It is not a pipeline — it is a *synthetic* `pipeline_runs` row written by the AllDay **sales** indexer ([app/api/allday-sales-indexer/route.ts:61,1095](app/api/allday-sales-indexer/route.ts#L1095)) for its inline **edition-CATALOG-fill** stage. `editions_hydrated_from_chain/relay` count new rows upserted into `editions` for editions first seen in that tick's sales. `0` means "no new AllDay editions needed" — **correct and healthy** on a complete catalog. It has **zero bearing on pack-pull attribution**. Two systems both named "resolve edition"; I conflated them.
- ❌ **"`get_allday_unresolved_pulls` has zero callers / the drain was never wired."** WRONG. It is called by the **deployed-but-ungitted** edge fn `resolve-allday-pull-editions`, driven by **pg_cron jobid 22 `rpc-allday-resolve-pull-editions` (`9,39 * * * *`, active)** — `cron.job_run_details`: **1,055 succeeded**, 7 failed (`job startup timeout`, last 07-25), latest success 2026-08-01 01:39Z. The drain runs fine and has for weeks.
- ❌ **"Fix that resolver, not a worker deploy."** WRONG target — nothing there is broken.

⚠ **DURABLE — a repo grep CANNOT see a pg_cron→HTTP caller of an ungitted edge function.** "Zero callers in the repo" ≠ "no caller." **Check `cron.job` before declaring any function dead.** The 07-31 revoke migration's own comment (`get_allday_unresolved_pulls(int) <- NO caller at all`) made the same error; the revoke itself is harmless (the edge fn calls with the service role — verified: the drain succeeded again *after* the revoke), but the reasoning was unsound and would not be for a wider grant.

**THE ACTUAL CAUSE — structural, not fixable by wiring or a deploy.** `resolve-allday-pull-editions` resolves a pull by **borrowing the moment at its open block** via Flow REST `/v1/scripts`. Forward pulls sit inside Flow's execution-state window, so they resolve → **100%**. Deep-history pulls do not: rest-mainnet **prunes execution state**, and `spork-proxy` fronts only `/v1/events` and `/v1/transactions`, **not `/v1/scripts`** ([supabase/functions/ingest-allday-pack-opens/index.ts:115-130](supabase/functions/ingest-allday-pack-opens/index.ts#L115-L130)). Historical rows therefore resolve only in the residual case where the moment is still borrowable today — which is exactly the observed **6.2–22.1%** on backfilled rows. Neither ingest mode writes `edition_id` at all ([index.ts:265-268,307-312](supabase/functions/ingest-allday-pack-opens/index.ts#L265-L268)) — the paths are byte-identical, so forward-vs-backfill is entirely a resolvability difference, not a code difference.

**Local sources are exhausted, now confirmed on a fourth table.** Of 293,274 still-NULL moments: `moments` **0**, `wmc` **95**, `nft_edition_map` **114**. Nothing left to mine in-database.

**CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PROGRAM (the thing that actually matters):** an opens-derived AllDay remaining pool can realistically only ever be built from **2026-01-01 onward**. Pre-2026 pull-level attribution is largely **unrecoverable**, so any AllDay remaining-pool model must either scope to 2026+ opens or carry an explicit coverage disclosure. Do not plan around "finish the AllDay attribution backfill" — it does not finish.

**WHAT STILL STANDS from the retracted entry** (re-verified, unchanged): the hydrator is **Top Shot only** (`TOPSHOT_COLLECTION_ID` hardcoded, [index.ts:84,122,238](workers/topshot-moments-hydrator/index.ts#L84)) and cannot attribute an AllDay pull; AllDay forward attribution is **100%** with a clean **2026-01-01** cutover (Jan 2026+ 0.0% NULL, May–Dec 2025 66–88%); the NULL count is **self-replenishing** as `allday-pack-opens-backfill` walks 2025 at 6–22% attribution; and **no `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` gates AllDay attribution** — the TS hydrator deploy gates only Top Shot pull provenance / realized-EV calibration.

**Monitoring gap noted, not shipped:** `resolve-allday-pull-editions` writes **no `pipeline_runs` row**, so a silent failure there would be invisible to `detect_stalled_pipelines()`; it is observable only via `cron.job_run_details` jobid 22 or the NULL-rate trend. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.

### 2026-07-31 (Cowork, interactive — resolved the "does the TS attribution gap matter?" question with measurement) — MEASURED, deliberately NOT shipped. Docs-only; no prod/DB state change, no deploy.

I flip-flopped twice on whether the 174k Top Shot moments-hydrator backlog is the Pack EV critical path. Settling it with numbers rather than a third opinion.

**It is a coverage issue, not a correctness catastrophe.** Top Shot pull capture is **92.6% mean** on recent packs (n=4,000 rips; 3,666 fully captured, 282 zero-capture) — nothing like the AllDay 0.31–0.91 pulls/pack confound that invalidated the earlier bias claim. And the realized MV already excludes the worst rows: `mv_topshot_pack_rip_values` filters `pr.pull_value_usd IS NOT NULL`, so only **0.1%** (29/37,367) of its rows are zero-valued.

**But it is not clean either: 14.3% of the MV's rips are PARTIALLY captured** (sampled n=3,000, mean capture **0.9230**), so their `pull_value_usd` is a partial sum of the pack's true value, and those rows feed `realized_mean` / `realized_median` → `calibrated_ev` (up to 0.85 weight) → the anon-readable `v_topshot_pack_ev_calibrated`.

⚠ **THE RESULT IS DIRECTION-SURPRISING, WHICH IS WHY NOTHING SHIPPED.** The obvious fix — restrict the MV to fully-captured rips (`attributed >= moments_pulled`) — was expected to raise realized values by recovering understated packs. Measured, it moves the per-dist mean **DOWN 7.35% (−$0.38)** and costs **19 of 184 qualifying dists** (184 → 165 at the `n_opens >= 10` gate). Plausible reading: a pack whose every moment is still attributable is a pack nobody moved — i.e. a low-value pack — so the capture effect and a selection effect point in **opposite** directions and this measurement cannot separate them.

**DO NOT ship the "keep only fully-captured rips" fix on this evidence.** It is a 7.35% shift of unproven sign-correctness that also drops 10% of covered distributions, and validating it needs exactly the realized-vs-actual ground truth we lack. Separating the two effects needs a capture-ratio-stratified comparison against packs with independent value evidence (e.g. secondary sale of the sealed pack), not a filter.

**Net effect on priorities:** the Top Shot hydrator deploy stays worth doing for coverage and for the ~173,500 Apr–May rows that are unreachable by construction, but it is **correctly ranked below** the publisher-side remaining-pool items — which is what the original 2026-07-31 handoff said before I talked myself out of it. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.

### 2026-07-31 (Cowork, interactive — "do what's best for RPC") — MEASURED a validated tier-scaled remaining basis and, more importantly, **quantified how wrong original-supply weighting is** using Top Shot ground truth. Docs-only; no prod/DB state change, no deploy.

**Starting point: every Top Shot distribution already carries publisher `remaining_by_tier`.** `topshot_pack_supply` has it for all **2,039** TS dists (`supply_ok`, ~16h fresh) — including all 679 with no drop pool, all 544 `original_supply_mislabelled`, and all 33 `placeholder_uniform`. That is authoritative publisher remaining data sitting unused on 1,325 dists / **148,163 sealed packs**.

**METHOD — tier-scaled remaining.** For edition `e` in tier `T` of a dist: `weight_e = orig_drop_weight_e × (remaining_by_tier[T] / original_by_tier[T])`, then normalize. It reconstructs a per-edition remaining distribution from original weights plus per-tier depletion.

**VALIDATED ON GROUND TRUTH, not asserted.** Tested on the 423 multi-tier dists where `pool_source='gql'` gives true per-edition `remaining`, comparing the weighted-mean FMV (the `gross_ev` basis) under each weighting:

| weighting | mean abs error vs truth |
|---|---|
| original-supply (`orig_drop_weight`) | **101.5%** |
| tier-scaled | **26.8%** |

Tier-scaled is closer on **299/423 (70.7%)** of dists — a **3.8× error reduction**.

⚠ **THE HEADLINE IS THE FIRST ROW, NOT THE SECOND: original-supply weighting carries ~101% mean absolute error against true remaining on multi-tier packs.** **AllDay, Golazos and Pinnacle are ALL on original-supply weighting.** This re-establishes the "AllDay EV is materially overstated" concern on sound footing after the earlier $523-vs-$65.63 evidence was correctly invalidated by the attribution-capture confound — and it does so **without touching AllDay data at all**, so the capture confound cannot contaminate it. Caveat carried honestly: measured on Top Shot pack structures; AllDay pack composition differs, so treat ~101% as "large and directionally established", not as AllDay's exact figure.

**ADDRESSABLE FOOTPRINT TODAY IS MODEST — stated plainly so this is not oversold.** Tier-scaling only discriminates on **multi-tier** dists, and 1,233 TS dists (351,833 sealed packs) are **single-tier**, where it collapses to a uniform rescale of the original weights and adds nothing. Applying it where a pool exists but is original-basis:
- `original_supply_mislabelled`: 544 dists → **78 multi-tier**, 9,090 sealed packs, **0 currently publishing EV** (latent correctness only).
- `placeholder_uniform`: 33 dists → **30 multi-tier**, 7,464 sealed packs, **30 currently publishing** — and these render **NULL** today, so tier-scaling would turn "no number" into a defensible number. That is the one immediate user-visible win.

**NOT SHIPPED, deliberately.** Changing how `gross_ev` is weighted is pricing logic, and per the standing rule (`data fixes OK; pricing LOGIC → hand off`) it needs a human diffing the EV output before/after. Nothing here is shelf-ware: the method, its validation numbers and the exact applicable dist sets are recorded so the change can be made in one pass with a known expected effect. **Do not apply tier-scaling to single-tier dists** — it is a no-op there and would only add false precision.

**Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.

### 2026-07-31 (Cowork, interactive) — TESTED and KILLED the "publisher-independent remaining" idea. Docs-only; no prod/DB state change, no deploy.

**The attractive idea:** every collection except Top Shot lacks per-edition remaining, and the APIs that would supply it are transport-blocked (AllDay `packEditionsV3` is CF-1009 blocked; Pinnacle unknown). So infer depletion from data we already own — an edition's minted circulation vs its original pool count — giving `remaining ≈ orig_drop_weight − circulation_count`. That would bypass the transport problem for AllDay, Golazos **and** Pinnacle at once. It does not work.

**Tested against Top Shot ground truth** (26,143 pool rows / 756 dists where `pool_source='gql'` supplies true per-edition `remaining`), correlating each candidate's normalized weight against the true remaining share:

| candidate weight | correlation with truth |
|---|---|
| original draw count (`orig_drop_weight`) | **0.812** |
| `orig_drop_weight − circulation_count` | **0.239** |

**Subtracting circulation makes the estimate substantially WORSE, and the reason is structural: `circulation_count >= orig_drop_weight` on 26,133 of 26,143 rows (99.96%).** Pack-pool editions are **not pack-exclusive** — an edition's minted circulation accumulates across many packs and non-pack sources, so it carries no information about how much of *this* pack's allocation is left. The subtraction is almost always clamped at zero. **The whole class of circulation-derived or observed-serial-derived depletion estimators is dead for the same reason**, and it cannot be rescued for Pinnacle either: Top Shot is the only collection with ground truth to validate against, so a Pinnacle-specific variant would be unvalidatable by construction. **Do not re-propose inferring pack depletion from circulation or observed serials.**

⚠ **METHODOLOGICAL NOTE worth keeping, because it explains an apparent contradiction in this thread.** Original weights correlate **0.812** with true remaining at the row level, yet the earlier measurement found original-supply weighting carries **~101% mean absolute error** on the FMV-weighted mean that `gross_ev` actually uses. Both are correct. EV is dominated by the high-FMV tail — precisely the chase editions that deplete first and whose remaining share collapses fastest — so a weighting can track the bulk of the pool well and still be catastrophically wrong about the money. **Judge a remaining proxy by the FMV-weighted quantity EV consumes, never by weight correlation.** A 0.81 correlation would have looked like a green light.

**Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.

**THE RULE (generalized, and it is not Cowork-specific).** `apply_migration` via MCP writes to `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` ONLY — never a repo file, never the ledger. Any migration applied that way is live in prod with **no revert path on disk** unless someone files it separately. Recovery is mechanical: `SELECT array_to_string(statements, E'\n') FROM supabase_migrations.schema_migrations WHERE version = '<v>';`

**⚠ THE REPO WAS NEVER THE SYSTEM OF RECORD — do not read "no migration file" as "unauthorized change."** Prod holds **2,334** migrations; the repo holds **242** (~10%). Filing a `.sql` has always been the exception, so a missing file proves nothing on its own. **The binding record per CLAUDE.md is the LEDGER** (date · what shipped · revert path). So the real audit question is "does this have a ledger entry with a revert path?", and the correct check is a two-key one — repo file OR ledger entry — not a repo-file scan. Across the 43 migrations applied 07-28→07-31, **11 had neither**; the rest were covered by one or the other.

### 2026-07-31 (Claude Code, interactive — AllDay sales serial-supply regression) — FIXED THE WRITER + backfilled 8,575 rows. The inbound handoff scoped this to `onchain_dapper_v2` (1,325 rows) and called v1 "unaffected"; measured, it is **all three AllDay onchain sources, 8,626 rows, and v1 is the largest and fastest-growing arm**.

**SHIPPED — writer fix (`app/api/allday-sales-indexer/route.ts`) + backfill migration `audit_20260731_allday_sales_serial_backfill_from_nft_edition_map`.**

**Root cause (measured, not inferred).** The indexer's ONLY serial sources were `wallet_moments_cache` and a Cadence borrow fallback capped at `CADENCE_FALLBACK_MAX = 12` per run that fires only when the **edition** is unresolved. wmc holds only moments in a wallet we have walked, so for these NFTs there was **no wmc row at all** (`wmc_row_exists = 0`, not merely a null serial). The borrow then resolved the edition while returning no usable `serialNumber` (`Number(undefined)` → NaN → 0 → the `if (resolvedSerial > 0)` guard skips the set), so the row was inserted with `serial_number: null`. `nft_edition_map` — the durable nftID→serial record — was never consulted on the direct-insert path, **even though `promote_unmapped_sales` already uses exactly that fallback**. The precedent existed in the DB path and was missing in the route.

**The load-bearing measurement: 1,321 of 1,325 v2 rows (99.7%) had a positive serial in `nft_edition_map` BEFORE the sale row was written** (median lag 0). The data was there at write time; the writer didn't read it. That is what makes this a writer defect rather than a recovery-timing problem — and it is why the writer fix had to land, not just a backfill.

**Scope correction — the handoff's "v1 is unaffected (0–3.4%)" is wrong.** All three sources are written by the SAME insert path (`source` is derived from `s.saleSource` inside one loop), so one fix covers all three. Weekly, by ingestion:

| source | 06-15→07-06 | 07-13 | 07-20 | 07-27 | bad rows | recoverable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `onchain_dapper_v1` | **0.0%** | 37.6% | 23.8% | **41.6%** (2,506) | 5,078 | 98.9% |
| `onchain` | **0.0%** | 15.4% | 6.0% | 3.3% | 2,223 | 100% |
| `onchain_dapper_v2` | **0.0%** | 11.6% | 9.6% | 20.5% | 1,325 | 100% |

Identical 07-13 onset on all three after 4+ weeks at a hard zero. v1 alone in the latest week (2,506 rows) exceeds the entire v2 finding the handoff reported.

**NOT caused by `5c1b0db9`** (the 07-04 "write NULL not phantom 0" commit), the obvious suspect: it landed a full week before the onset and the week of 07-06 is still 0.0% on all three arms. That commit changed the *sentinel* (0 → NULL); it did not create the gap.

**Impact.** `serial_number` drives `serial_fmv_estimate`, the special-serials board and jersey-match. Nothing monitored it — `allday-sales-indexer` is green throughout because it writes rows successfully. Same shape as the Panini sale-field outage: a healthy pipeline silently dropping one field.

**Backfill result:** 8,575 rows recovered, **0 mismatches**, 59 left (genuinely no map row with a positive serial). Audit table records every mutated row. RLS enabled + anon/authenticated REVOKED; `check_public_security_invariants()` 0 rows, `rowsecurity=false` 0 tables after.

**Test:** `__tests__/api-allday-sales-indexer-deep.test.ts` — new case reproduces the exact prod mechanism (no wmc row + borrow returns no `serialNumber` + map holds the serial). **Verified it FAILS without the fix** (`serial_number: null` vs expected `42`) and passes with it, so the pin cannot silently rot into a test that asserts nothing.

**Revert path:**
```
git revert <code-sha>
```
```sql
UPDATE public.sales s SET serial_number = NULL
  FROM public.audit_20260731_allday_serial_backfill a
 WHERE s.id = a.sale_id AND s.serial_number = a.new_serial;
DROP TABLE public.audit_20260731_allday_serial_backfill;
```

**SECOND FINDING — the serial RECOVERY lane has the identical blind spot, and had been failing on these rows for 26 days while green.** `sales-serial-backfill` (edge fn, 37/37 ok runs, 4,314 rows written/30d) resolves serials **only on-chain**, by borrowing the moment from its *current holder* — `nft_edition_map` appears nowhere in it. That structurally cannot work for a sold NFT that has since moved or sits in escrow. **7,276 of the 8,575 rows I just backfilled were sitting in `sales_serial_backfill_failures`** with **46,376 accumulated retries** (`onchain_nil` 5,508 / `no_holder` 1,768), first failing **2026-07-06** and still retrying at **02:41Z today** — the durable local map held the answer the whole time. `get_serial_backfill_targets` was NOT the problem: it correctly includes AllDay and keys on `serial_number IS NULL OR = 0`, so these rows were eligible every run. The lane picked them up, went on-chain, failed, and logged `ok=true`.

**This class has recurred once already, which validates the writer-first ordering.** `audit_20260705_allday_serial_backfill` (**8,964 rows**) is a prior manual backfill of the same defect on 07-05. It drained the rows and did NOT fix the writer, so the gap re-accumulated to 8,626 within ~3 weeks. A backfill alone buys ~3 weeks.

**Side benefit, quantified:** the backfilled rows now carry a serial, so they drop out of `get_serial_backfill_targets` automatically — the lane's daily futile on-chain retry load fell from **~7,674 → 398 rows**.

**⚠ POST-DEPLOY CORRECTION — I FIRST DEFERRED THE RECOVERY-LANE FIX ON A BAD MEASUREMENT. IT IS THE ITEM THAT ACTUALLY CLOSES THIS. Read this before acting on anything above.**

I initially wrote that teaching `sales-serial-backfill` to read `nft_edition_map` "would recover exactly 1 row today" and deferred it. **That number was a point-in-time artifact: I measured the residual in the one minute after my own backfill had just drained it.** The correct denominator is the ONGOING arrival rate, and it is not small.

**Verified against the first post-deploy indexer runs (03:36Z / 03:41Z):**

| path | rows | no serial |
|---|---|---|
| `onchain_dapper_v2` | 4 | **0** ✅ |
| `onchain_dapper_v1` | 24 | 22 ❌ |
| `onchain` | 10 | 10 ❌ |

**32 rows arrived with a null serial in the ~22 min after deploy, and 31 of them (96.9%) are recoverable from `nft_edition_map` NOW** — i.e. the map is populated *shortly after* the sale is written, by a later pipeline. My writer fix reads the map at ingest, so it fixes the case where the NFT is ALREADY mapped (which was 99.7% of the 8,626-row backlog — hence the clean drain) but it **cannot** fix a first-sight NFT whose map row does not exist yet. For that, only a **re-sweep after the map fills** works — which is precisely what `sales-serial-backfill` is for, and precisely what it fails at by going on-chain instead of reading the map.

**So: the writer fix + backfill closed the accumulated backlog and the already-mapped case; the ONGOING case is still open and the recovery-lane fix is the thing that closes it.** Do not read the headline "31.3%/9.1%/7.1% → 0.4%/0.0%/0.0%" as the ongoing rate — that is the state of the *stock* after the backfill, not the *flow*.

Also corrected: `promote_unmapped_sales` is a second writer of these rows (matched by exact `ingested_at` ↔ its `pipeline_runs` timestamps, 03:36:17.459/03:41:37.394) — it DOES read `nft_edition_map`, but in those transactions the map row is written in the same txn and is not visible to its lookup, so it falls through its `COALESCE(..., 0)` → trigger → NULL. That is a distinct ordering defect from the route defect fixed above.

**Consequence to expect, and it is CORRECT behaviour:** the `sales_serial_supply_worst_pct` arm shipped tonight reads **0.75** right now only because its 24h window is still dominated by pre-fix rows that the backfill filled. As the window rolls forward onto the ongoing flow, it will climb and **may breach 5 and page**. That is the metric working, not a false alarm — the underlying gap is real and unfixed. Do not silence it; fix the recovery lane.

**✅ ROOT CAUSE OF THE ONGOING CASE FOUND AND FIXED — it was NOT the recovery lane, and it was a one-line route bug in 3 files.** Chasing the residual to its source: `promote_unmapped_sales` inserts `COALESCE(r.serial_number, r.map_serial, 0)`, where `r.serial_number` is `unmapped_sales.serial_number` and `map_serial` is the `nft_edition_map`→`wmc` fallback. **All three onchain sales indexers wrote `unmapped_sales` with a HARDCODED `serial_number: 0`** — and `COALESCE` returns the first **non-null** value, so a literal `0` always wins and **`map_serial` is unreachable DEAD CODE**. The row then lands in `sales` as 0 → `trg_sales_coerce_zero_serial_to_null` → NULL. A serial we already had on file was being discarded at the last step, and the DB-side fallback everyone (including the inbound handoff) assumed was working had never once executed for these rows.

`5c1b0db9` (2026-07-04) established NULL as the canonical unknown-serial sentinel and fixed the `sales` writer — **it missed the `unmapped_sales` writer**, which is where the COALESCE actually reads from. That is why the gap opened without any code change to the serial logic itself.

**SHIPPED:** `serial_number: 0` → `null` in the `unmappedRows` push of **`allday-sales-indexer`, `golazos-sales-indexer`, `ufc-sales-indexer`**. AllDay is the proven-affected one; Golazos/UFC carry the identical dead-fallback defect and are fixed preventively (same literal, same COALESCE, column is nullable with no default).

**Caller sweep done before shipping (the "enumerate EVERY consumer" rule):** `unmapped_sales.serial_number` has ZERO code readers; DB readers are `promote_unmapped_sales`, `backfill_nft_edition_map_from_sales`, `analytics_data_quality_overview` and 4 views. Only the DQ function references a literal `0`, and it is already NULL-aware (`s.serial_number IS NULL OR s.serial_number = 0`) **and reads `sales`, not `unmapped_sales`**. Nothing depends on the 0.

**Tests: three existing assertions PINNED THE BUG** (`serial_number: 0` on the unmapped row) and were rewritten. Note the two Golazos/UFC `serial_number: 0` assertions that REMAIN are correct and deliberately untouched — they assert the `sales` insert, where the trigger coerces 0→NULL harmlessly; only the `unmapped_sales` path poisons the COALESCE. 27 tests green, `tsc` clean.

**Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (restores `serial_number: 0` in all three; DB unchanged, no migration).

**AND THE PENDING STOCK, TOO — `audit_20260731_unmapped_sales_zero_serial_to_null` (DB-only, no deploy).** The writer fix only affects NEWLY written unmapped rows; the pending backlog still carried the poisoned literal. UFC (1,554) and Golazos (153) have no recoverable serial and are unaffected. **Lossless** — 0 is not a real Flow serial, it is a non-value, so nothing is destroyed and the revert is exact. Verified after apply: 96,577 / 96,577 NULL / 0 zero. **Revert:** `UPDATE public.unmapped_sales SET serial_number = 0 WHERE serial_number IS NULL;`

**Root cause — a known bug, already found and fixed twice, never generalized.** `runIdOnlyBackfill` writes `edition_key: null` deliberately (helpers L546-559), on the stated premise that *"out-of-band edition resolvers populate player/set/tier on the editions table and reads JOIN at query time."* **Nothing can JOIN to `editions` without an `edition_key`**, and only **0.0%** of these rows are recoverable via `moments` (TopShot 2.3%). Prod DB migration (applied via MCP + committed) + re-pinned DB test.

- **Context:** the TODO sweep re-confirmed the standing finding (every live TODO is RESOLVED/GATED — nothing safe + straightforward to implement), so on the "also fix bugs" directive I took the sole open Sentry issue: `JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-22` "set detail unavailable: canceling statement due to statement timeout" on `GET /[collection]/set/[slug]` (1 user, last seen ~07-30).
- **Root cause (profiled, not guessed):** `get_set_detail`'s only expensive work is the per-edition latest-FMV rollup. For Top Shot "Base Set" (3,606 thumbnail-bearing editions) the `LEFT JOIN LATERAL … ORDER BY computed_at DESC LIMIT 1` fans out to 3,606 correlated probes across the yearly `fmv_snapshots` partitions — **~2.0s warm** (+3,883 cold reads) — and cold under contention it exceeded the request statement budget and THREW, erroring the whole public set page. `rpcWithRetry` (which the page's read already uses) deliberately does NOT retry 57014 (07-26 change — a slow query just re-times-out), so retry was never the fix.
- **Rejected alternatives (measured, not assumed):** the CLAUDE.md "use `fmv_current`" rule is for the JS-1000-row-cap correctness case, NOT this in-DB path — a `fmv_current` DISTINCT-ON join is **11× WORSE (22.5s)** (materializes the DISTINCT ON over all ~942k snapshot rows before filtering). A covering `INCLUDE(fmv_usd,floor_price_usd)` index doesn't help either: the wanted row is always the newest = a hot, not-all-visible page, so index-only still heap-fetches. Precompute into `sets_summary` is wrong-scoped (its `edition_count` deliberately excludes the thumbnail filter) + a sensitive daily-matview change. So the LATERAL stays and we bound its FAILURE instead.
- **SHIPPED — `audit_20260801_get_set_detail_graceful_fmv_timeout` (DB-only, no deploy).** Wrapped ONLY the rollup in `BEGIN … EXCEPTION WHEN query_canceled` so a request-level statement timeout DEGRADES the header stats to NULL (page renders "—" via `fmtCount(null)`) instead of throwing; the page — incl. the separately-fetched editions grid — still renders. Also dropped the RETURN's `COALESCE(edition_count,0)` so a degraded read shows "—" not a misleading "0" beside a populated grid. Happy path behaviourally byte-identical (COUNT(*) is never NULL; normal sets finish in a few ms). STABLE preserved; grants preserved + re-asserted (service_role-only; anon/auth EXECUTE false).
- **Durable finding (cost a live break, now fixed):** `statement_timeout` is armed at the TOP-LEVEL command boundary and CANNOT be re-armed mid-function — a `SET LOCAL statement_timeout` inside the body throws "SET is not allowed in a non-volatile function" on a STABLE fn (my first apply broke the fn on EVERY call for ~2 min until the fix), and even under VOLATILE the inner SET is a no-op (verified: `pg_sleep(1)` under `SET LOCAL '50ms'` completes). So the handler catches the ROLE/request timeout that was ALREADY firing (the one producing the Sentry error); no new inner budget is added, and the final ship is the clean STABLE + `BEGIN/EXCEPTION` wrapper only.
- **Verified:** live happy path (Base Set 3606/3603 + real FMV; a Pinnacle set; unknown slug → NULL); graceful degrade proven DETERMINISTICALLY on local postgres:16 (rollup > budget → `query_canceled` caught → envelope returned with NULL stat, no throw); DB-invariant test re-pinned to the new migration + verbatim block (local `run-db-tests.sh` get_set_detail ✓, drift guard 57/57); `tsc` clean; live `pg_proc` == committed migration (has EXCEPTION handler, no COALESCE, STABLE).

### 2026-08-01 (Claude Code, interactive — handoff drain, cont.) — SHIPPED the fix for the queued TS-PACK-OPENS-HISTORY-BACKFILL-SPORK-FLOOR-500. The diagnosis in that queued item was wrong on three counts; the real defect is an all-or-nothing 25k-block window against a FLAKY (not dead) spork. Edge fn `ingest-topshot-pack-opens-history` now checkpoints partial scan progress. Repo + DEPLOYED v4 via Supabase MCP.

- **Three corrections to the queued item, each evidence-backed.** (1) **"rows_written=0 for four days incl. the green days" is NOT silent loss — it is correct dedup.** Positive control: the 03:56Z run logged `rows_found=81` over blocks 95,090,659–95,115,658, and `pack_rips` holds **exactly 81** TS rips in that window. It found 81 opens, all 81 already stored, wrote 0. The signal was missing because **`rows_skipped` was never instrumented** on this route (logged 0 despite 81 dedups) — `rows_written` alone is a null instrument for a *re-walking* backfill. (2) **The "cursor-skip" was a fast-forward, not a skip.** 95,090,659 → 61,930,346 = exactly `MIN(pack_rips.block_height)` for TS; coverage from there to head is dense and gapless (20/20 width_buckets populated, 21k–120k rips each). Nothing was stepped over. (3) **`c4c4d3c9` cannot be the cause — it is a docs-only ledger commit** (`git show --stat`: 1 file, `docs/overnight/ledger.md`). The correlation was spurious. Also: AllDay is not out-finding TopShot — both find 80–330/run; AllDay *writes* them because it is on uncovered ground.
- **Where the low-range data actually came from:** all **272,559** TS rips below block 96M were written on **one day, 2026-07-11**, spanning 61,930,346–95,999,995 — the Dapper `searchPackNft` registry bulk load ([[dapper-searchpacknft-opens-registry]]), not this event scanner. So the fn has been re-verifying the registry's work, which is why it found plenty and wrote nothing.
- **THE ACTUAL DEFECT.** The fn scans a 25,000-block window as ~100 sequential 250-block `/events` queries and abandons the **entire** window on the first failure (`after = anyTransient ? cur : start`). The deep-history spork is **flaky, not down** — the 41 failing runs died at query **1,2,3,4,5 in rotation**, i.e. different sub-windows each time, several getting 4 chunks deep. With any per-query failure rate, a 100-query all-or-nothing window essentially never completes, so the cursor never moved and 96 runs/day burned. This is NOT the spork-floor problem the queued item assumed (`floor` was already correctly set to 27,341,470 and `spork_available:true`).
- **SHIPPED — descending scan + checkpoint (edge fn, repo + deployed v4).** `scanOpens` now walks **DESCENDING** (end→start, matching the cursor's direction) and returns `scannedFloor` = the lowest block CONFIRMED scanned; an ascending scan cannot checkpoint because a mid-window failure leaves a hole *above* the scanned prefix. `resolveOpens` returns `resolvedFloor` + `exhausted` so the cursor never advances past opens the tx budget left unwritten (scanning a block ≠ having written its rips). Cursor advances to `min(scannedFloor-or-resolvedFloor, cur)`, clamped at `floor`. Progress is now **monotonic under any upstream failure rate**. Also: `rows_skipped` is now populated (= dedup count) via `writeRips` returning `{written, candidates}`, and `ok` = *progressed OR no error* — a checkpointed run that advanced did its job (failure preserved in `extra.scan_err` + new `extra.partial`); only a run that moved NOTHING stays `ok=false` and pages.
- **The "how far back" question the queued item deferred is already answered IN THE FN's own header** — `SPORK_FLOOR = 27,341,470` (mainnet17 root, 2022-04-06). Public sporks bottom out there; TS genesis (~block 7M, Oct 2020) is permanently unreachable and documented as an explicit gap. So there is **~34.6M blocks of real, reachable, un-indexed TS pack-open history** (2022-04-06 → 2023-09-29) below the registry floor. No decision was needed and none was invented — the fn should keep walking to 27,341,470.
- ⚠ **Deployed as a MINIMAL DIFF: the deployed body keeps its inline `https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2` import** while the repo file uses the bare specifier via `supabase/functions/deno.json`. That is the documented pre-existing repo↔deployed divergence, deliberately not changed in the same deploy as a logic fix.
- ⚠ **Unexplained-by-code:** nothing in the repo sets the cursor to 61,930,346 — the fn only ever writes `start`. Consistent with a deliberate manual fast-forward to the registry floor; noted, not treated as a defect.
- **POST-DEPLOY VERIFICATION — fix CONFIRMED working, and the flaky-not-dead diagnosis is now PROVEN.** 14:57:19Z tick: `ok=false`, `progress_blocks=0`, failed chunk `61,930,096–61,930,345` (the top chunk — descending scan starting nearest the cursor, as designed). 15:11:01Z tick: **that same chunk SUCCEEDED**, `ok=true`, `partial=true`, `q=2`, cursor 61,930,346 → **61,930,096**, `scanned_floor=61,930,096`. A chunk that 500s and then serves 14 min later is conclusive — the sub-61.93M region is flaky, not dead, so the queued spork-floor guard would have been wrong. Under the old code that 15:11 run would have been `ok=false` with zero progress; the 250 blocks are now kept.
- ⚠ **NEW RISK INTRODUCED BY THIS FIX — do not read the above as a clean win. THROUGHPUT, and the loss of every alarm.** At ~1–3 chunks/tick (~250–750 blocks) against **34.6M blocks remaining**, this region would take on the order of YEARS. Worse, because the cursor now moves and runs report `ok=true`, **neither `cursor_stalled` NOR the fail-rate alarm can ever fire for it again** — the job is now invisible while making ~1% of design throughput. That is precisely the [[green-pipeline-blind-to-its-own-work]] class. The fix is still strictly better than a hard wedge (it was making ZERO progress and paging), but the pipeline now needs a *rate* signal, not a liveness one. ⚠ **The ETA is a 2-SAMPLE estimate** — the ascending history (failures at query 1–5, i.e. 0–4 chunks succeeding) is the same order but this must be measured over a full day before anyone acts on it.
- **QUEUED (next lever, deliberately NOT taken unilaterally — it is a cost/throughput tradeoff against the spork proxy): raise the per-chunk retry budget on the spork events path.** `j()` gives up after 3 tries at 400ms×n backoff; since the identical chunk demonstrably succeeds minutes later, a larger in-run retry budget (or a longer backoff) should raise chunks-per-run substantially and is a one-constant change. Second queued item: a **backfill-rate metric** (e.g. blocks/day per history cursor, or an ETA-to-floor arm on `v_rpc_trust_health`) so a crawling-but-green backfill is visible — without it this fix trades a loud wedge for a silent one.
- **SAME-CLASS DEFECT FOUND + FIXED IN THE ALLDAY TWIN — and it is ACTIVELY LOSING DATA TODAY (repo only, NOT deployed).** `ingest-allday-pack-opens` carries the identical ascending-scan + `after = anyTransient ? cur : start`. It is not wedged (its region isn't flaky yet, 53,165 rows/24h) but it has the **second** failure mode live: on a `MAX_TX=180` tx-budget stop it still advances the FULL 25,000-block window over opens it never resolved. **Measured: 16 of 143 runs in 24h hit `tx_fetched = 180` exactly, every one advancing the full 25,000 blocks** (e.g. 11:56Z `rows_found=939`, budget hit, cursor 111,465,659 → 111,440,659). Those opens are never revisited — the cursor only walks down.
- ⚠ **DURABLE — scan direction MUST match the caller's cursor direction, and this fn has TWO walkers going opposite ways.** A naive port of the Top Shot fix (unconditional descending) would have silently changed which rows the FORWARD walker's budget drops: forward walks UP, so a descending scan leaves its *lowest* opens unresolved while it advances to `end`. Fixed properly instead — `scanOpens(start, end, dir)` with `"desc"` for backfill and the default `"asc"` for forward/probe, so **forward-mode behaviour is byte-identical to today** and only backfill gains the checkpoint. Getting the direction backwards is silent loss, not an error: the unscanned hole ends up on the side the cursor is about to claim.
- **Why AllDay is NOT deployed this session (deliberate, not a deferral of work — the artifact is committed and reviewable):** it is a healthy, high-volume live pipeline, and the MCP deploy channel inlines the whole ~460-line body by hand, which CLAUDE.md flags as a transcription risk for byte-exact constants. It deserves its own deploy + post-deploy tick verification rather than riding at the tail of another change. Both fns type-clean under `tsc --strict` (only the pre-existing `Deno.serve` `req: any`, identical in both). **To deploy:** same MCP call as the Top Shot one, `verify_jwt:false`, then confirm a backfill tick shows `cursor_after < cursor_before` with `extra.resolve_exhausted` honoured. **Forward-mode tx-budget loss is left OPEN** (pre-existing; needs the asc-side checkpoint) — queued, not silently fixed.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` restores the repo file; to unwind PROD, redeploy the previous body — `mcp__supabase__deploy_edge_function` with `ingest-topshot-pack-opens-history`, `verify_jwt:false`, using the **v3** source (recoverable via `get_edge_function` history, or `git show <sha>^:supabase/functions/ingest-topshot-pack-opens-history/index.ts` with the import line swapped back to the esm.sh form). No DB or cursor change to unwind — the cursor moves only forward-down and re-walking is idempotent on `tx_hash`.

### 2026-08-01 (Claude Code, interactive — picking up the handed-over "trust-health view takes 49s" item) — DISPROVED the handoff's diagnosis, then fixed the REAL hot spot. One DB-only index; `v_rpc_trust_health` 7,999ms → 1,006ms with the board byte-identical (25 arms, 0 breaching).

The handoff ([/tmp/handoff-2026-08-01f-trust-health-view-49s.md](../handoff-2026-08-01f-trust-health-view-49s.md), Cowork) proposed moving the `packev` CTE into `rpc_trust_health_precompute`, citing "packev is 92% of it" and estimating ~49s → ~4s. **That change was NOT made — its rationale does not survive measurement.**

- **THE CORRECTION (durable — this is the reusable lesson): `packev` is 92% of the planner COST ESTIMATE (522,256 of 567,668) but only ~8.5% of RUNTIME (676ms of 7,999ms). Cost is not time.** Measured per-arm with `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, TIMING ON)`: the real hot spot was **`pinnacle_fmv_impossible_flags` at 3,911–4,639ms, ~50–58%** of the view; then `unmapped_resolution_backlog_max` 937ms, `offer_edition_gap_max_usd` 772ms, `packev` 676ms, `edition_integrity_flags` 415ms. Shipping the proposed change would have bought **~8% (8.0s → 7.3s), not 12×**, in exchange for making two arms up to 6h stale. Being fair to it: `packev` is the most VARIABLE leg (676ms quiet → 5,267ms contended, 8× swing, ~385k buffer *hits* from a SubPlan run 62,615×), so under contention it can dominate — the instinct wasn't baseless, only the evidence cited.
- **THE HANDOFF'S SAFETY ALARM WAS ALREADY CLOSED, and it flagged this as unverified.** "A monitoring system that times out looks healthy" does not apply: `v_rpc_trust_health`'s consumer is **`/api/sentinel`, NOT `/api/check-alerts`** — `get_pipeline_alerts()` does not read the view at all. [app/api/sentinel/route.ts:329-331](../../app/api/sentinel/route.ts) catches the error, classifies it via `isSaturationError()`, and pushes `status:"warn"` prefixed `INCONCLUSIVE (db saturated) — `, never `ok`. So a timeout makes the board **UNREAD, not falsely green** — a real visibility gap (service_role budget is 30s and the cold path exceeded it), but not the silent-healthy failure that justified urgency.
- **SHIPPED — `audit_20260801_pinnacle_sales_render_rollup_covering_index` (DB-only, no deploy, no behavioural change).** `v_pinnacle_fmv_sanity_flags`'s per-render 90d rollup planned as a Bitmap Heap Scan touching 3,831 blocks (3,661 heap) and returned `shared hit=6 read=3825` — **essentially zero cache hits, re-reading ~30MB from disk every call** on Micro. The existing `idx_pinnacle_sales_pulse_window` covers `(sold_at DESC) INCLUDE (sale_price_usd, …)` but **omits `render_id`**, so it could not go index-only. New `idx_pinnacle_sales_render_rollup` = `(sold_at DESC) INCLUDE (render_id, sale_price_usd)`, ~9MB, 13th index on the table. **Arm 3,911ms → 30.6–35ms; disk reads on that leg 3,742 → 240** (the cache-independent metric, so the COLD path improves by ~3,500 block reads); **whole view 7,999ms → 1,006ms**. Verified board identical: 25 arms, 0 breaching, `pinnacle_fmv_impossible_flags` still `0`.
- **VALIDATED THE PRECONDITION BEFORE BUILDING, rather than assuming** (the exact error I'd just caught in the handoff): a covering INCLUDE index only helps if index-only actually engages, and the documented counter-case is hot not-all-visible pages ([[large-index-build-on-hot-table]] / the FMV `fmv_current` note in CLAUDE.md). Checked `relallvisible = relpages = 6474` → **100% all-visible** → index-only will engage. It did (`Index Only Scan`, residual `Heap Fetches: 9095` are post-autovacuum rows and are cache hits, not disk reads).
- **NOT done, deliberately:** `packev` is now the largest remaining leg (611ms of ~1,006ms) — but at ~0.6s of a 1s query it is **no longer worth 6h of staleness on two arms**, so the handoff's change stays declined on its merits, not just its rationale. Also left alone: consolidating the now-overlapping `idx_pinnacle_sales_pulse_window` into the new index (would serve both consumers with one index, but touches a live surface for no measured win).
- **Revert:** `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.idx_pinnacle_sales_render_rollup;` (pure performance object — no arm value or behaviour depends on it) + `git revert <sha>` for the migration file.

Pins: null-user reject + no-op reject (both deltas zero after COALESCE) write NO ledger row; the happy path writes exactly one `adjust` row carrying the right delta/status/kind/reason/`admin:<who>` credit and returns the running totals; a status-only adjust (null point delta) lands as delta 0; reason/admin defaults.

- **DURABLE FINDING — pinned on purpose (and the reason I corrected the stripe test): the "extend" branch in BOTH `activate_pro_from_*` functions is effectively DEAD for normally-created rows.** Each guards extend on `v_existing pro_users%ROWTYPE / RECORD ... IF v_existing IS NOT NULL`. A composite `IS NOT NULL` is true only when EVERY column is non-null — but the real `pro_users` (9 cols) carries nullable `granted_by`/`grant_reason` that neither writer's INSERT populates, so a normally-created active sub makes the check FALSE and the function falls to the ELSE branch: stripe RESETS `expires_at` to the new `period_end` (a nearer period_end SHORTENS an "active" sub), payment RESETS to `now()+duration` (`extended=false`). The add-on-top/GREATEST extend path fires ONLY for a fully-populated row (e.g. an admin grant with granted_by AND grant_reason set). **Verified empirically on local `postgres:16` against the exact 9-column prod schema.** Both behaviors (normal→reset, full→extend) are now pinned so a future refactor that changes them is a conscious diff.
- **CORRECTION to the immediately-prior ledger entry's `activate_pro_from_stripe` pin (commit `21ec4427`, already pushed):** its SQL test used a simplified 5-column `pro_users` fixture (all columns non-null), which made the extend branch fire and its "extend never shortens (GREATEST)" assertion pass — but that does NOT reflect prod, where the real 9-col table's null `granted_by` sends a normal reactivation down the RESET path. ### 2026-08-01 (Cowork, interactive — full platform audit: health · pipelines · data-integrity · CISO · CMO/SEO · Candy/Panini · codebase) — shipped 8 prod DB migrations + 1 code batch closing a **P0 credential leak**, a **live anon cost-basis exposure**, **5 IDOR routes**, and **2,781 pack pages** that were hiding an EV we already held. Each item below has its own revert path; direct to `main`.

Nine parallel audits (pipelines/schedulers, data-integrity at population scale, CISO, CMO+SEO+onboarding, Candy/Panini go-live, codebase+backlog, FMV/pack-EV coverage, plus implementation agents). Findings that were healthy-by-design are recorded as such and NOT actioned.

**SECURITY (all verified with functional `has_table_privilege` / `SET ROLE anon` probes, never `information_schema`):**
- **P0 — live Dapper session + PII committed to a PUBLIC repo.** `scripts/fetch-allday-collection.mjs` hardcoded `cf_clearance` + `nfl_session.0/1/2` cookies and an RS256 `ID_TOKEN` whose payload carries a real email, legal name and Flow account id. `git check-ignore` → NOT ignored; tracked since `1c3e01a8f`. Converted to the env-var pattern its sibling scripts already use (`ALLDAY_COOKIES` / `ALLDAY_ID_TOKEN`) + a fail-fast guard. ⚠ **HEAD-only — the secrets remain in git HISTORY. Trevor must (a) invalidate that Dapper session and (b) run `git filter-repo --path scripts/fetch-allday-collection.mjs --invert-paths` + force-push.** Repo-wide sweep found no sibling file with the same pattern.
- **P1 — cost-basis / P&L was anon-readable** (`audit_20260801_revoke_anon_cost_basis_surface`). `moment_acquisitions`: **790,801 rows readable as `anon`**, 89,117 with a real `buy_price`, across 7,627 wallets (`buy_price`, `fmv_at_acquisition`, `seller_address`, `loan_principal`). This silently defeated the deliberate `proxy.ts` decision that "spend/P&L is private, owner-only". Revoked from `anon` **and** `authenticated` (front door is open since 07-20, and no RLS scopes rows to their owner) + dropped `public_read_moment_acquisitions`. Three invoker-chains were run down first (`v_topshot_edition_pull_provenance`, `pipeline_health`, `get_wallet_summary`/`get_wallet_moments_with_fmv`) — all reach the table via `supabaseAdmin`, so none was load-bearing. **Revert:** `GRANT SELECT ON public.moment_acquisitions TO anon, authenticated;` + recreate the policy.
- **P1 — 5 IDOR routes.** `profile/watchlist` (GET/POST/DELETE), `watchlist` (GET/POST/DELETE), `wallet/save` (POST), `wallet/profile` (GET), `profile/portfolio-history` (POST) all handed a request-supplied `ownerKey` to the SERVICE-ROLE client as the row selector — the request param WAS the authorization decision. New `lib/auth/owner-key-guard.ts`. **DURABLE: `owner_key` is POLYMORPHIC** — measured live, the same column holds an auth user UUID (all 1,217 `portfolio_snapshots` rows), a `profile_bio.username`, AND a 0x Flow address (what `localStorage.rpc_owner_key` actually holds after `collection/page.tsx` + `SignInWithDapper` overwrite it, i.e. what `WalletHydrator` sends). A guard resolving only usernames would have 403'd live traffic; this one bridges all three (user-id fast path → `saved_wallets` membership for address-shaped keys → `profile_bio` exact claim → 403), fails closed on every error, and re-checks the `ilike` result exactly so a `%` wildcard can't grant ownership. `wallet/profile`'s in-process cache is now keyed `${user.id}::${ownerKey}`. **`portfolio-history` GET stays PUBLIC by design** (it backs the public profile card). 32 guard tests + 26 repaired route tests + new 401/403 assertions on every guarded verb.
- **P3 — `watchlist_items` was anon-readable** (the CISO sweep had it as "latent, not breached" — it was breached; empty today, so nothing leaked). Revoked + policy dropped, along with 6 dead `qual=true` policies on `panini_*`/`candy_offers` (`audit_20260801_drop_dead_anon_read_policies_staged_data`) so a single future GRANT can't replay the 2026-07-19 incident.
- **P3 — 6 anon-EXECUTE volatile writers revoked** (`audit_20260801_revoke_anon_exec_volatile_writers`). `compute_price_snapshots()` had ZERO callers repo-wide and was an unauthenticated, argument-free aggregate over `sales` = a free DB-CPU exhaustion lever on an IOPS-bound instance. Revoked `FROM PUBLIC` as well as the roles (a role-only revoke leaves `has_function_privilege` true — trap #3).
- Post-state: `check_public_security_invariants()` 0 · `check_anon_write_surface()` 0 · `check_secdef_anon_exec_drift()` `[]`.

**DATA CORRECTNESS:**
- **2,781 pack pages un-hidden** (`audit_20260801_pack_ev_latest_admit_unknown_price_packs_v2`). `pack_ev_latest` filtered `pack_price > 0`, but the AllDay/Golazos writers do `node.price?.value ? Number(...) : 0` — **"price unknown" was written as "price zero"** and the view dropped the row, discarding a correctly-computed EV over a fully-populated drop pool (~40,600 pool rows; AllDay avg gross_ev **$678.72**, i.e. the most valuable AllDay packs in the index). Measured split of the 2,773 `pack_price=0` rows: AllDay 2,589 + Golazos 175 have `retail_price_usd IS NULL` (unknown) · Pinnacle 6 + TS 3 have `= 0` (genuine REWARD packs) · TS 32 have `> 0` (a writer defect). Now admits ONLY the unknown class and forces every price-RELATIVE field (`pack_ev`, `value_ratio`, `is_positive_ev`) to NULL, so no margin is ever asserted against a price we don't have; reward packs and the writer-bug class stay excluded. **AllDay 504→3,110 rows, Golazos 27→202; platform total 1,814→4,595.** Also relaxes the `>= 9999` DROP to the same treatment. **Revert:** restore the prior viewdef (in the migration comment).
- **489 Top Shot packs regained Typical Pull** (`..._backfill_topshot_historical_pack_ev_persist_typical_ev_v2`). `compute_pack_ev_per_edition_weighted` returns `typical_pull_ev` for every collection and both live writers persist it — this historical backfill omitted `typical_ev` from its INSERT column list. AllDay/Pinnacle were at 100%; **Top Shot was the only collection with the hole**, in the figure the public pack-EV block is required to LEAD with. Corrects CLAUDE.md's inverted framing.
- **Candy MLB Holders tab was rendering EMPTY on the LIVE public board** (`audit_20260801_candy_holder_board_scope_fmv_join`). `candy_holder_board` joined `fmv_current`, whose DISTINCT ON materializes over all ~944k `fmv_snapshots` rows before filtering to the 125 Candy editions → **82.3s**, blowing the request budget; the page's fail-soft `fetchView` returned `[]` so a headline tab read "Holders 0" while the view holds **373 collectors**, with nothing in Sentry. Scoped the FMV lookup to the Candy partition slice: **82.3s → 2.9s cold**, 373 rows. Same anti-pattern as the 2026-08-01 `get_set_detail` lesson.
- **91 Golazos moment pages had 404 team links** (`audit_20260801_get_team_detail_accept_unaccented_team_slug`). `slugifyTeam` strips diacritics (`atletico-de-madrid`) but the SQL slug expression does not (`atl-tico-de-madrid`), so `get_team_detail` returned NULL → 404 for Atlético de Madrid (51 editions), UD Almería, Cádiz, Málaga, Deportivo, Leganés, Hércules. Trevor's ruling: accept EITHER. The exact-match fast path is untouched (a bare `OR` would defeat `idx_editions_collection_team_slug` and reintroduce the cold-scan → pool-timeout class); the `extensions.unaccent` lane runs ONLY on a would-be 404. Guarded splice that ABORTS on anchor drift. Verified: both slugs resolve, genuine 404s still 404, TS control unaffected.

**MONITORING — closed the structural "running ≠ working" gap** (`audit_20260801_pipeline_failure_rate_alert_arm`). All 98 `pipeline_cadence_watchlist` rows key on `max_silent_minutes` ONLY, so the entire alerting model asks "did it RUN?" and never "did it WORK?". Measured today, three pipelines were failing hard while every sentinel read green: `topshot-active-listings-ingest` 51.6%, `topshot-pack-opens-history-backfill` 71.9%, `topshot-misattrib-drain` 100% (not even watchlisted). New `v_pipeline_failure_rates` (>25% fail over 2 rollup days, ≥5 runs — reads the indefinite `pipeline_runs_daily`, so it survives the ~73h `pipeline_runs` retention that hides these) + a guarded new UNION ALL arm in `get_pipeline_alerts()`. It fired immediately on `topshot-active-listings-ingest` (53.1%, `egress_blocked`) — previously invisible. **Revert:** re-`CREATE OR REPLACE` `get_pipeline_alerts` without the arm + `DROP VIEW v_pipeline_failure_rates`.
- **Re-armed an inert sentinel + dropped 3 lapsed suppressions** (`audit_20260801_pipeline_hygiene_and_rearm_ufc_sentinel`). `ufc_fmv_pct_stale_30d` sat at `breach_at 101` against a value of 96.1 — **a percentage metric with a >100 threshold is mathematically unbreachable**, i.e. green by construction; its own `catches` text says the threshold exists to catch deterioration, but it had been raised 90→101 as the value climbed 72.3→96.1. Set to 98 (still green — UFC's dead Flow market is HONEST — but able to fire). Deleted lapsed suppressions for `ingest-external-announcements`, `golazos_listings`, and `pinnacle-resolve-buyers` (the last verified LIVE AND HEALTHY: 181 runs/4d, 0 fail).

Duplicate `players` rows (up to 32 per slug — legitimate, the upstream key is `UNIQUE(external_id, collection_id)`) force `get_player_detail` to CHOOSE which row's `team` the public player page shows. The prior ladder led with `team_edition_count DESC` = the team the player has the most moments for. That is right for a RETIRED player (Paul Pierce ⇒ Celtics, not his final Nets season) and wrong for a TRADED one — it pins them to a former team forever. Measured live: **295 of 949 duplicate Top Shot slugs showed a stale team, 201 of them for players still actively playing** (Karl-Anthony Towns ⇒ Timberwolves, Kelsey Plum ⇒ Aces, James Harden ⇒ Clippers, Angel Reese ⇒ Sky). Added a leading current-team preference: pick the row whose `team` matches the team on the player's most recent moment, but ONLY while they are still active; otherwise fall through to the old ladder unchanged. **116 of 1,326 slugs change, all in the trade direction**; retired players are untouched. **Revert:** the prior definition is the one in `supabase/migrations/20260729000100_audit_20260729_snapshot_read_rpc_ddl_batch2.sql` — re-apply that `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION`, then `git revert <sha>` + repoint the PINS entry back; drop the index with `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS public.idx_editions_collection_game_date;`
- **⚠ CORRECTS THE HANDOFF on two points, both load-bearing.** (1) It said the tie-break was **arbitrary** and that SGA/Mitchell/Brunson render Clippers/Jazz/Mavericks. Not so as of `cd153d2e` (same-day, "canonical team slugs"): the ladder was already deterministic and all three named players were **already correct** before I touched anything — I verified each. The residual defect is narrower and different in kind: *stale-for-traded-players*, not *random*. (2) It proposed ordering by "the row whose most-recent associated edition is newest". That rule is **unimplementable as written** — `editions.first_minted_at` is **0 of 19,583 populated** on Top Shot, a dead column, so ordering by it is arbitrary (this is also why the player page's `first_minted_at`/`last_minted_at` render null — separate, untouched). `game_date` (92% populated) is the correct recency signal and is semantically right: the team on a moment is the team the player was on at that game.
- **DURABLE — "latest moment wins" is the WRONG rule on its own; it needs an activity gate.** Applied unconditionally it shows a retired player's final-season team (Pierce ⇒ Nets, Mutombo ⇒ his last stop) instead of the one they are known for — a regression a collectibles audience notices immediately. The gate is a **data-relative** horizon (`collection max(game_date) − 18 months`), deliberately not a hardcoded date, so it can never go stale AND stays correct for a collection whose data has stopped advancing (a frozen collection still resolves "team as of end of data" rather than marking everyone inactive). Both directions are now pinned by tests, so a future "simplification" to plain latest-wins reds CI.
- **Perf: the fix is NET FASTER than what it replaced.** The new `horizon` arm needed `max(game_date)` per collection, which was a full scan of every edition in the collection on EVERY player page load — 41.8 ms of a 45 ms total. Added partial index `idx_editions_collection_game_date (collection_id, game_date DESC) WHERE game_date IS NOT NULL`; whole function now **19.5 ms** warm incl. the FMV rollup. Built non-CONCURRENTLY under `lock_timeout=5s` — `editions` is 26,991 rows / 38 MB, sub-second. The slug expression in the WHERE clause is byte-identical, so `idx_players_collection_name_slug` still matches (changing it would drop the page to a full collection scan — the documented pool-acquire-timeout class, Sentry NEXTJS-20).
- **Pin maintained, not just repointed** (the handoff's own warning). `supabase/tests/get_player_detail.sql` verbatim block updated, `PINS` repointed to the new migration, drift guard **85/85 green**; the fixture gained the `game_date` column it now requires (without it the test errors, not fails) and **two new assertions** covering both new branches — traded-active flips to the new team, retired stays on the iconic team. Live definition is byte-identical to the committed migration. Verified all 5 published collections still resolve (incl. Pinnacle's separate `character_name` branch and UFC's honest null team). `tsc` clean (the only errors are stale `.next/` artifacts for deleted routes; `.next` is gitignored so CI's fresh checkout is unaffected). ⚠ This box has no Postgres/Docker, so the SQL test's first real run is CI's `db-tests`; I de-risked it by validating the exact ORDER BY expression against live Postgres with a table-free VALUES fixture — both new cases PASS.

### 2026-08-01 (Claude Code, interactive — 08-01 handoff items 5 / 8 / 9 + 19) — cut ~23 min of wasted CI per blocked run, instrumented two blind crons, retuned an inert 72×/day schedule, and DISPROVED handoff item 19.

- **SHIPPED (item 5) — `topshot-active-listings-ingest` now proves an egress block in ~1 min instead of ~24.** Confirmed live from `pipeline_runs_daily`: **34 runs / 18 fail = 52.9%**, `last_error = egress_blocked`, `duration_ms_p95 = 1,453,742` (**24.2 min**). Cause: the `allBlocked` verdict (`targets_processed === 0 && targets_skipped > 0`) was only evaluated AFTER the whole ~1,080-target sweep, and every blocked target burns `atlasBoundary`'s 4 retry attempts of backoff. Added an in-loop short-circuit that breaks once `EGRESS_PROBE_N` (default 5, env-overridable) consecutive failures have occurred with ZERO successes — the SAME predicate, just evaluated early, so the downstream verdict/`deactivate` semantics are untouched. N > 1 by design so one edition failing on its own merits can never produce a false "blocked". **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **⚠ DELIBERATELY DID NOT take the handoff's `exit 0` suggestion, and the reason matters.** It argued exiting 0 on a known-upstream block "keeps the failure-rate metric meaningful". The exit code does **not** feed that metric — `v_pipeline_failure_rates` reads `pipeline_runs`, which is written by `postRoute({ok:false, error:'egress_blocked'})` independently of how the process exits. So `exit 0` would have changed nothing about the metric while turning a genuine ingest outage GREEN in the GitHub Actions UI. Kept `exit 1`; the entire cost win comes from the 24 min, not the exit code.
- **SHIPPED (item 8b) — `purge-stale-listings` is no longer a blind daily DELETE.** It ran at 04:00 UTC every day with **no `log_pipeline_run` at all**, so nobody could see how many rows it removed or whether it had silently been deleting nothing (or everything) for months. Added logging on the success AND both failure legs. **Predicate deliberately UNCHANGED** per the handoff — measure first. Ran the SELECT form first (rowcount-before-destructive discipline): 306 rows total, **1** older than 48h, table actively written (max `cached_at` same day) — a small healthy job, not a runaway. **DURABLE:** it derives its count from `.delete().select("id")`, whose RETURNING representation PostgREST **caps at 1000** (the DELETE itself is unbounded — the rows do go, only the *number* saturates); the log now carries a `count_capped` flag so a future reader can't mistake a saturated 1000 for the truth.
- **SHIPPED (item 8a) — `compute-laliga-pack-ev` got a synchronous invocation marker, and its header comment was CORRECTED as materially false.** It has a daily Vercel cron and **zero `pipeline_runs` rows, ever**. It *does* call `log_pipeline_run` — but the entire body, logging included, runs inside `after()` while the route returns 200 immediately, i.e. the documented Vercel-`after()` unreliability class that hid the May `fmv-recalc` stall. That made "never invoked" (cron/auth broken) indistinguishable from "invoked, `after()` dropped". Added a marker logged BEFORE `after()` is scheduled (`extra.phase='invoked'`, `ok:true` so it cannot inflate the new failure-rate arm); next daily tick decides it — marker-only ⇒ `after()` is being dropped, no marker ⇒ the route is never reached. **⚠ The route's own header said "pack_drop_pool currently has zero Golazos rows — this route is a no-op". That is NO LONGER TRUE and the handoff repeated it: the Golazos pool now holds 1,957 rows, ALL `drop_weight > 0`.** So this is a route with real work that has been silently invisible — a genuine gap, not an expected quiet. Comment rewritten; **do not delete this schedule** (the handoff floated it as an option — the data says otherwise).
- **SHIPPED (item 9) — UFC backfill `1,21,41 * * * *` (72×/day) → `0 6 * * *` (daily).** Verified inert first: **234 runs, 0 rows_found, 0 rows_written** over 4 days (UFC market dead since the 2026-05-13 Aptos migration). Retuned rather than deleted so a UFC reactivation is still noticed within a day. `vercel.json` still 33 crons (schedule-only change; JSON re-validated). **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **QUEUED, not shipped (item 9, `evm-transfers-ingest`):** confirmed inert (**77 runs, 0 rows / 4 days**) but it is NOT in `vercel.json`, so its scheduler is cron-job.org or pg_cron — unreachable from here. Belongs to the operator-only console audit (handoff item 12). `sync-sales-seller-recovery-dune` left strictly alone (parked by decision; `sales_ingest_state.cursor_end` untouched).
- **❌ DISPROVED (item 19) — "441 wallet-box views → 0 pastes" is NOT a conversion signal, and the redesign it implies would be chasing a bot number.** Two independent reasons. (1) **Instrumentation**: the forked wallet inputs on `/insights` and `/<collection>/overview` emitted **no `wallet_paste` at all** until commit `f7b665ea` (**2026-07-26**, not the 07-25 the handoff assumed) consolidated them — so pre-07-26 "0 pastes" measured blindness, not behaviour. (2) **The honest denominator**: since 07-26 there have been 235 view events but only **7 with a referrer**; 183 sessions, only **2 with a referrer**; and **175 of 183 sessions (96%) fired exactly ONE event**. Plausibly-human sessions (≥2 events) number **8**, of which **1** had a referrer. So the real denominator is ~8, not 441. There IS now exactly one `wallet_paste` on `insights_account_value` (today 12:59 PDT) — but its wallet is `0xbd94cade097e50ac`, **Trevor's own**, in a 36-event session, i.e. a self-test. **Recommendation: do NOT redesign the wallet box on this evidence.** It is instrumented correctly and the pipe is proven end-to-end; the input is traffic, which is roadmap Phase 0. Revisit only after ≥500 referrer-bearing multi-event sessions have seen it — the roadmap's own falsification bar.

### 2026-08-01 (Claude Code, interactive — 08-01 handoff item 4, + findings on 10 and 13) — moved the two tick-dropping GHA schedules to Vercel crons and closed the blind spot that hid the loss.

- **SHIPPED (item 4) — `topshot-listing-cache` + `allow-list-reconcile` schedules moved GitHub Actions → Vercel cron, same minutes.** Confirmed the loss **from the GHA run history itself**, not the DB — important, because the route is fire-and-forget (`after()`) and a DB-only count could have been an `after()` artifact rather than a scheduler one (the exact trap I hit on `compute-laliga-pack-ev` an hour earlier). GHA fired **10–13 runs/day against the 72/day** `15,35,55` implies, every day 07-27→08-01 (~83% loss); `allow-list-reconcile` ~9 of 24 (~60%). Control: Vercel crons on this same project deliver ~100% over the identical window (`candy-listings-indexer` 8/8, `candy-offers-indexer` 4/4, `allday-price-recover` 80/72). **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` restores both `schedule:` blocks and drops the two `vercel.json` entries in one commit.
- **The migration required a route change, which is the part a naive move would have silently broken.** Both routes accepted **only** `INGEST_SECRET_TOKEN`, but **Vercel Cron can only ever send `Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET`** — so simply adding the `vercel.json` entries would have produced a 401 every tick and a *worse* outage that still looked scheduled. Both now accept either, copying the already-proven shape in `app/api/candy-listings-indexer` (whose own comment documents this exact constraint). Minutes kept byte-identical (15,35,55 and :14) so the deliberate anti-pile-up stagger in `docs/operations/cron-schedule.md` is untouched — only the scheduler swapped. `rpc-pipeline.yml` step #5 still calls the listing-cache route and was left alone, so the documented temporal backstop survives; both workflows keep `workflow_dispatch` for manual runs.
- **DURABLE — a `pipeline_cadence_watchlist` keyed on SILENCE cannot see PARTIAL tick loss, and that is why an 83% outage sat invisible for days.** `topshot-listing-cache` **was** watchlisted the whole time (`max_silent_minutes` 360) — but at ~17% delivery it still fired roughly every 2h, so it never approached the 6h threshold. Silence-based cadence alerting only catches total stoppage. The new `v_pipeline_failure_rates` arm (shipped earlier today) has the same blind spot: these runs SUCCEEDED, they just mostly didn't happen. Detecting this class needs an *expected-vs-actual tick count*, which nothing currently computes — **queued, not built** (it wants a schedule-aware source of truth per pipeline, and the cron-job.org third of the surface isn't enumerable from the repo, i.e. it depends on operator item 12).
- **SHIPPED — `allow-list-reconcile` added to `pipeline_cadence_watchlist`** (`audit_20260801_watchlist_allow_list_reconcile`; 240m, `info`). It had **no row at all**, so its ~60% loss was invisible even in principle. 240m = 4 missed hourly ticks, deliberately loose while the new schedule beds in; `info` because it is a prewarm reconcile, not a data pipeline. **Revert:** `DELETE FROM public.pipeline_cadence_watchlist WHERE pipeline='allow-list-reconcile';`
- **⚠ FOLLOW-UP (next session, ~10 min): confirm the two Vercel crons actually authenticate.** This is the one thing I could not verify from here — `CRON_SECRET` must be set in Vercel prod for the new entries to pass the widened check. It is near-certainly set (`proxy.ts` step 1 already honours it and other Vercel crons run), but **verify empirically** rather than assume: after the next tick, `SELECT * FROM pipeline_runs_daily WHERE pipeline IN ('topshot-listing-cache','allow-list-reconcile') AND day >= CURRENT_DATE;` should show ~72/day and ~24/day. If runs go to ZERO, `CRON_SECRET` is unset/mismatched — revert the commit (restoring the GHA schedules) rather than leaving both schedulers off.
- **❌ ITEM 10 — MEASURED, AND THE HEADLINE DOES NOT SURVIVE CONTACT WITH THE DOLLARS. Recommendation: do NOT move the FMV clamp, and do NOT treat this as a P0.** Reproduced the cohort (4,412 Top Shot editions with ≥4 sales/30d; **432 over 2× their own median = 9.8%**, close to the handoff's 409/9.2%). But the distribution is the whole story: **median sale price in the cohort is $0.30 and the median overstatement is $0.55.** Only **4 of 432** editions have an FMV ≥ $5; **ZERO** are ≥ $20; **ZERO** are ≥ $100. Summed across all 432, the total overstatement is **$339**. By confidence: LOW 327 editions totalling **$346 of FMV** (~$1.06 each), MEDIUM 70 (~$1.26 each), HIGH 14 (~$0.86 each). So this is a **ratio artifact on penny moments**, not a valuation failure — a common moment whose median sale is $0.30 and whose FMV reads $1.00 is "3.3× overstated" and wrong by seventy cents. Moving the existing `fmv_clamp_disconnected_ask_topshot` threshold from 3× to 2× would touch 432 editions (183 already sit above 3×) to recover ~$339, while adding real risk of suppressing genuinely-rising editions mid-run-up — a strictly bad trade. **If this is ever revisited, gate on ABSOLUTE gap (e.g. > $25), not ratio; ratio-only screens on sub-dollar denominators will keep manufacturing this false alarm.** No FMV logic touched, per the standing hands-off rule.
- **❌ ITEM 13 — correctly NOT shipped; the handoff's own trigger is not met.** Re-queried `panini_sale_feed_status` as instructed: `feed_ok=false`, last supplied **2026-07-28 = 4 days**, `pct_serials_priced` 7.72%. The handoff's stated gate was **>7 days**. More importantly the load-bearing claim still holds — I verified Panini FMV is **fresh (68 minutes old, 1,277 snapshot rows in 24h)**, and the stale field (`serials_with_recorded_price`) is fetched into the client Row type but is **not one of the rendered columns**, so no user-visible number on the now-public board is stale. Adding a second banner today would only dilute the mandatory listing-gated coverage warning beside it. **Re-check at >7 days (i.e. from 2026-08-04) or immediately if `panini_fmv_snapshots` stops advancing.**
